# Lviv Stauropegion Lenten Triodion (Lviv, 1906) <a id="lviv-stauropegion-lenten-triodion-lviv-1906"></a>

[Title Page: ornate architectural border with floral vignettes and acanthus scrollwork]

THE LENTEN TRIODION
or
THE THREE-ODE CANON
in Greek:
TRIODION.

Unto the glory of the Holy, Consubstantial, Life-Creating, and Undivided Trinity,
of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit,

this Book was printed

through the diligence and at the expense of
THE STAUROPEGION INSTITUTE
at the Church of the Dormition of the Most Holy Mother of God.[^1]

[Seal of the Institute: circular impression bearing the inscription "STAUROPEGION INSTITUTE" surrounding an escutcheon with the Patriarchal cross and monogram of Christ]
[Ex-libris stamp: "REV. IHOR G. SHPYTKOVSKY / 501 MUNROE AVE. / WINNIPEG 15, MAN."]
[Library oval stamp: "Lviv Theological Academy / Library"]

IN LVIV
At the Typography of the same Stauropegion Institute,
in the year 1906.

[Handwritten dedication in Ukrainian cursive at the bottom margin:][^2]
"For Most Reverend Kyr I. Prasko — gratefully, Fr. Ihor. Melbourne, 29.VII.1968."

[Library stamp at upper right: "THEOLOGICAL ACADEMY / LIBRARY / 502049"]
[Plate: Architectural engraving of the ensemble of the Dormition Church in Lviv, showing the Korniakt bell tower, the Chapel of the Three Hierarchs, and the Church of the Dormition of the Most Holy Mother of God, enclosed within a geometric border][^3]

[Calligraphic vyaz inscription beneath the engraving:]
THE WORK OF THE KING AND HIS SON By the grace of the All-Merciful God, this soul-profiting Book was published,

When the Universal Pontiff was
POPE PIUS X,

When the reigning Austrian Emperor was
FRANZ JOSEPH I.

No. 1946
On the 26th day of the month of June,
in the year 1906.[^4]

BY THE BLESSING
Of His Excellency, the Most Reverend
Kyr
ANDREY
COUNT OF SZEPTYCE SZEPTYCKY,
Metropolitan of Halych, Archbishop of Lviv, Bishop of Kamianets-Podilskyi, Privy Councillor to His Imperial and Royal Apostolic Majesty, Member of the House of Lords of the Austrian Imperial Council, Vice-Marshal of the Diet of the Kingdom of Galicia and Lodomeria with the Grand Duchy of Cracow, Doctor of Sacred Theology, Law, and Philosophy, etc., etc.

In the days
Of His Grace, the God-beloved
Kyr
KONSTANTYN CHEKHOVYCH,
Bishop of Peremyshl, Sambir, and Sanok, Domestic Prelate and Assistant to the Pontifical Throne of His Holiness the Pope, Roman Count, Knight of the Grand Cross of the Holy Sepulchre of the Lord in Jerusalem, and of the Order of the Iron Crown, Member of the Diet of the Kingdom of Galicia and Lodomeria with the Grand Duchy of Cracow, etc., etc.

and
Of His Grace, the God-beloved
Kyr
HRYHORII KHOMYSHYN,
Bishop of Stanyslaviv, Member of the Diet of Galicia and Lodomeria with the Grand Duchy of Cracow, Doctor of Sacred Theology, etc., etc.

The printing was begun
Under the Senior Warden of the Stauropegion Institute, Mykola Herasymovych, and was completed under the Senior Warden Roman Ilnytsky, and with him Mykola Snizhlak and Venedykt Ilsky.[^5]
The Priest Volodymyr Hurhula labored over the edition.
Manager of the Typography of the Stauropegion Institute, Mykhailo Reftsio.

[Headpiece: decorative vignette depicting the Holy Cross in radiant beams, flanked by grapevine foliage]

PRAYER
to Our Lord Jesus Christ.[^6]

O God, King of ages, and Creator of all creation: Thou art our only hope; Thou art the ever-existing, unsearchable God in love for mankind, eternal. Thou art the Giver of all life, Who upholdest our temporary and mortal life, unto daily and nightly instruction, and Thou dost grant us all things for the reception of good things, unto the salvation of our souls and bodies. Since Thou art the God Who lovest mankind, Who grantest rest unto every toil-loving ascetic labor, receive the present strivings toward the world to come as an odor of spiritual fragrance, according to the saying: "The heavens are Thine, and the earth is Thine; and Thine own of Thine own we offer unto Thee alone upon this Tablet." Do Thou therefore, as the Lover of mankind, receive the unworthy lifting up of our hands; grant unto us the revelation of Thy incomprehensible mysteries through Thy sovereign, incomprehensible Wisdom, which was sent from Thee unto us for our salvation, that we may know Thee, the God and Father of us all, and may delight in Thine ineffable mysteries. Grant unto us in Thy Wisdom, which is the Son and Word of God, through which Word the heavens were established, to abide patiently, and in Her to behold Thee, our God and Father, to be well-pleasing unto Thee through Her, guarding ourselves against the spiritual Pharaoh, and praying earnestly concerning this unto Thee, our God on high: so that in the water of tears we may drown the hypocrisy of the Pharisee, and, shamelessly fleeing vainglory, may escape it, and may overcome our visible and invisible enemies, and may proclaim Thy glory before men; that we may be accounted worthy to be crowned by Thee, the God Who lovest mankind, with the crown of victory, and in our eternal Fatherland and in Thy Kingdom to glorify Thee, such a great Benefactor, together with Thine Only-begotten Son, our Savior, Who was eternally begotten of Thee, and with Thy Holy, Good, and Life-Creating Spirit, unto endless ages of ages. Amen.

---

# PART I: PRE-LENTEN PERIOD (SUNDAYS OF PUBLICAN & PHARISEE, PRODIGAL SON, MEATFARE, AND CHEESEFARE)

[Headpiece: ornate rectangular woodcut depicting Christ the Savior amidst foliate scrollwork]

*The Lenten Triodion*[^7]

*That is, the Three-Ode Canon, containing the proper liturgical sequence, with God the Holy One.*

*The Sunday on which is read the Holy and Sacred Gospel of the parable of the Publican and the Pharisee.*

*On Saturday evening, after the Introductory Psalm, we chant: "Blessed is the man," the entire first Kathisma.*

*At "Lord, I have cried,"*[^8] *we set 10 stichera: and we chant 3 Resurrectional stichera of the Octoechos, and 4 Anatolian:*[^9] *and 2 idiomelon stichera of the Triodion, repeating the first.*

Let us not pray after the manner of the Pharisee, brethren; for he that exalts himself shall be humbled. Let us humble ourselves before God, calling out with fasting as the Publican: Cleanse us sinners, O God!

The Pharisee, overcome by vainglory, and the Publican, bowed down by repentance, drew near unto Thee, the only Master. But the one, having boasted, was deprived of good things; while the other, uttering nothing, was accounted worthy of gifts. In his sighing confirm me, O Christ God, as Thou art the Lover of mankind.

*Glory, Tone 8:*

O Almighty Lord, I know how great is the power of tears: for they brought up Hezekiah from the gates of death, and delivered the sinful woman from the transgressions of many years, and justified the Publican above the Pharisee; and I pray Thee: Numbering me with them, have mercy on me.

*Now and ever, the first Theotokion of the Tone of the week.*

*At the Litiya, the sticheron of the Saint of the monastery, according to custom.*

*Glory, Tone 3:*

Having understood the difference between the Publican and the Pharisee, O my soul, abhor the haughty voice of the one, and emulate the prayer of deep compunction of the other, and cry aloud: O God, cleanse me a sinner, and have mercy on me!

*Now and ever, the Resurrectional Theotokion, in the same Tone.*

*At the Aposticha, the Resurrectional stichera of the Octoechos in alphabetical order.*

*Glory, Tone 5:*

With mine eyes weighed down by mine iniquities, I cannot gaze and behold the height of heaven; but receive me, O Savior, as the repenting Publican, and have mercy on me!

*Now and ever, Theotokion, in the same Tone: "Thou art the temple and the gate:"*

*Troparion: "Rejoice, O Virgin Theotokos," is said thrice. And there takes place the blessing of loaves, and the distribution: and the great reading from the Epistles of the Apostles.*

*The sequence of the Saint who falls on this Sunday is chanted on Friday at Compline, or behold when the ecclesiarch shall decide; unless there happen to be a great Saint, or the Saint of the church: for the temple...*

*...and not of a great Saint, follows more the great Saint, on whatever church feast is his, for which a vigil must take place, and in no way is it to be left out in his commemoration, nor is it transferred to another day. But we chant the service of the church, as also to the Meeting of the Lord, on all days on which the Meeting of the Lord also occurs.*

*At Matins, after the Six Psalms, "God is the Lord," in the Tone of the Octoechos. And we say the Resurrectional Troparion twice, the Theotokion once, and the customary Kathisma readings. Sessional Hymns of the Octoechos. After the Evlogitaria, the Troparia: "The angelic council:" the Hypakoe, the Graduals, and the Prokimenon of the Tone: "Let every breath:" the Resurrectional Gospel of the week. "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ:" Psalm 50.*

*Glory, Tone 8:*[^10]

Open unto me the doors of repentance, O Giver of life; for my spirit rises early toward Thy holy temple, bearing the temple of my body all defiled: but as Thou art compassionate, cleanse me by Thy loving-kindness.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*

Guide me into the paths of salvation, O Theotokos; for with shameful sins have I stained my soul, and in laziness have I squandered all my life: but by thine intercessions deliver me from all uncleanness.

*Then, Tone 6:*

*Have mercy on me, O God, according to Thy great mercy; and according to the multitude of Thy tender mercies blot out my transgression.*

Pondering the multitude of the dread deeds I have committed, wretched that I am, I tremble at the fearful day of judgment: but trusting in the mercy of Thy loving-kindness, like David I cry unto Thee: Have mercy on me, O God, according to Thy great mercy!

*The Resurrectional Canon of the Octoechos, with the Heirmos to 4; and the Cross-Resurrectional to 2; and the Theotokos to 2; and in the Triodion to 6.*

*A composition of George. Whose acrostic in the Theotokia is: OF GEORGE.*[^11]

*Ode 1, Tone 6. Heirmos: "Traversing the deep on foot as on dry land, Israel:"*

Christ, Who by parables leads all unto the correction of life, lifts up the Publican from humility, showing the Pharisee humbled by pride.

Beholding high-exalting honor from humility, and a dire fall from haughtiness, emulate the good deeds of the Publican, and abhor the malice of the Pharisee.

Every good is emptied out through haughtiness, but every evil is destroyed through humility: let us believers embrace this, openly abhorring the image of the vainglorious.

Wishing His disciples to be humble-minded, the King of all, instructing them, taught them to emulate the sighing and humility of the Publican.

*Glory:*

Like the Publican I groan, and with unceasing laments, O Lord, I now draw near to Thy loving-kindness: show pity also on me, who now spend my life in humility.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*

*[Margin: G]* Understanding, counsel, expectation, body, soul, and spirit, O Sovereign Lady, I commit unto thee: from cruel enemies and tribulations, and from future condemnation deliver me, and save me.

*Katavasia: "I shall open my mouth:"*

*Ode 3. Heirmos: "There is none holy like unto Thee:"*

From the dunghill of passions the humble one is exalted, but from the height of virtues every haughty one falls grievously: let us flee the image of his malice.

Vainglory squanders the wealth of righteousness, but humility scatters the multitude of passions: show us, O Savior, who imitate this, to be partakers with the Publican.

Like the Publican let us also, smiting our breasts, cry out with compunction: Cleanse us sinners, O God, that we may receive the forgiveness of our sins!

Let us come to zeal, O believers, cultivating meekness, dwelling together with humility in the groaning of the heart, in weeping and in prayer, that we may obtain forgiveness from God.

*Glory:*

Let us cast away, O believers, boastful pride, cruel haughtiness, and abominable arrogance, and the most wicked, unbecoming ferocity of the Pharisee toward God.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*

*[Margin: E]* Fleeing unto thee, the only refuge, I hope that I may not fall away from good expectation: but that I may obtain thy help, O Pure One, delivered from every harm of evil things.

*Sessional Hymns, Tone 4. Model: "Speedily anticipate:"*

Humility exalted the Publican held fast by evils, who groaned and cried unto the Creator: "Cleanse me!" But haughtiness brought down from righteousness the wretched Pharisee who spoke with boasting. Therefore let us emulate the good, departing from evil.

*Glory:*

Humility of old exalted the Publican, who cried out with weeping: "Cleanse me!" and was justified. Let us all imitate him, who have fallen into the depth of evils, and let us cry to the Savior from the depth of the heart: We have sinned, cleanse us, O only Lover of mankind!

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*

Speedily accept our supplications, O Sovereign Lady, and bear them unto Thy Son and God, O all-immaculate Lady: loosen the tribulations of those who run unto thee, shatter the snares, and cast down the audacity of those who impiously arm themselves against thy servants, O all-pure one.

*Ode 4. Heirmos: "Christ is my power:"*

The Word, Who humbled Himself even unto the form of a servant, showed an excellent way of exaltation, even humility: imitating which, everyone who humbles himself is exalted.

The righteous man was exalted, and the Pharisee fell down; but weighed down by a multitude of evils, the Publican humbled himself, yet he was exalted, unexpectedly justified.

Folly proved to be an intercessor of poverty from the wealth of virtues; but humility immediately proved to be an abundance of righteousness from extreme poverty: which let us acquire.

Thou didst foretell, O Master, that Thou wouldst oppose the proud in every way, and giving Thy grace unto the humble, O Savior: send down Thy grace upon us who are now humbled.

*Glory:*

The Savior and Master, Who ever leads us up unto divine exaltation, showed forth humility that works on high: for with His own hands He washed the feet of His disciples.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*

*[Margin: O]* As thou didst bring forth the Unapproachable Light, O Virgin, disperse the darkness of my soul with the illuminating radiance, and guide my life into the paths of salvation.

*Ode 5. Heirmos: "With Thy divine light, O Good One:"*

Let us strive to emulate the virtues of the Pharisee, and to emulate the humility of the Publican, hating in both the senseless conceit and the ruin of their falls.

The vain course of righteousness was exposed when the Pharisee joined conceit unto it; but straightway the Publican acquired as a companion humility, that virtue which works on high.

The Pharisee thought to run as a charioteer in the virtues; but running on foot, the Publican outran the Lybian chariot, having yoked humility unto compassion.

Having all understood with our minds the parable of the Publican, come, let us emulate his tears, offering a contrite spirit unto God, seeking the remission of our sins.

*Glory:*

Let us who are prudent cast far away the boastful, wicked, haughty, and arrogant disposition of the Pharisee, cruel and high-vaunting, lest we be stripped of divine grace.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*

*[Margin: R]* Send down upon all of us who run unto thee the rod of power, O Mother of God, granting us to rule in the midst of all enemies, and delivering us from every harm.

*Ode 6. Heirmos: "The sea of life:"*

Together the Publican and the Pharisee ran the course of life; but the one, held fast by conceit, sank shamefully, while the other was saved by humility.

As we sail the perilous course of life, let us zealously emulate the mind of the Publican; but let us flee the haughtiness of the abominable Pharisee, and we shall live.

Let us emulate the ways of Jesus the Savior and His humility, desiring to obtain the unceasing dwelling of joy, taking up our abode in the land of the living.

Thou hast shown unto Thy disciples, O Master, humility that works on high: girded with a towel about Thy loins, Thou didst wash their feet, commanding them to imitate this example.

*Glory:*

The Pharisee traversed life in virtues, and the Publican in transgressions; but the one, through foolish pride, fell away from humility, while the other was exalted, having shown himself humble-minded.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*

*[Margin: G]* Created naked in simplicity and artless life, the enemy deceived me through the deceit of transgression and the coarseness of the flesh; but now through thine intercession, O Maiden, I am saved.

*Kontakion, Tone 4. Model: "Thou hast appeared today:"*

Let us flee the haughty speaking of the Pharisee, and let us learn the height of the humble words of the Publican, crying out with repentance: O Savior of the world, cleanse Thy servants!

*Second Kontakion, Tone 3. Model: "The Virgin today:"*

Let us bring Publican-like groanings unto the Lord, and let us sinners draw near unto Him as to a Master: for He wills the salvation of all men, and grants forgiveness unto all that repent, for for our sake He was incarnate, being God co-beginningless with the Father.

*Ikos:*

Let us all humble ourselves, brethren, with groanings and with weeping let us strike our conscience, that at that eternal judgment we may appear there as faithful, innocent, having obtained forgiveness: for there truly is forgiveness, which let us now beseech that we may behold; there pain, sorrow, and sighing from the depth have fled away, in marvelous Eden, whereof Christ is the Creator, being God co-beginningless with the Father.

*Short Preface of the Synaxaria, that is, the collections of Xanthopoulos, for the Triodion Synaxaria.*[^12]

*The collections of Nikephoros Kallistos Xanthopoulos for the notable feasts of the Triodion, each giving the historical reason how and when it came to be from the beginning, and for what reason they are held thus now, and how they were instituted by the holy and God-bearing Fathers with certain known particular details, beginning from the Publican and the Pharisee and ending even unto All Saints.*

*The monthly Menaion Synaxarion should be read first at the Seventh Ode according to custom, and after that the present one.*

*These verses are spoken after the readings. Verses on the Triodion:*

*Unto the Creator of things above and things below:*
*Accept the Thrice-Holy hymn from the Angels,*
*And the Three-Ode Canon also from men.*

*On the Publican and the Pharisee:*
*Whoso lives like the Pharisee is far from the Church:*
*For Christ is within, received by humility.*

On the present day, with God, we also begin the Triodion: which indeed many of our holy and God-bearing beauty-making Fathers, well and as was fitting, being moved by the Holy Spirit, composed as hymnody. The first of all who conceived this—I mean the Three Odes, after the pattern of the Persons of the Holy and Life-Originating Trinity—was the great hymnodist Cosmas,[^13] who conceived these odes for the great and holy Passion of the Lord God and our Savior Jesus Christ, sitting by the day's acrostics, briefly completing them. From him also the other Fathers, especially Theodore and Joseph the Studites, zealous for his emulation, composed also for the remaining weeks of the Holy and Great Forty Days, and first delivered them to their holy monastery, especially having instituted and left the hymns; and the other books, gathered and acquired here and there from the Fathers. And since Sunday concludes the first of the days as resurrectional, being the first, and the eighth, and the final, making for the second day—that is, Monday—they appointed the first Ode. Likewise for the third day—that is, Tuesday—the second Ode. For the fourth day—that is, Wednesday—the third. For the fifth, the fourth Ode, which is Thursday. And for the sixth day—that is, Friday—the fifth Ode. For the sixth, Saturday, as also for the seventh, and the other two, the eighth and the ninth, which all days commonly possess as most true. Thus indeed the divine Cosmas placed the Four-Ode Canon for Great Saturday, and so they did: even if later the most wise Emperor Leo, having commanded the monk Mark, who was revealed as a bishop, to complete the canons, accomplished it. By need it is called the Triodion, although it does not always contain three odes: for it presents completely perfected rules, but received its title from the greater part; or because of Great Week, as was said before. It was the intention of our holy Fathers, by the whole book of the Triodion, briefly to commemorate all the divine benefactions toward us from the beginning, and to set forth for the remembrance of all: how we were created by Him, and were cast out from the delight of Paradise, having transgressed the commandment given to us for our knowledge, and were rejected through the envy of the prime-evil serpent and enemy...

...cast down for his pride. And how we remained rejected from good things and led by the devil. And how the Son and Word of God, having suffered through His bowels of compassion, bowed down the heavens and came down, and dwelt in the Virgin, and for our sake became man, and by His life after that showed forth the ascent unto heaven, that is to say, with humility leading the way, and by fasting, and by the rejection of evil things, and by His other deeds. And how He suffered and arose, and ascended again into heaven, and sent down the Holy Spirit upon His holy disciples and Apostles: and how the Son of God and perfect God was proclaimed concerning all these things. And what again the divine Elias worked together by the grace of the All-Holy Spirit, so that at the end of all the saints, they gathered them together by preaching, filling the world on high: which was also the intention from the beginning of Him Who created us. But in these thoughts of the Triodion, the present three feasts—of the Publican and the Pharisee, of the Prodigal Son, and of the Second Coming—were conceived by the holy Fathers as a kind of preliminary training and instruction. That we might be pre-disposed and prepared for the spiritual labors of the fasts, putting away our defiled habits from custom. And first of all, they set before us the parable of the Publican and the Pharisee, and name it the Pre-announced Week. For even as those who are about to go forth to bodily warfare learn beforehand from the commanders the time of battle, so that having cleansed and polished their weapons, and having ordered all other things well, and having removed every stumbling block from their midst, they eagerly brace themselves for the contests, and provide what is needed. And often before the engagement they bring to mind words, narratives, and parables, sharpening the souls of the young unto zeal, and driving away laziness, fear, despondency, and whatever else is harmful. So also the divine Fathers sound the trumpet beforehand, sending fasting as an army against the demons, so that for our souls they might cleanse away any pre-existing passion, and the poison wrought by long time; and further, that what we do not possess of good things we might eagerly acquire, and having armed ourselves fittingly, might thus go forth prepared unto the labors of the fast. For since the first weapon unto virtue is repentance and humility, and conversely the greatest obstacle unto humility is pride and arrogance, they set forth this present venerable parable from the divine Gospel first of all. Teaching us through the Pharisee to put away the passion of pride and arrogance, and through the Publican conversely to produce the contrary of this passion, humility and repentance. For the first and worst passion is pride and arrogance, through which the devil fell from heaven, who before that was Lucifer, but through these became darkness and was so called. And the forefather Adam on account of these was cast out from paradise. Through these the saints teach us in a certain manner that no one should exalt himself over his good deeds, nor rise up against his neighbor, but always be humble: for the Lord resists the proud, but gives grace unto the humble; for it is better for the sinner to turn back than for him who does right to exalt himself. For I say unto you, He said, that the Publican went down justified rather than the Pharisee. Therefore the parable shows that no one should exalt himself, even if he has good deeds; but always humble himself, and pray from the soul unto God, even if he fall into the lowest evils, for he is not far from salvation. For the Publican is he who takes taxes from the princes, and through extreme injustice buys and acquires therefrom. And the Pharisee is as one cut off, perhaps, and surpassing others in knowledge. And the Sadducee from a certain Zadok, which means righteous: for tsedek is righteousness. And there were three sects among the Jews: Essenes, Pharisees, and Sadducees, who accepted neither the resurrection, nor an angel, nor the spirit to exist. By the prayers of all Thy holy hymnodists, O Christ our God, have mercy on us. Amen.

*Ode 7. Heirmos: "The God-given furnace:"*

Exalted by deeds of righteousness, the Pharisee was grievously puffed up by the snares of vainglory, boasting immeasurably; but the Publican, borne up on the light wings of humility, drew near unto God.

Using humility as a ladder after a certain manner, the Publican was raised up to heavenly height; but the wretched Pharisee, lifted up by rotten pride and foolishness, descended to the nethermost hell.

The deceitful one ensnares the righteous by images of vainglory, and binds sinners with the nets of despair; but let us who emulate the Publican strive to be delivered from both evils.

With prayer let us fall down before our God, with tears and warm groanings, imitating the Publican's humility that works on high, chanting, O believers: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Glory:*

Instructing Thy disciples, Thou didst foretell, O Master, not to mind high things, but teaching them to associate with the humble, O Savior. Therefore we cry unto Thee, O believers: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*

*[Margin: I]* Knowing thee, O Pure One, as beauty and the divine ladder which Jacob saw of old stretched out on high, descending from above God incarnate, and leading earthly men up again.

*Ode 8. Heirmos: "From the flame for the venerable ones:"*

With a humble-minded disposition, sighing in prayer to the Lord, the Publican found mercy and was saved; but by the image of the cruel, boastful tongue, the Pharisee fell away from righteousness.

Let us believers flee the arrogance, lineage, and named purity of the Pharisee, emulating the well-pardoned humility and disposition of the Publican.

Let us believers utter the words of the Publican in the holy church: "O God, cleanse me," that together with the Publican we may obtain forgiveness, delivered from the ruin of the high-vaunting Pharisee.

Let us all emulate the groaning of the Publican, and speaking unto God with warm tears, let us cry out unto Him: O Lover of mankind, we have sinned, O compassionate and merciful One, cleanse and save us!

*Let us bless the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, the Lord.*

God was inclined by the groaning of the Publican, and having justified him, showed unto all to be ever inclined, asking forgiveness of transgressions with groanings and tears.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*

*[Margin: O]* We know of no other defense besides thee; I set thee forth as an intercessor, O all-immaculate, pure Lady, for I make thee an advocate unto Him Who was born of thee: show me free from all that afflict me.

*Ode 9. Heirmos: "God cannot be seen of men:"*

Having taken from Christ the way of exaltation, humility, as an image of salvation, let us emulate the manner of the Publican, casting far away the arrogance of pride, and moving the Lord to compassion by a disposition of humble-mindedness.

Let us cast away spiritual pride, and acquire the right way of humble-mindedness, not striving to justify ourselves; let us hate the haughtiness of vainglory, and with the Publican let us entreat God.

Let us offer Publican-like prayers of mercy unto the Creator, turning away from the ungrateful prayers of the Pharisees and their boastful voices which bring judgment upon their neighbor, that we may draw God's mercy and light unto ourselves.

Weighed down by an accumulation of many transgressions, I have surpassed the Publican in abundance of malice, and I have acquired the boastful haughtiness of the Pharisee; being utterly bereft of all good things, O Lord, spare me!

Count those worthy of Thy beatitude who are poor in spirit for Thy sake: for by the teaching of Thy commandment, we offer a contrite spirit unto Thee, O Savior; receiving it, save those who serve Thee.

*Glory:*

The Publican, having once prayed in the temple, went in faithfully and was justified: for coming with groanings and tears, and with contrition of heart, he laid aside the whole burden of sins through cleansing.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*

*[Margin: U]* Grant unto us who worthily honor thee, O all-pure one, and who magnify thy childbearing, to sing, glorify, and bless thee, O only blessed one: for thou art the boast of Christians and an acceptable intercessor unto God.

*The Resurrectional Exapostilarion.*[^14]

*Then, of the Triodion. Model: "Let us go up with the disciples:"*

Let us flee the boastful speaking of the most wicked Pharisee, and let us learn the excellent humility of the Publican, that we may be exalted, crying unto God with him: Cleanse Thy servants, O Christ Savior, Who wast born of the Virgin of Thine own will, and didst endure the Cross, raising up the world by Thy divine power!

*Now and ever, Theotokion, same model:*

The Creator of creation, and God of all, took human flesh from thine immaculate womb, O all-immaculate Sovereign Lady, and renewed all my corrupt nature, leaving thee again after childbirth as thou wast before childbirth; therefore, praising thee with faith, we all cry out: Rejoice, O glory of the world!

*At the Praises, 4 Resurrectional stichera of the Octoechos: and 4 idiomelon stichera of the Triodion.*

Let us not pray after the manner of the Pharisee, brethren:

The Pharisee, overcome by vainglory: *[Margin: Written at Vespers.]*

*Verse: Arise, O Lord my God, let Thy hand be lifted up; forget not Thy poor unto the end. Tone 3:*

Having understood the difference between the Publican and the Pharisee, O my soul, abhor the haughty voice of the one, and emulate the prayer of deep compunction of the other, and cry aloud: O God, cleanse me a sinner, and have mercy on me!

*Verse: I will praise Thee, O Lord, with my whole heart; I will speak of all Thy marvelous works.*

Having hated the boastful voice of the Pharisee, O believers, and having emulated the contrite prayer of the Publican, let us not think high things, but humbling ourselves, let us cry aloud with compunction: O God, cleanse our sins!

*Glory, Tone 8:*

Condemning the Pharisee who justified himself by boasting of his deeds, O Lord, and justifying the Publican who humbled himself and asked for cleansing with sighs, Thou dost not give heed to haughty thoughts, nor dost Thou despise contrite hearts. Therefore we also fall down before Thee in humility, Who didst suffer for our sake: grant forgiveness, and great mercy.

*Now and ever: "Thou art most blessed, O Virgin Theotokos:"*
*Great Doxology, and Dismissal.*
*And the customary Litiya in the narthex, in which we sing: Glory, and now and ever: the Matins Gospel sticheron. And the First Hour.*

*It should be known that all 11 Matins Gospel stichera,*[^15] *from this present Sunday and even unto All Saints, are sung at the Matins Litiya in the narthex at "Glory, and now and ever."*

*Be it also known that from this Sunday we begin to read in the narthex, after the dismissal of the Litiya, the Catecheses of our holy father Theodore the Studite.*[^16] *And if the Hegumen is present, they are read by him; but if not, then by the Ecclesiarch, while the brethren stand and listen with attention. At the conclusion of the reading we sing the troparion to the Venerable Theodore, Tone 8: "Teacher of Orthodoxy," without Theotokion. And the complete Dismissal. At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes of the Octoechos: and from the Canon, Ode 6. Prokeimenon of the occurring Tone. The Apostle to Timothy, pericope 296.*[^17] *Alleluia. The Gospel according to Luke, pericope 84.*[^18] *Communion Verse: "Praise the Lord from the heavens:"*

*It should be known that during this week the thrice-accursed Armenians keep their abominable fast, called Artzivurion.*[^19] *We, however (the monastics), on each day (that is, on Wednesday and Friday as well) eat cheese and eggs (at the 4th hour); and the laity eat meat, overturning the decree of that great heresy. If the feast of the Meeting of the Lord happens to fall on Meatfare Saturday, the entire service for the deceased is chanted in the crypt, evening and morning; but if there is no crypt, it is chanted on this Saturday before the Sunday of the Prodigal Son; and there on Meatfare Saturday, the service is chanted for the Feast alone.*

## SUNDAY ON WHICH IS READ THE HOLY GOSPEL OF THE PARABLE OF THE PRODIGAL SON

*On Saturday evening at the Vigil, after the customary Kathisma reading of the Psalter, at "Lord, I have cried," we set 10 verses: and we sing 2 Resurrectional stichera of the Octoechos, and 3 Anatolian; and of the Triodion 5, repeating them. Tone 1:*

Having entrusted myself to a sinless and living land, sowing sin, I reaped the ears of sloth with a sickle, and bound the sheaves of my deeds into bundles, which I spread out not upon the threshing-floor of repentance. But I pray Thee, our pre-eternal Farmer and God, with the wind of Thy loving-kindness winnow the chaff of my deeds, and grant unto my soul the wheat of forgiveness, shutting me up into Thy heavenly granary, and save me.

Let us recognize, brethren, the power of the mystery: for when the prodigal son returned from sin unto the fatherly house, the all-good Father went forth to meet him and kissed him, and again bestowed upon him the knowledge of His own glory; and He made a mystical rejoicing for those on high, slaying the fatted calf, that we might worthily live together with the loving Father Who sacrificed, and with the glorious Offering, the Savior of our souls.

*Glory, Tone 2:*

Oh, of how many good things have I, wretch, deprived myself! Oh, from what a kingdom have I, passionate one, fallen away! I exhausted the wealth which I received; I transgressed the commandment. Woe is me, passionate soul! Thou art henceforth condemned to the eternal fire. Therefore, before the end, cry aloud unto Christ God: Receive me as the prodigal son, O God, and have mercy on me.

*Now and ever, Theotokion of the First Tone. Entrance. "O Gladsome Light:" Prokeimenon: "The Lord reigns:" At the Litiya, the sticheron of the temple as usual.*

*Glory, Tone 4:*

As the prodigal son I also came, O compassionate One, having spent my whole life in wandering; I scattered the riches which Thou gavest me, O Father: receive me repenting, O God, and have mercy on me.

*Now and ever, Theotokion of the same Tone. At the Aposticha of the Octoechos, in alphabetical order. Glory, Idiomelon, Tone 6:*

Having squandered the wealth of the fatherly gift, I pastured with senseless beasts, wretched one; and desiring their food, I wasted with hunger and was not satisfied; but returning unto the compassionate Father, I cry with tears: Receive me as a hired servant falling down before Thy love for mankind, and save me.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*

*O Maker and Redeemer:*[^20] *Dismissal Troparion: "O Virgin Theotokos:" three times. And the rest of the order of the Vigil as usual.*

*At Matins, at "God is the Lord," the Resurrectional Troparion of the Octoechos, and Theotokion; the customary Kathisma reading of the Psalter, and the Polyeleos.*

*The customary two Psalms; and unto these we also append the third Psalm: "By the waters of Babylon,"*[^21] *with the fair Alleluia. The Anavathmoi, and the Prokeimenon of the Tone. "Let every breath praise the Lord:" The Matins Gospel. Then, Glory, Tone 8: "Open unto me the doors of repentance:" Now and ever, Theotokion. Model: "Guide me on the paths of salvation:" Then, Tone 6: "Have mercy on me, O God:" "When I think upon the multitude of my dread deeds:" (see fol. 2).*[^22]

*The Resurrectional Canon, with the Heirmos to 4; and the Cross-Resurrectional to 2; and of the Theotokos to 2; and of the Triodion to 6.*
*The sequence of the Menaion is sung at Compline on Friday evening. The Canon is the work of Lord Joseph.*[^23]

*Ode 1, Tone 2. Heirmos: "A Song of Moses:"*

O Jesus God, receive now me also as the prodigal son as I repent, who have lived my whole life in sloth, and have provoked Thee to wrath.

That divine wealth which Thou didst give me of old, I squandered evilly; I departed far from Thee, living prodigally: O compassionate Father, receive therefore me also as I return.

*Glory:*

Stretching out Thy fatherly embrace now, O Lord, receive me also as the prodigal, O all-compassionate One, that I may thankfully glorify Thee.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*

Having shown forth all Thy goodness upon me, O God, overlook the multitude of my transgressions as the Benefactor, through the divine entreaties of Thy Mother.

*And for the Katavasia we sing the Heirmoi of the Canon:*
*Taking up a song of Moses, cry aloud, O soul: He was unto me a Helper and Protector unto salvation; this is my God, and I will glorify Him.*

*Ode 3. Heirmos: "My barren mind:"*

Being wholly outside of myself, with a darkened mind I cleaved unto the inventors of passions; but receive me, O Christ, as the prodigal.

Emulating the voice of the prodigal, I cry aloud: I have sinned, O Father! As him, therefore, embrace me also now, and cast me not away.

*Glory:*

Stretching out Thine arms, O Christ, mercifully receive me as I return from the far country of sin and passions.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*

O thou who art good among women, enrich me also with forms of virtues, who have been impoverished by many sins, O pure one, that I may glorify thee.

*Heirmos:*
*Show my barren mind to be fruitful, O God, Farmer of good things and Planter of blessings, through Thy tender compassion.*

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 1. Model: "Thy tomb:"*

Make haste to open unto me Thy fatherly embrace; prodigally have I spent my life; looking upon the inexhaustible wealth of Thy compassions, O Savior, despise not now my impoverished heart; for unto Thee, O Lord, I cry with compunction: Father, I have sinned against heaven and before Thee.[^24]

*Glory, the same. Now and ever, Theotokion. Same model:*

O unwedded, pure Virgin Theotokos, only mediatress and shelter of the faithful: deliver all who place their hope in thee, O Maiden, from misfortunes, sorrows, and cruel distresses; and save our souls through thy divine prayers.

*Ode 4. Heirmos: "Thy Nativity from the Virgin:"*

The wealth of good things which Thou gavest me, O heavenly Father, I squandered evilly, enslaved unto strange citizens; therefore I cry unto Thee: I have sinned against Thee; receive me as the prodigal of old, stretching out Thine arms unto me.

I was enslaved to every evil, bowing down wretchedly to the workers of passions, and through heedlessness I came to be outside of myself; have compassion on me, O Savior, heavenly Father, who flee unto Thy many compassions.

*Glory:*

I am filled with all shame, not daring to gaze up to the heavenly height; for having senselessly bowed down to sin, now returning I cry with compunction: I have sinned against Thee; receive me, O King of all.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*

O help of men, firm hope of all Christians, pure refuge of the saved: save me, O Virgin, by thy motherly prayers, and account me worthy of the life to come.

*Heirmos:*
*Foreseeing Thy Nativity from the Virgin, the Prophet proclaimed, crying aloud: I heard Thy report and was afraid; for from Teman and from the holy overshadowed mountain Thou hast come, O Christ.*[^25]

*Ode 5. Heirmos: "The night having passed:"*

I was enslaved to strange citizens, and went away into a corrupting country, and was filled with shame; but now returning, I call unto Thee, O compassionate One: I have sinned.

Open unto me now Thy fatherly compassions, who have turned away from evils, O heavenly Father, and cast me not away, Who hast exceeding great mercy.

*Glory:*

I dare not look up on high, having provoked Thee to wrath without number, O Christ; but knowing Thy merciful compassions, I cry: I have sinned against Thee; cleanse and save me.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*

O most holy Virgin full of grace, who didst bear the cleansing for all: lighten the heavy burden of my transgressions by thy prayers.

*Heirmos:*
*The night having passed, the day has drawn near, and the light has shone forth upon the world; therefore the angelic ranks praise Thee, and all creation glorifies Thee.*

*Ode 6. Heirmos: "In the depth of sin:"*

The depth of transgressions holds me fast continually, and the tempest of sins drowns me; pilot me to the haven of life, O Christ God, and save me, O King of glory.

I squandered my fatherly wealth cruelly, and became impoverished, and was filled with shame, enslaved to unfruitful thoughts; therefore I cry unto Thee: O Lover of mankind, have compassion and save me.

*Glory:*

Wasting away with hunger for all good things, and having estranged myself from Thee, O all-good One, have compassion on me who now return, and save me, O Christ, who sing of Thy love for mankind.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*

Having given birth to Christ the Savior and Redeemer, account me worthy of salvation, O Maiden, who am impoverished of all good things, O pure Virgin, that I may sing of thy marvelous deeds.

*Heirmos:*

I am held fast in the depth of sin, O Savior, and am storm-tossed in the tempest of life; but as Jonah from the whale, lead me up also from the passions, and save me.

*Kontakion, Tone 3. Model: "Today the Virgin:"*[^26]

I have senselessly withdrawn from Thy fatherly glory, and in evils have squandered the riches which Thou didst deliver unto me; therefore I offer unto Thee the voice of the prodigal: I have sinned before Thee, O compassionate Father; receive me repenting, and make me as one of Thy hired servants.

*Ikos:*

As our Savior daily teaches us with His own voice, let us hear the Scriptures concerning the prodigal, and chaste once again; and let us emulate his good repentance with faith; unto Him Who knows the hidden secrets of all, let us cry aloud with humility of heart: We have sinned against Thee, O compassionate Father, and are nevermore worthy to be called children, as before; but as Thou art by nature the Lover of mankind, do Thou receive me, and make me as one of Thy hired servants.

*And the reading takes place, first of the Synaxarion in the Menaion; then in the Triodion according to the order.*

*Verses:*
*If any man be a prodigal like me, let him take courage and come:*
*For the door of God's compassions is opened unto all.*

*On this day we celebrate the return of the prodigal son,*[^27] *which our divine fathers instituted second in the Triodion, for the following reason: Because there are certain men who, conscious in themselves of many terrible deeds, and having lived very prodigally from youth, spending their time in drunkenness and impurities, and having thus fallen into the depth of evils, fall into despair (which is the offspring of pride); and hence they are by no means willing to come unto the care of virtue, and proposing evil deeds, they fall headlong into yet worse evils. The holy Fathers, having a loving and fatherly disposition toward such men, and desiring to rescue them from despair, instituted this parable here after the first, uprooting the passion of despair from the very root and raising them up to the acquisition of virtue, showing forth the loving and all-good compassions of God unto those who have sinned greatly and lived prodigally; demonstrating from this parable of Christ that there is no sin that can overcome His love for mankind. For the two sons of the man (that is, of the God-Man, the Word) are the righteous and the sinners. The elder is he who abides continually in the commandments of God and in His goodness, never departing from Him. The younger is he who loved sin, and by shameful deeds of self-will broke away from fellowship under the yoke; and in him the love of God for mankind was revealed, though he had lived prodigally: for he did not preserve whole that which was according to the image, but followed the wicked demon, and was enslaved through pleasures to the will of the evil one, yet was unable to satisfy his desire; for sin is an insatiable thing, tempting by custom for the sake of temporary enjoyment. This the parable likens unto husks, which are the food of swine: for husks at first offer something sweet, but afterward become something harsh and like chaff, which is very much the nature of shame and sin. Scarcely therefore recovering himself, the prodigal, perishing as it were from hunger for virtue, comes to the Father, saying: Father, I have sinned against heaven and before Thee, and am no more worthy to be called Thy son. And He receives him repenting, not reproaching him, but spreading forth His arms and embracing him, showing forth His divine and fatherly tender compassions. And He gives him a robe, that is, Holy Baptism; and a ring and pledge, the grace of the All-Holy Spirit; and unto these also sandals, that his steps toward God may no more be wounded by serpents and scorpions, but that he may rather be able to crush their heads. Afterward, with exceeding great joy, the Father slays the fatted calf for his sake, His Only-begotten Son, and gives him to partake of His Flesh and Blood. And though the elder son marveled at His overflowing mercy, saying whatever he said, the Lover of mankind silences him also, entering in with quiet, meek, and affectionate words: "Thou art ever with Me," saying, "and it was fitting to rejoice and celebrate with the Father, for this my son was dead in sin before, and is alive again, having repented of the irrational things he did; and he was lost, having been far from Me by custom of pleasures, and is found by Me Who suffered through My tender compassion and called him with a merciful disposition." This parable may also be applied to the Jewish people and to us. For this reason therefore this parable was instituted here by the Holy Fathers: uprooting, as was said, despair and fear of repenting by good deeds, and instructing unto repentance and compunction those who have sinned like the prodigal; which is indeed the greatest weapon for driving away the arrows of the adversary, and a mighty help. Through Thine ineffable love for mankind, O Christ our God, have mercy on us. Amen.*

*Ode 7. Heirmos: "Emulating the Cherubim:"*

I bowed down unto bodily pleasures in utter wretchedness, and was completely enslaved to passionate inventions, and became estranged from Thee, O Lover of mankind; but now I cry with the voice of the prodigal: I have sinned, O Christ, despise me not, as Thou alone art merciful.

I cry aloud: I have sinned! In no wise daring to look up unto the heavenly height, O King of all; for in folly I alone provoked Thee to wrath, having rejected Thy commandments; therefore, as Thou alone art good, cast me not away from Thy presence.

*Glory:*

By the supplications of the Apostles, O Lord, and of the Prophets, and of the Venerable, and of the honorable Martyrs, and of the Righteous: forgive me all wherein I have sinned, provoking Thy goodness to wrath, O Christ, that I may hymn Thee unto all ages.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*

Shown forth higher than the Cherubim and Seraphim, and more radiant than all the heavenly hosts: with them entreat the divine Word of the unoriginate Father, Whom thou didst incarnate, O all-immaculate one, that we all may be accounted worthy of the eternal good things.

*Heirmos:*
*Emulating the Cherubim, the Children in the furnace danced, crying aloud: Blessed art Thou, O God, for in truth and in judgment Thou hast brought all these things upon us because of our sins; Thou Who art exceedingly praised and glorified unto all ages.*

*Ode 8. Heirmos: "In the bush unto Moses:"*

O Thou Who camest down to earth to save the world through voluntary poverty out of much tender compassion: save me, who am now impoverished of every good deed, as Thou art merciful.

I departed far from Thy commandments, and in utter wretchedness was enslaved to deceit; but now receive me who return and fall down before Thee as the prodigal of old, O heavenly Father.

*Let us bless the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, the Lord.*

By corrupting thoughts I became completely darkened, and departed far from Thee, being wholly outside of myself, O compassionate One; therefore save me as I fall down before Thee in repentance.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*

O pure Parent of God, sole restoration of the fallen: restore me also, who am crushed by all kinds of sins, and humbled.

*Heirmos:*
*Praise, bless, and supreme exalt Him unto all ages, Who of old prefigured the miracle of the Virgin unto Moses in the bush on Mount Sinai.*

*Ode 9. Heirmos: "Who of the earthborn has heard such a thing:"*

Behold, O Christ, the sorrow of my heart; behold my return; behold my tears, O Savior, and despise me not; but embrace me again for Thy compassion's sake, numbering me with the multitude of the saved, that I may thankfully sing of Thy mercies.

Like the thief I cry: Remember me; like the publican with compunction I beat my breast, and now call out: Cleanse me! As the prodigal, receive me, O all-compassionate One, from all my evils, O King of all, that I may hymn Thine extreme condescension.

Sigh now, O my utterly wretched soul, and cry aloud unto Christ: O Lord, Who for my sake didst voluntarily become poor, enrich me with the wealth of good things, who am impoverished of every good deed, as Thou alone art good and plenteous in mercy.

*Glory:*

The rejoicing which Thou didst once make at the willing return of the prodigal, O God: do Thou make this now also over me, wretched one, stretching out Thine honorable arms unto me, that being saved I may hymn Thine extreme condescension.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*

By thy radiant prayers, O Virgin, enlighten my spiritual eyes, which are darkened by evil, I pray thee, and lead me into the paths of repentance, that I may worthily hymn thee, who didst bear in the flesh the Word beyond all word.

*Heirmos:*
*Who of the earthborn has heard such a thing, or who has ever seen that a Virgin was found with child in the womb, and without travail gave birth to an infant? Such is thy wonder, and thee, O pure Theotokos, do we magnify.*

*The Resurrectional Exapostilarion of the Octoechos; then the following of the Triodion.*
*Model: "Hear, O women:"*

Having departed, wretched one, I spent the wealth of grace which Thou gavest me, O Savior, living prodigally, and scattering it deceitfully unto demons; therefore receive me as I return, as the prodigal, O compassionate Father, and save me.

*Another, same model. Glory:*

I have squandered and spent Thy wealth, O Lord, and in wretchedness was subject to wicked demons; but O Savior all-compassionate, have pity on the prodigal, and cleanse me who am defiled, restoring unto me the first robe of Thy kingdom.

*Now and ever, Theotokion. Same model:*

O holy Virgin Mother, great proclamation of the Apostles, Martyrs, Prophets, and the Venerable: make Thy Son and Lord merciful unto us thy servants, O Parent of God, when He sits to judge each according to his worth.

*At the Praises, 4 Resurrectional stichera of the Octoechos, and 1 Anatolian;*[^28] *and 3 idiomelon stichera of the Triodion. Tone 2:*

I offer unto Thee the voice of the prodigal, O Lord: I have sinned before Thine eyes, O good One; I have squandered the wealth of Thy gifts; but receive me repenting, O Savior, and save me.

*Tone 4. Verse: Arise, O Lord my God, let Thy hand be lifted up; forget not Thy poor unto the end:*

As the prodigal son I also came, O compassionate One, having spent my whole life in wandering; I scattered the riches which Thou didst give me, O Father: receive me repenting, O God, and have mercy on me.

*Tone 8. Verse: I will praise Thee, O Lord, with my whole heart; I will speak of all Thy marvelous works:*

Prodigally I spent the wealth of my fatherly estate, and having scattered it, I was destitute, dwelling in the land of wicked citizens; and no longer enduring fellowship with them, returning I cry unto Thee, the compassionate Father: I have sinned against heaven and before Thee, and am no more worthy to be called Thy son; make me as one of Thy hired servants, O God, and have mercy on me.

*Glory, Tone 6:*

O good Father, I departed far from Thee; leave me not, neither show me to be unprofitable for Thy kingdom. The all-wicked enemy stripped me and took my wealth; I squandered the spiritual gifts prodigally; arising therefore, returning unto Thee I cry: Make me as one of Thy hired servants; O Thou Who for my sake didst stretch out Thy most pure hands upon the Cross, that Thou mightest snatch me away from the cruel beast, and clothe me in the first robe, as Thou alone art plenteous in mercy.

*Now and ever: "Thou art most blessed, O Virgin Theotokos:"*

*Great Doxology. Litanies, and Dismissal. And the customary Litiya, at which is sung: Glory, and now and ever: the Matins Gospel sticheron; and the Catecheses are read. And the First Hour in the narthex, and the complete Dismissal. At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes of the Octoechos to 6, and of the Triodion Ode 6, to 4. Prokeimenon of the Apostle according to the Tone. The Apostle to the Corinthians, pericope 135.*[^29] *Alleluia of the Tone. The Gospel according to Luke, pericope 79.*[^30] *Communion Verse: "Praise the Lord from the heavens:"*

*It should be known that in Meatfare week we do not sing "Alleluia" on weekdays; we omit one Kathisma of the Psalter from Matins, and recite it at Vespers. We do not recite the Biblical Canticles in the Psalter. Neither the Mid-Hours nor the Supplicatory Canon to the Most Holy Theotokos at Compline are chanted; and Small Compline is sung. In like manner we do in Cheesefare week, except on Wednesday and Friday; but the Fathers have indicated concerning all this in that place. And on any day of this week at Matins we read the Homily of Saint Macarius concerning the Forty Days and the Fifty Days,*[^31] *whose beginning is:*

*My little children, my heart rejoices for your sake:*

*Be it also known that the sequence of occurring Saints on Meatfare Saturday and Meatfare Sunday is sung at the preceding Complines. We do likewise concerning Cheesefare Saturday and Cheesefare Sunday; or as the Superior decides, unless the commemoration of a great Saint occurs anywhere.*

## ON MEATFARE SATURDAY

*We perform the commemoration of all Orthodox Christians who from the ages have fallen asleep, our fathers and brethren.*[^32]

*On Friday evening, after the Introductory Psalm and the customary Kathisma reading of the Psalter, at "Lord, I have cried," we set 6 verses: and we sing 3 Martyrs' stichera of the Octoechos, of the Tone of the week;*
*And 3 prosomoia of the Triodion. Tone 8. Model: "Paradise in Eden:"*

Making memory today, O believers, of all the dead from the ages by name who have lived piously in faith, let us praise the Savior and Lord, asking earnestly that He may grant them at the hour of judgment to give a good answer unto that same God of ours Who judges all the earth, to obtain a place at His right hand in joy, in the portion of the righteous and in the bright lot of the Saints, and to be worthy of His heavenly kingdom.

Thou Who with Thy blood didst ransom men, O Savior, and by Thy death didst deliver us from bitter death, and dost bestow eternal life upon us by Thy Resurrection: give rest, O Lord, to all who have fallen asleep piously, whether in deserts, or in cities, or in the sea, or on land, or in any place: rulers, hierarchs, bishops, monks, and laymen, of every age of all humankind; and account them worthy of Thy heavenly kingdom.

By Thy rising from the dead, O Christ, death no longer holds dominion over those who have died piously; therefore we pray earnestly: Give rest unto Thy servants in Thy courts and in the bosom of Abraham, who from Adam even unto this day have served Thee purely, our fathers and brethren, friends and kinsmen, every man who has served faithfully in this life and has departed unto Thee in manifold ways and manners, O God; and account them worthy of Thy heavenly kingdom.

*Glory, Tone 8:*

I weep and lament when I contemplate death, and behold our beauty created according to the image of God lying in the tombs, formless, inglorious, having no shape.[^33] O wonder! What is this mystery that has come to pass concerning us? How have we been handed over unto corruption? How have we been yoked unto death? Truly by the command of God, as it is written, Who grants rest unto the departed.

*Now and ever, the First Theotokion of the Tone.*
*O Gladsome Light: And instead of the Prokeimenon, we sing "Alleluia," in Tone 8.*
*Verse: Blessed are they whom Thou hast chosen and taken, O Lord, and their memory is from generation to generation.*[^34]
*Verse: Their souls shall dwell amid good things.*[^35]

*At the Aposticha, the Martyrs' sticheron of the Tone, and 2 funeral stichera of John Damascene.*[^36] *And we append the above-mentioned verses:*
*Blessed are they whom Thou hast chosen and taken, O Lord, and their memory is from generation to generation.*
*And: Their souls shall dwell amid good things.*

*Glory, Tone 6:*

Thy creative command was my origin and substance: for wishing to fashion me as a living creature out of invisible and visible nature, Thou didst fashion my body from the earth, and didst give me a soul by Thy divine and life-creating breath; therefore, O Savior, give rest unto Thy servants in the land of the living, and in the tents of the righteous.

*Now and ever, Now and ever, Theotokion, same Tone:*

By the prayers of her who gave birth to Thee, O Christ, of Thy martyrs, and Apostles, and Prophets, and Hierarchs, of the Venerable, and Righteous, and of all the Saints: give rest unto Thy departed servants.

*"Now Thou dost dismiss:" Troparion, Tone 8:*

O Thou Who with profound wisdom dost order all things with love for mankind, and dost bestow upon all that which is profitable, O sole Creator: give rest, O Lord, to the souls of Thy servants, for they have placed their hope in Thee, our Maker and Fashioner and God.

*Glory, and now and ever, Theotokion, same Tone:*

We have thee as a wall and a haven, and an acceptable intercessor before God Whom thou didst bear, O unwedded Theotokos, salvation of the faithful.

*Litany, and Dismissal.*
*And after the dismissal of Vespers, we celebrate a Panikhida for the deceased in the narthex, and sing the Canon for the dead of the Tone of the week.*[^37]

*At Matins, after the Six Psalms, "Alleluia," in Tone 8. Troparion: "O Thou Who with profound wisdom:" twice. Glory, and now and ever, Theotokion: "We have thee as a wall and a haven:" And the customary Kathisma reading of the Psalter. The words concerning the dead from the First Epistle to the Corinthians are also read.*[^38] *The Amomos (Psalm 118) is sung in two stases,*[^39] *with the refrains: "Blessed art Thou, O Lord:" in Tone 5. And after them, the Troparia of the Dead, Tone 5:*

*Refrain: Blessed art Thou, O Lord, teach me Thy statutes.*[^40]

The choir of the Saints has found the Fountain of Life and the Door of Paradise; may I also find the way through repentance: I am the lost sheep, call me back, O Savior, and save me.

*Blessed art Thou, O Lord:*

Having proclaimed the Lamb of God, and having been slain as lambs, O holy ones, and having passed over unto the never-aging and ever-existing life: do ye martyrs earnestly pray Him to grant us remission of debts.

*Blessed art Thou, O Lord:*

Ye who have walked the narrow way of sorrow, all ye who in life have taken up the cross as a yoke, and followed Me in faith: come, enjoy the honors and the heavenly crowns which I have prepared for you.

*Blessed art Thou, O Lord:*

I am an image of Thine ineffable glory, though I bear the wounds of transgressions; have compassion on Thy creature, O Master, and cleanse me through Thy tender compassion, and bestow upon me the longed-for fatherland, making me again a citizen of Paradise.

*Blessed art Thou, O Lord:*

Thou Who of old didst fashion me from nothingness, and didst honor me with Thy divine image, but through transgression of the commandment didst return me again unto the earth from which I was taken: lead me back unto that which is according to Thy likeness, to be refashioned in the ancient beauty.

*Blessed art Thou, O Lord:*

Give rest, O God, unto Thy servants, and establish them in Paradise, where the choirs of the Saints, O Lord, and the righteous shine as luminaries; give rest unto Thy departed servants, overlooking all their transgressions.

*Glory:*

Devoutly let us hymn the threefold radiance of the one Godhead, crying aloud: Holy art Thou, O unoriginate Father, co-unoriginate Son, and divine Spirit; enlighten us who serve Thee in faith, and snatch us from the eternal fire.

*Now and ever:*

Rejoice, O pure one, who didst bear God in the flesh for the salvation of all, through whom the human race found salvation; through thee may we find Paradise, O pure, blessed Theotokos.

*Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia, glory to Thee, O God. Three times. We sing the Litany for the deceased: "Again and again in peace:" The Priest recites the prayer: "O God of spirits:"*[^41] *And we chant: "Lord, have mercy," 40 times.*

*And after the exclamation, the Sessional Hymn, Tone 5:*

Give rest with the righteous unto Thy servants, O our Savior, and settle them in Thy courts, as it is written: overlooking as good their transgressions, voluntary and involuntary, and all that they did in knowledge or in ignorance, O Lover of mankind.

*Glory, and now and ever, Theotokion:*

O Christ God Who didst shine forth unto the world from the Virgin, and through her didst reveal sons of light: have mercy on us.

*And we recite the Biblical Canticles: "Let us sing unto the Lord:"*
*And we sing the Canon of the patron saint of the monastery to 6, and of the Triodion to 8. The Second Ode is also sung without the Canticle versification. And again of the Psalter. The Canon is the work of the Studite;*[^42] *in the Triadica and Theotokia troparia the acrostic is:*
*Of unworthy Theodore.*[^43]

*Tone 8. Ode 1. Heirmos: "Let us send up a song, O people:"*

Let us all pray unto Christ, making memory today of the dead from the ages, that He may deliver from the eternal fire those who have fallen asleep in faith and in the hope of eternal life.

By the depth of Thy judgments, O Christ, all-wisely hast Thou foreordained the end of life of each man, its term and manner; therefore save at the judgment, O all-compassionate One, those whom the grave has covered in every land.

O Thou Who gavest the terms of our life, show forth as sons of the day that knows no evening, O Lord, those who have fallen asleep from the night of this life: orthodox priests, rulers, and all Thy people.

Those whom the water covered, and whom war mowed down, whom earthquake seized, and whom murderers slew, and whom fire consumed: among the faithful, O merciful One, assign them unto the portion of the righteous.

Overlooking all our bodily debts, O our Savior, at every age of all the human race, place uncondemned before Thy judgment seat those who give answer unto Thee, the Creator.

*Glory, Trinity Hymn:*

*[Margin: T]* I sing of the three hypostatic Persons of one essence: the unbegotten Father, the begotten Son, and the Holy Spirit; unoriginate kingdom, authority, one Godhead.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*

*[Margin: O]* Truly thou hast appeared as a heaven on earth, greater than the highest heaven, O unwedded Virgin: for from thee the Sun shone forth in the world, reigning with righteousness.

*Katavasia:*
*Let us send up a song, O people, unto our marvelous God, Who freed Israel from bondage, singing a song of victory and crying aloud: Let us sing unto Thee, the only Master.*

*Ode 2. Heirmos:*
*See, see, that I am your God, begotten before the ages of the Father, and from the Virgin in these latter days conceived without a man, and having loosed the sin of forefather Adam, as the Lover of mankind.*

See, see, that I am your God, Who by righteous judgment hast fixed the bounds of life, receiving into incorruption from corruption all who have fallen asleep in hope of the eternal resurrection.

From the four corners of the earth, O Lord, receiving those who have fallen asleep in faith: in the sea, or on land, or in rivers, springs, lakes, or pits, or who became food for beasts, birds, and reptiles: give rest unto all.

All things are in Thy hand, O Lord; Thou hast foreordained that those who have dissolved into the four elements, having gathered them at Thy coming, Thou wilt raise up, forgiving them all transgressions committed in ignorance or in knowledge.

Oh, of Thy dread Second Coming, O Lord! For coming upon earth as in the form of lightning, Thou wilt raise all Thy creation to be judged: account those who then lived in faith toward Thee and met Thee to be with Thee.

*Glory, Trinity Hymn:*

*[Margin: Y]* All-perfect Trinity, pre-divine, tri-hypostatic, unbegotten Father, and Only-begotten Son, Spirit proceeding from the Father and revealed through the Son: one essence and nature, Lordship, Kingdom, save us all.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*

*Theotokion:*

*[Margin: T]* Ineffable is the miracle of thy childbirth, O Virgin Mother: for how dost thou give birth, and art still pure? How dost thou bear an Infant, and knowest no experience of man at all? Even as the Word of God born of thee, Who was incarnate beyond nature, knows.

*Katavasia: "See, see, that I am:"*

*Ode 3. Heirmos: "Thou Who hast established with Thy hand:"*

Account those who have passed the course of life worthy, O God, to be clothed in the pious glory of the crowns of the righteous, and to enjoy eternal good things.

Those suddenly snatched away, consumed by lightning, frozen by frost, and slain by every wound: give rest unto them, O God, when Thou shalt try all things with fire.

Those who have sailed over the ever-surging sea of life, O Christ: account them worthy to run unto the incorruptible haven of Thy life, who were piloted by an Orthodox life.

Those whom every creature of the sea and birds of heaven received as food, O Christ: by Thy judgments raise them up with glory in the last day, O God.

*Glory, Trinity Hymn:*

*[Margin: A]* In mind I contemplate the divine Unity in three Persons, simply cutting together that which is indivisible; for as swift lightning shining in three radiances it is seen in unity.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*

*[Margin: P]* Inscrutable is thy wonder: for without a man thou dost give birth, and dost preserve thy virginity after childbirth, O pure one; therefore the multitude of angels and the human race hymn thee unto ages.

*Katavasia:*
*Thou Who didst establish the heavens with Thy hand, O Word of God, by the enlightenment of Thy true knowledge: establish also the hearts of us who hope in Thee.*

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 5. Model: "Co-unoriginate Word:"*

O Thou Who for our sake didst endure the Cross and death, and didst put Hades to death, and didst raise the dead together with Thyself: give rest unto those who have departed from us, O Savior, as Thou art the God Who lovest mankind; and at Thy trembling and dread coming, O Giver of life, as Thou hast a multitude of mercies, account them worthy of Thy kingdom.

*Glory, the same. Now and ever, Theotokion:*

Show forth thy swift protection, help, and mercy upon thy servants, and calm the waves of vain thoughts, O pure one; and raise up my fallen soul, O Theotokos: for I know, yea, I know, O Virgin, that thou canst do whatsoever thou dost will.

*Ode 4. Heirmos: "From the overshadowed mountain:"*

Fathers and forefathers, grandfathers and great-grandfathers, from the first even unto the last, who have died in righteousness and in the right faith: remember them all, O our Savior.

Those left behind in faith on mountains, on journeys, in desert places, monks and laymen, youths and elders: settle them with the Saints, O Christ.

Those who have departed unexpectedly from sorrow and joy, who through faith immediately changed this life, who suffered in prosperity or in adversity: give rest unto all, O our Savior.

Those whom the sword slew, and the horse dragged away, whom hail, snow, and torrential rain destroyed, whom a falling tile suffocated, or dust covered over: give rest unto them, O Christ our Savior.[^44]

*Glory, Trinity Hymn:*

*[Margin: E]* Strange it is how the Godhead is one and three, all undivided in each single Person: for Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are worshipped as one God.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*

*[Margin: I]* Guide us, O Virgin, by thy prayers, piloting those storm-tossed by the waves of sin unto the saving havens, O Parent of God,[^45] delivering them from all cruel things.

*Katavasia:*
*From the overshadowed mountain, O Word, the prophet divinely foresaw thee, the only Theotokos, about to become incarnate, and with fear he glorified Thy power.*

*Ode 5. Heirmos: "My spirit rises early:"*

Making memory today of each of the dead who have lived piously from the ages, O Lord, we earnestly cry unto Thee: Give rest unto them all with Thy Saints.

From every generation and generation whomsoever Thou hast received, whether among kings, princes, or Orthodox monastics: deliver them from eternal torment, O Merciful One.

O Thou Who knowest what is profitable for all whom Thou hast fashioned, unto whomsoever Thou didst permit, O Lord, to die unexpectedly by sudden falls: deliver them from all torment, O our God.

From the unquenchable fire, and from lightless darkness, from the gnashing of teeth, and the worm that torments without end, and from every punishment: deliver all who have died in faith, O our Savior.

*Glory, Trinity Hymn:*

*[Margin: Θ]* Co-enthroned, unoriginate, Tri-hypostatic Unity, unity by division, and possessing one nature across Persons: unite us unto the one desire of Thy commandments.[^46]

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*

*[Margin: Y]* Beyond the fiery Seraphim hast thou been revealed more honorable, O pure one, having given birth unto the Savior Jesus, Who is inaccessible unto them, and Who by His incarnation deified the clay of the earthborn.

*Katavasia:*
*My spirit rises early unto Thee, O God, for Thy commandments are a light of Thy coming; wherewith do Thou enlighten our mind, O Master, and guide us unto the path of life.*

*Ode 6. Heirmos: "Held fast by many sins:"*

Having loosed the pains of death by suffering, O Author of life, our God: give rest unto Thy servants who have fallen asleep from the ages.

By Thine unsearchable judgments, give rest with the Saints, O Lord, unto those whom poisonous potions have slain, or bone-choking and strangling have suffocated.

When Thou shalt judge all things, as they stand naked and bare before Thy face: then, O Merciful One, spare those who have served Thee in faith, O God.

When Thine Archangel shall sound the final trumpet unto the resurrection of the life of all: then, O Christ, give rest unto Thy servants.

Account worthy all the faithful human race whom Thou hast received from the ages, O God, to glorify Thee unto the ages with those who serve Thee.

*Glory, Trinity Hymn:*

*[Margin: O]* Thrice-holy, co-enthroned Godhead: Father, Son, with the Holy Spirit; Thou art my God, Who by Thy sovereign might upholdest all things.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*

*[Margin: Δ]* From thy root has blossomed forth the Flower of life; leap for joy, O forefather Jesse! For Christ God, Who saves the world, comes forth from the pure Maiden.

*Katavasia:*
*Receive me who am held fast by many sins, O Lover of mankind, and who fall down before Thy compassions, as Thou didst the Prophet, O Lord, and save me.*

*Kontakion, Tone 8:*
With the Saints give rest, O Christ, unto the souls of Thy servants, where there is neither sickness, nor sorrow, nor sighing, but life everlasting.

*Ikos:*
Thou alone art immortal, Who hast made and fashioned man; for we mortals were formed from the earth, and unto the same earth shall we go, as Thou didst command Who fashioned me and said unto me: "For dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return,"[^48] whither all we mortals go, making the funeral lamentation a song: Alleluia.

*Synaxarion of the Menaion first, then the following:*

*Verses:*
Call not to mind the transgressions of the departed, O Word;
Show not Thy good compassions to be dead.

On this day, the most divine Fathers instituted the commemoration of all people who have piously fallen asleep from the ages, for the following reason:[^47] Forasmuch as some people often met an untimely death while journeying abroad, in the sea, in impassable mountains, on precipices and chasms, in pestilences, famines, conflagrations, freezes, wars, cold, and having endured all other manners of death; likewise being poor and infirm, they were not accounted worthy of the prescribed psalms and memorial hymns. Moved by love for mankind, the divine Fathers decreed that the Catholic Church celebrate a general commemoration of all these, having received this tradition from the holy Apostles, so that those who did not receive the individual prescribed services may also be remembered in this common commemoration, showing that what is done on their behalf procures great benefit for them. In one way, then, the Church of God makes commemoration for souls thus. In the second place, since they intended to set the Second Coming of Christ upon the following day, they fittingly make commemoration of souls, as it were supplicating the dread and impartial Judge to show His customary mercy unto them and to establish them in the promised delight. In another way, as the holy Fathers intend to set forth Adam’s expulsion on the coming Sunday, they devise this day as a kind of resting-place, and most conclusively of all, by our present resting-place today, they might begin as it were from the beginning; for the last of all who have lived among us shall be examined at the unendurable judgment, and by terrifying men with these things, they may make them well-disposed toward the ascetical struggles of the Fast. We always make commemoration of souls on Saturday, because "Sabbath" signifies "rest" in Hebrew; and for the dead, as having rested from worldly and all other cares, on the day of rest we make supplications for them; which indeed is observed on every Saturday, but today we commemorate them universally, praying for every pious soul. For the divine Fathers knew that the memorials made for the reposed—I mean alms and liturgies—bring them great relief and benefit; and they urge the Church to perform this both privately and in common, having received this from the holy Apostles, as has been said. Even as Dionysius the Areopagite says, that the things done for them benefit souls;[^49] and this is testified by many others as well. Gregory the Theologian also establishes that offerings for the departed are good, in his funeral oration on his brother Caesarius; and the great Chrysostom, writing to the Philippians, says thus: "Let us devise benefit for the departed; let us give them fitting assistance—alms, I mean, and oblations; for this brings great alleviation to them, and especially gain and benefit. For not in vain was this decreed, nor was it by chance that it was handed down to the Church of God by His all-wise disciples, that the priests should make commemoration of the reposed in faith at the dread Mysteries." And again: "Include in thy testament thy children and relatives, and let thy document have an heir and one name; but let not thy memorial leave the poor without a portion, and I will be surety for them." Whatsoever things are done for the departed provide benefit, as the divine Fathers declare. For this reason we make commemoration of souls; do Thou, O Master Christ, establish them in the dwellings of Thy righteous ones, and have mercy on us, as Thou alone art immortal. Amen.

*Ode 7. Heirmos: "Thou Who in the beginning didst establish the earth:"*

Commemorating those who have piously departed from the ages, we cry out: Blessed art Thou unto the ages, O Lord God of our fathers.

Unto those who have died piously of a sudden, and who have fallen from every precipice, from trees, iron, or any stone: give rest, O God, unto the faithful departed.

At Thy dread coming, O Merciful One, set at the right hand of Thy sheep those who in life have served Thee in Orthodox fashion, O Christ, and have passed over unto Thee.

Rank Thy servants in the choir of Thine elect, O Christ, that they may cry out unto Thee: Blessed art Thou unto the ages, O Lord God of our fathers.

O merciful Savior, Who didst fashion dust from the earth and quickened the flesh with the Spirit: give rest in the unfading life, O God, unto those whom Thou hast received.

*Glory, Trinity Hymn:*

*[Margin: Ω]* Even as the Godhead is praised as with three suns by a single commingling of light: Father, and Son, and the divine Spirit, one in essence, yet three in hypostases.[^50]

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*

*[Margin: Ρ]* In concord with David we chant unto thee a hymn, calling thee the mountain of God, O Virgin, in whom the Word, having dwelt in the flesh, divinely deified us unto Himself.

*Katavasia:*
*Thou Who in the beginning didst establish the earth, and by the Word didst make firm the heavens: blessed art Thou unto the ages, O Lord God of our fathers.*

*Ode 8. Heirmos: "Glorified on the holy mountain:"*

O Lord of glory, Who didst first destroy the shadow of death and didst shine forth as the sun from the tomb: make sons of Thy resurrection all who have died in faith unto the ages.

O Witness of things unknown and secret, when Thou shalt reveal the works of darkness and the counsels of our hearts: then enter not into reckoning with all who have fallen asleep in faith.

When Thou shalt sit upon the throne and command those gathered by the trumpet from the ends of the earth to stand before the judgment: then spare all, O Christ, forasmuch as Thou art merciful.

Unto those who have died suddenly by firebrands, or by violent apoplexy, swift current, suffocation, strangling, or beating: O Lord of glory, grant relief unto the ages unto those who have fallen asleep in faith.[^51]

Let us bless the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, the Lord.

*[Margin: O]* I praise Thee as a Unity in essence, and I honor Thee as a Trinity in Persons: Father, and Son, and most Holy Spirit; I glorify the unoriginate dominion of Thy kingdom unto the ages.[^52]

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*

*[Margin: Y]* Thou hast been revealed as a sealed fountain of living water, O Virgin Theotokos; for having given birth without a man unto the Lord, thou dost water the faithful with the water of immortality unto the ages.[^54]

*Let us praise, bless, and worship the Lord. Heirmos:*
*Praise the Lord and exalt Him above all unto all ages, Who was glorified on the holy mountain and by fire in the bush revealed the mystery of the Ever-Virgin unto Moses.*

*Ode 9. Heirmos: "The birthgiving of the Ever-Virgin revealed on the mountain:"*[^53]
