Where the dwelling of Thy joyful Saints is, O Lord: account worthy all who have fallen asleep from the ages in faith and hope to rejoice.

Unto those who died by the divine chastisement, when deadly thunders were brought down from heaven, the earth rent asunder, or the sea surged: give rest, O Christ, unto all the faithful.

Unto every age, elders and youths, infants and children, and sucklings at the breast, male and female nature: give rest, O God, unto the faithful whom Thou hast received.

Unto those who died of venomous bites, swallowed by serpents, trampled by horses, or strangled and hanged by their neighbor: give rest unto those who have served Thee in faith.

Unto each of those who died in faith by name, from the ages and from generation of generations: account them worthy, O Word, to stand uncondemned before Thee at Thy coming.

*Glory, Trinity Hymn:*

*[Margin: O]* O God, one in Trinity, glory be unto Thee unceasingly; for though each is God, yet Father, Son, and Spirit are one in essence by thrice-radiant properties.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*

*[Margin: Y]* Thy birthgiving is beyond the mind; for thou dost give birth unto Him Who was before, and ineffably dost nourish with milk the Nourisher of the world, and thou dost hold Christ, Who holds all things, our only Redeemer, O all-immaculate one.

*Katavasia:*
*The birthgiving of the Ever-Virgin revealed on the mountain unto the Lawgiver in fire and the bush unto our salvation as the faithful, do we magnify with unceasing hymns.*

*Exapostilarion. Model: "The heaven with stars:"*

Ruling over the living and the dead as God: give rest unto Thy servants in the dwellings of the elect; for though they sinned, O Savior, yet they turned not away from Thee.

*Another. Glory. Model: "Give ear, ye women:"*

Give rest unto Thy servants in the land of the living, O Lord, whence sickness, sorrow, and sighing have fled away; cleanse whatsoever they sinned in this life, as Thou art the Lover of mankind; for Thou alone art sinless and the merciful Master of the dead and the living.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*

O Mary, Bride of God, unceasingly entreat Christ on behalf of us thy servants, together with the divinely-speaking Prophets, the assemblies of Martyrs, Hierarchs, and Venerable ones, and all the Righteous, that we may be fellow-heirs of the heavenly kingdom.

*At the Praises, 4 Stichera, Tone 8. Model: "Paradise in Eden:"*

Come before the end, all ye brethren, beholding our dust and the weakness of our nature, and let us see our wretchedness and end, and the organs of the bodily vessel, and that man is dust, food for worms and corruption, that our dry bones have no breath whatsoever. Let us look into the graves: Where is glory? Where is the beauty of form? Where is the eloquent tongue? Where are the eyebrows? Or where is the eye? All are dust and shadow; therefore spare us all, O Savior.

Why is man deceived in boasting? Why does he disturb himself, being himself clay for a little while? Why does the dust not consider that it is dirt, commingling, and an offcasting of corruption and rot? If, then, we men are clay, why have we cleaved unto the earth? And if we are akin to Christ, why do we not run unto Him, and casting away all this temporal and fleeting life, follow the incorruptible life, which is Christ, the illumination of our souls?

O Savior Who with Thy hand didst fashion Adam and set the boundary of incorruption and mortality, and didst likewise alter life unto grace, translating him unto the first life: do Thou Thyself, O Master, give rest with the righteous and in the choir of the elect unto Thy servants whom Thou hast received from us; and having written their names in the book of life, and having raised them up at the Archangel's voice and the sound of the trumpet, account them worthy of Thy heavenly kingdom.

Christ is risen, having loosed the bonds of Adam the first-formed and destroyed the strength of Hades! Take courage, all ye dead: death is put to death, Hades is taken captive along with it, and Christ has reigned, Who was crucified and is risen! He has granted us incorruption of the flesh, He raises us up, and grants resurrection unto us, and with rejoicing accounts all worthy of that glory, who with steadfast faith have fervently believed in Him.

*Glory, Tone 2. For the Departed:*[^55]

As a flower fades, and as a shadow passes by, so every man is dissolved; but when the trumpet sounds again, all the dead shall rise as in an earthquake to meet Thee, O Christ God: then, O Master, establish the spirits of Thy servants in the dwellings of Thy Saints, O Master, who have passed away from us, forever.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*

Rejoice, O Mary Theotokos, indissoluble temple, or rather most holy, as the Prophet cries out: "Thy temple is holy, wonderful in righteousness."[^56]

*At the Aposticha, prosomoia stichera of Theophanes of the Octoechos according to the Tone.*[^57]

*Glory, Tone 6. By Damascene:*

Grief came unto Adam of old in Eden by the tasting of the tree, when the serpent vomited out venom; for thereby entered death upon all mankind, devouring man. But the Master came and cast down the serpent, and granted us rest; unto Him therefore let us cry out: Spare, O Savior, and give rest with Thine elect unto those whom Thou hast received.

*Now and ever, Theotokion, the same Tone:*

Thou art our God, Who dost make and accomplish all things in wisdom; Thou didst send Prophets, O Christ, to foretell Thy coming, and Apostles, to proclaim Thy marvelous deeds; and some indeed foretold Thy coming, while others illuminated the nations through baptism; and the Martyrs, having suffered, received what they desired; and the choir of both, with her that gave Thee birth, entreats Thee: Give rest, O God, unto the souls whom Thou hast received, and account us worthy of Thy kingdom, O Thou Who didst endure the Cross for my sake who was condemned, my Redeemer and God.

*It is good to give praise. Trisagion. Troparion: "With depth of wisdom." Glory, now and ever: "Thee we have as a wall." We also join the First Hour. And the Dismissal.*

*At the Liturgy, the Typika; and from the Canon of the Triodion, Odes 3 and 6.*

*Prokeimenon of the Apostle, Tone 6:* Their souls shall dwell amid good things.
*Verse:* Unto Thee, O Lord, have I lifted up my soul.
*The Epistle to the Corinthians, Pericope 141; another for the reposed, to the Thessalonians, Pericope 270. Alleluia, Tone 6:*
Blessed are they whom Thou hast chosen and taken, O Lord. *Verse:* And their remembrance is from generation to generation.
*The Gospel from Luke, Pericope 105; another for the reposed, from John, Pericope 16.*
*Communion Hymn:* Blessed are they whom Thou hast chosen and taken, O Lord, and their remembrance is from generation to generation.[^58]

*Be it known that this order is performed without change also on the Saturday of Holy Pentecost.*[^59]

## SUNDAY OF MEATFARE

*On Saturday evening, at Vespers, after the Introductory Psalm, the customary kathisma psalmody.*

*At "Lord, I have cried," we set 10 verses. And we chant 3 Resurrectional stichera of the Octoechos, and 3 Anatolian; and 4 prosomoia of the Triodion for the day, Tone 6:*[^60]

*[Margin: Anatolian]*
*Model: "Having set aside all:"*

When Thou shalt come to execute righteous judgment, O most righteous Judge, seated upon the throne of Thy glory, a river of fire drags all before Thy dread judgment seat, the heavenly Hosts standing before Thee, and men being judged with fear according to what each has done: then spare us, and account us worthy of the portion of those who are saved, O Christ, forasmuch as Thou art tender-hearted, we pray Thee in faith.

The books shall be opened, the deeds of men shall be revealed before the unendurable judgment seat; and the whole valley shall resound with the dread gnashing of weeping, as it beholds all who have sinned being sent away unto eternal torments by Thy righteous judgment, weeping unprofitably, O Merciful One: therefore we pray Thee, O Good One: spare us who praise Thee, O Thou Who alone art abundant in mercy.[^61]

The trumpets shall sound, the tombs shall be emptied, and all human nature shall rise up trembling; they that have done good rejoice with joy, expecting to receive their reward; while they that have sinned tremble, bitterly lamenting, being sent unto torment and separated from the elect. O Lord of glory, have compassion on us as Thou art good, and account us worthy of the portion of those who have loved Thee.

I weep and lament when I perceive the eternal fire, the outer darkness, and Tartarus, the cruel worm, and again the gnashing of teeth and unceasing agony that is to come upon those who have sinned beyond measure, and who have provoked Thee, the all-good One, by evil ways, of whom I, wretched one, am one and the first: but O Judge, save me by Thy mercy, as Thou art tender-hearted.[^62]

*Glory, Tone 8:*

When the thrones are set up, and the books are opened, and God sits in judgment, oh, what fear shall there be then, while the Angels stand by in dread, and the river of fire draws near! What shall we do then, men guilty of many sins, when we hear Him calling the blessed of the Father unto the kingdom, but sending sinners unto torment? Who shall endure that dread sentence? But O only Lover of mankind, Savior, King of the ages, before the end draws near, turn me in repentance and have mercy on me.

*Now and ever, Theotokion, the first of the Tone.*

*Entrance. O Gladsome Light. Prokeimenon: "The Lord is King." And the rest.*

*At the Litiya, Glory, idiomelon, Tone 7:*

Having understood the commandments of the Lord, let us live thus: let us feed the hungry, let us give drink to the thirsty, let us clothe the naked, let us bring in the stranger, let us visit the sick and those in prison, that He Who is to judge all the earth may say also unto us: "Come, ye blessed of My Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you."[^63]

*Now and ever:*

Fleeing under thy protection, O Sovereign Lady, all we earthborn cry out unto thee: O Theotokos, our hope, deliver us from immeasurable transgressions, and save our souls.

*At the Aposticha, stichera of the Octoechos in alphabetical order.*

*Glory, Tone 8:*

Woe is me, O darkened soul! How long wilt thou not desist from evil? How long wilt thou lie in despondency? Why dost thou not ponder the dread hour of death? Why dost thou not tremble throughout at the dread judgment seat of the Savior? What, then, wilt thou, O sinner, answer, or what wilt thou say? Thy deeds stand ready to convict thee, thine actions accuse thee as accusers! The time has now arrived, O soul: run, make haste, cry aloud in faith: "I have sinned, O Lord, I have sinned against Thee; but I know Thy tender mercy, O Lover of mankind, Good Shepherd: do not separate me from standing at Thy right hand, for the sake of Thy great mercy."

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*

*Unwedded Virgin:*

*Dismissal Troparion: "Virgin Theotokos, rejoice:" three times. And the rest of the order of the Vigil. And there is a reading from the Acts of the Apostles.*

*At Matins, "God is the Lord," in the Tone of the troparion of the Octoechos. The Resurrectional Troparion, and the Theotokion, and the customary kathisma psalmody. We also read the Homily of the Theologian on Love for the Poor, in three sections, the beginning of which is: "Men and brethren, and fellow-poor:"[^64] And the Polyeleos. The Gradual Hymns of the Tone. The Prokeimenon, and the regular Matins Gospel. Psalm 50. Glory, Tone 8: "Open unto me the doors of repentance:" Now and ever, Theotokion. Model: "Guide me on the paths of salvation:" fol. 2.[^65] Then, Tone 6: "Have mercy on me, O God: When I ponder the multitude of evil deeds I have done:" And the Canons: Resurrectional, and Cross-Resurrectional to 6; and the Triodion to 8.*

*Canon, the composition of lord Theodore the Studite.*[^66]

*Ode 1, Tone 6. Heirmos:*
*He was a helper and protector unto my salvation; He is my God, and I will glorify Him; my father's God, and I will exalt Him; for He is gloriously glorified.*

Pondering the dread day of Thine ineffable coming, I am seized with dread; trembling, I foresee that day wherein Thou shalt sit in judgment over the living and the dead, O my all-powerful God.

When Thou shalt come, O God, amid myriads and thousands of Angelic heavenly ranks: account me, wretched one, worthy to meet Thee in the clouds, O Christ.[^67]

Come, take heed, O my soul, unto that hour and day when God shall visibly appear; and weep, lament, that thou mayest be found pure at the hour of examination.

The unquenchable fire of Gehenna terrifies and frightens me, the bitter worm, the gnashing of teeth: but loose me, forgive me, and rank me, O Christ, in the standing of Thine elect.

May I, wretched one, also hear Thy longed-for voice that calls Thy Saints unto joy, and may I find the ineffable enjoyment of the heavenly kingdom.

Enter not into judgment with me, bringing forth my deeds, examining words, and trying impulses: but overlooking my cruel sins in Thy compassions, save me, O All-powerful One.

*Glory, Trinity Hymn:*

Tri-hypostatic Unity, sovereign Ruler of all, primordial Origin of supreme perfection: do Thou Thyself save us: Father, and Son, and most Holy Spirit.[^68]

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*

Who has ever given birth to a son without the sowing of fatherly laws? Yet the Father begat Him without a mother; O most glorious marvel! For thou, O pure one, didst give birth to God and man together.

*Katavasia: "He was a helper and protector:"*

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
*Establish, O Lord, upon the rock of Thy commandments my shaken heart, for Thou alone art holy and the Lord.*

The Lord comes, and who shall endure His dread presence?[^69] Who shall appear before His face? But be ready, O my soul, to meet Him!

Let us run before with weeping, let us be reconciled unto God before the end; for dread is the judgment seat where we shall all stand bare.

Have mercy, O Lord, have mercy on me, I cry unto Thee, when Thou shalt come with Thine Angels to render unto all according to the worth of their deeds.

How shall I endure the unendurable wrath of Thy judgment, O Lord, having disobeyed Thy commandment? But spare, spare me in the hour of judgment.

Turn, sigh, O wretched soul, before the festival of this life comes to an end, before the Lord shuts the door of the bridal chamber.[^70]

I have sinned, O Lord, as no other among men has sinned, having transgressed beyond measure; before the judgment be merciful unto me, O Lover of mankind.

*Glory, Trinity Hymn:*

O simple, uncreated Trinity, unoriginate Nature praised in a Trinity of Hypostases: save us who in faith bow down before Thy dominion.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*

Thou hast budded forth, O all-pure one, through seedless birthgiving the living Word, Who became incarnate in thy womb without change: glory, O Mother of God, unto thy birthgiving.

*Katavasia: "Establish, O Lord:"*

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 6:*

I ponder the dread day, and I weep over my evil deeds: how shall I answer the immortal King? With what boldness shall I, prodigal one, look upon the Judge? O compassionate Father, only-begotten Son, Holy Spirit, have mercy on me.

*Glory:*

In the valley of weeping, in the place which Thou hast appointed, when Thou shalt sit, O Merciful One, to execute righteous judgment:[^71] reveal not my secret sins, neither put me to shame before the Angels: but spare me, O God, and have mercy on me.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*

O good Virgin Theotokos, hope of the world, I pray for thine only and dread intercession: have compassion upon a people in distress and trial;[^72] entreat the merciful God that our souls may be delivered from all wrath, O thou who alone art blessed.

*Ode 4. Heirmos: "The Prophet heard:"*

The day is at hand, the judgment is already at the doors: watch, O soul, where kings and princes, rich and poor are gathered together, and each man shall receive according to the worth of what he has done.

In his own rank, monk and hierarch, old and young, slave and master shall be examined; widow and virgin shall be scrutinized: and woe unto all then who have not lived a blameless life!

Thy judgment is unconstrained, Thy judgment seat is unbribed by eloquence, no skill of rhetoricians can steal away justice, no false testimony can overturn what is right; for before Thee, the God of all, all secret things stand revealed.

May I not go into the land of weeping, may I not see the place of darkness, O my Christ, the Word! Neither let me be bound hand and foot and cast outside Thy bridal chamber, I who, all-wretched, have defiled the garment of incorruption.[^73]

When Thou shalt separate the sinners from the righteous, judging the world: number me, O Lover of mankind, among Thy sheep, parting me from the goats, that I may hear that blessed voice of Thine.[^74]

When the examination takes place, and the books of deeds are opened: what wilt thou do, O wretched soul, as a sinner? What wilt thou answer at the judgment seat, having no fruits of righteousness to offer unto Christ and thy Creator?

Hearing the rich man weeping in the flame of torment, I weep and lament, wretched one, being subject unto the same condemnation, and I pray: Have mercy on me, O Savior of the world, in the time of judgment.[^75]

*Glory, Trinity Hymn:*

I glorify the Son from the Father and the Spirit, as light and ray from the sun: the One indeed by way of begetting, for He is the Begotten, and the Other by way of procession, for He is the Proceeding, the co-unoriginate divine Trinity, worshipped by all creation.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*

O Virgin who didst give birth to an Infant and preserved thy purity, thou hast been revealed, O pure one, having given birth unto God and man, the One same Person in two forms: thy marvel, O Virgin Mother, strikes with awe every ear and mind.[^76]

*Katavasia:*
*The Prophet heard of Thy coming, O Lord, and was afraid, that Thou wast to be born of a Virgin and appear unto men, and he said: "I have heard report of Thee and was afraid: glory to Thy power, O Lord."*

*Ode 5. Heirmos: "Rising early from the night:"*

There is ineffable trembling and fear there; for the Lord comes, and each man's deed with Him: and who henceforth will not weep for himself?

The river of fire disturbs me and consumes me; the gnashing of teeth scrapes me, and the darkness of the abyss: and how, or by doing what, shall I appease God?

Spare, spare Thy servant, O Lord, lest Thou ever deliver me unto bitter tormentors, the cruel angels, among whom there is no finding rest.

Prince and commander together, rich and ignoble, great and small alike shall be examined there: woe henceforth unto everyone who is unprepared!

Remit, forgive, O Lord, and pardon whatsoever I have sinned against Thee, and show me not there before the Angels unto the condemnation of fire and unending shame.

Spare, spare Thy creature, O Lord; I have sinned, forgive me: for Thou alone art pure by nature, and none other besides Thee is without defilement.

*Glory, Trinity Hymn:*

I praise Thee as a Unity in essence, O Trinity: unoriginate, incomprehensible, sovereign, royal, most perfect Unity, God and Light and Life, and Creator of the world.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*

In thy birthgiving beyond nature, O pure one, the laws of nature were clearly dissolved for thee; for without seed thou dost give birth unto the eternal God, begotten of the Father.

*Katavasia:*
*Do Thou Who art the Lover of mankind enlighten me who rise early from the night, I pray Thee, and guide me in Thy commandments, and teach me, O Savior, to do Thy will.*

*Ode 6. Heirmos: "I cried with all my heart:"*

At Thy dread coming, O Christ, when Thou shalt appear from heaven, and the thrones shall be set up, and the books opened: spare, spare Thy creature then, O Savior.

Nothing can help there when God is the Judge: neither diligence, nor crafts, nor glory, nor friendship: except the strength that comes from thy deeds, O my soul!

There prince and leader, poor and rich together, O soul: neither father can help, nor mother assist, nor brother deliver from condemnation.

Pondering the dread examination of the judgment seat, O soul, be terrified henceforth; prepare thy defense, that thou mayest not be condemned unto eternal bonds.

May I, Thy servant, not hear Thee say, O Lord: "Take what is thine," as I am sent away from Thee; neither: "Depart into the cursed fire"; but rather may I hear the longed-for voice of the righteous.

Deliver me, O Lord, from the gates of Hades, from the abyss and lightless darkness, from the nethermost parts and unquenchable fire, and from all other eternal torments.

*Glory, Trinity Hymn:*

I praise the Godhead of the Trinitarian Unity: Father, Son, and divine Spirit, the dominion of one Principle, distinguished by three characters.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*

Thou art the gate through which alone entered and went forth Jesus, Who fashioned Adam and is thy Son, without breaking the seals of virginity, O pure one.[^77]

*Katavasia:*
*I cried with all my heart unto the merciful God, and He gave ear unto me from nethermost Hades, and brought up my life from corruption.*

*Kontakion, Tone 1:*
When Thou shalt come, O God, upon earth with glory, and all things tremble, and the river of fire flows before the judgment seat, the books are opened, and secret things are made manifest: then deliver me from the unquenchable fire, and account me worthy to stand at Thy right hand, O most righteous Judge.

*Ikos:*
Pondering Thy dread judgment seat, O all-good Lord, and the Day of Judgment, I am terrified and afraid, convicted by my conscience, when Thou shalt sit upon Thy throne and make examination: then no one will be able to deny sins, truth convicting and fear holding fast; then the fire of Gehenna shall roar greatly, and sinners shall gnash their teeth: therefore have mercy on me before the end, and spare me, O most righteous Judge.

*Synaxarion. Verses:*
When Thou, the Judge of all, shalt sit to judge the earth:
Judge me worthy also to hear that voice: "Come!"

On this day we make commemoration of the Second and Incorrupt Coming of Christ,[^78] which the most divine Fathers appointed after the two parables, lest anyone, learning of God's love for mankind in them, should live negligently, saying: "God is the Lover of mankind, and whenever I turn away from sin, I have all things ready to be fulfilled." They appointed this dread day here, so that by terrifying the negligent with death and the expectation of future evils, they might lead them back unto virtue, not relying solely on His love for mankind, but also beholding that the Judge is righteous, and renders unto each according to his works. In another way, after the departed souls, it was fitting that the Judge should come: and the present feast is a certain type, because the end of all feasts is set today, even as it shall itself be our final end. For it is fitting to observe that on the coming Sunday they will set the beginning of the world and the very fall of Adam from Paradise, while the present day is the end of all days and of the world itself. They placed it during Meatfare, curtailing, I think, food and gluttony for the sake of the awe of the feast, and summoning us unto mercy toward our neighbor. And in another way: since through feeding we were cast out of Eden, and came under judgment and curse, for this reason they placed the present feast here; and because on the next Sunday we are to be cast out with Adam after the pattern of Eden, until Christ, having come, shall lead us back into Paradise. It is called the "Second Coming," because He first came to us in the flesh, but quietly and without glory; but now He will come with supernatural wonders and manifest radiance from the heavens, and with a body, that He may be recognized by all: that this is He Who also came at first and redeemed our race, and Who will Himself judge whether they kept well what was given them. When this coming will take place, no one knows; for this the Lord concealed even from the Apostles. Certain signs, however, will precede it, which some of the Saints have explained at greater length. Before His coming, the Antichrist will come, and he will be born, as Saint Hippolytus of Rome says, of a polluted woman and supposed virgin, from among the Jews of the tribe of Dan, who was the servant of Jacob;[^79] and he will live in imitation of Christ, and perform miracles such as Christ worked, and will raise the dead. Yet all these he will do in delusion: both his birth, and his flesh, and all the rest, as the Apostle says. And then, he says, the son of perdition will be revealed in all power, signs, and lying wonders. Yet the devil himself will not be transformed into flesh, as John of Damascus says; but a man born of fornication will receive all Satan's working, and will arise suddenly, and then show himself good and gentle unto all. And there will be a great famine then: he will please men, study the divine Scriptures, and practice fasting; and he will be compelled by men and proclaimed king; and he will love the Jewish race exceedingly, arrive in Jerusalem, and rebuild their temple. Enoch and Elijah will come, preaching unto the people not to receive him: but he will openly kill them and cut off their heads. He will give abundant freedom to those found doing mad deeds, who will hide in the mountains; yet those days will be shortened for the sake of the elect, and there will be a great famine, all the elements being transformed, so that almost all will be consumed. After these things, suddenly, like lightning from heaven, the coming of the Lord will take place, His precious Cross going before Him, and a river of fire boiling before Him, cleansing the whole earth from defilement. The Antichrist will immediately be seized, and his servants, and they will be delivered unto eternal fire. And when the Angels sound the trumpet, suddenly from the end of the earth and from every element, all the human race will come unto Jerusalem, because it is the center of the earth, and there the thrones will sit for judgment: nevertheless with their own bodies and souls, all having passed over unto incorruption, and having one appearance, and the elements having received a transformation for the better.[^80] And with a single word the Lord will separate the righteous from the sinners. And the doers of good will go, receiving eternal life; but the sinners again unto eternal torment, and never will their end be. It is to be known that Christ will not require fasting then, nor nakedness, nor wonders, though these also are good: but what is many times better than these: alms and simplicity of heart. For He will speak unto the righteous and the sinners six commandments: "For I was hungry, and ye gave Me food; I was thirsty, and ye gave Me drink; I was a stranger, and ye took Me in; naked, and ye clothed Me; I was sick, and ye visited Me; I was in prison, and ye came unto Me; for forasmuch as ye did it unto one of the least of these, ye did it unto Me": which everyone can do according to his strength.[^81] Then everyone will confess that the Lord Jesus Christ is to the glory of God the Father.[^82] The torments which the holy Gospel has handed down are these: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth, their worm shall not die, and their fire shall not be quenched, and cast him into outer darkness.[^83]
*[Margin: compassion]*
*[Margin: pleasures]*
Which things the Church of God having received in every way does not consider that delight and the kingdom are one thing, but rather to be with God in the dwelling of the Saints, who behold that unceasing radiance and ascension. And torment and darkness and suchlike, to be estrangement from God, and the souls being scorched by conscience, seeing how through negligence and temporary pleasure they were deprived of divine glory. Through Thine ineffable love for mankind, O Christ God, account us worthy of Thy longed-for voice, and number us with those at Thy right hand, and have mercy on us. Amen.

*Ode 7. Heirmos: "We have sinned, we have transgressed:"*

Let us fall down and weep before that judgment, O ye faithful, when the heavens shall perish, the stars fall, and all the earth be shaken, that at the end we may find the God of our fathers merciful.

Unconstrained is the examination, dread is the judgment there, where the Judge cannot be deceived, where there is no accepting of persons for gifts: then spare me, O Master, and deliver me from all Thy dread wrath.

The Lord comes to judge: who shall endure the sight of Him? Tremble, O wretched soul, tremble, and prepare thy deeds for departure, that thou mayest find Him merciful and peaceful, the blessed God of our fathers.

The unquenchable fire disturbs me, the bitterest worm gnaws me, soul-destroying Hades terrifies me, yet I am not moved unto compunction at all: but O Lord, Lord, before the end establish me in Thy fear.

I fall down before Thee, and I offer unto Thee my words as tears: I have sinned as the harlot never sinned, and have committed iniquity as no other upon earth: but have compassion, O Master, upon Thy creature, and call me back.

Turn, O soul, repent, uncover what is secret, speak unto God Who knows all things: "Thou knowest my secrets, O only Savior; but do Thou Thyself have mercy on me, as David sings, according to Thy mercy."[^84]

*Glory, Trinity Hymn:*

Three, one in essence, and one, three in Persons, do I praise these: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, one power, will, and operation, one thrice-holy God, one most sovereign kingdom.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*

The most comely God comes forth from the bridal chamber of thy womb, as a King clothed in a robe woven of mildness, dyed by the secret immersion of thy most pure blood, O Unwedded Bride, and He reigns over the earth.

*Katavasia:*
*We have sinned, we have transgressed, we have done unrighteously before Thee, neither have we kept nor done as Thou hast commanded us: but deliver us not up utterly, O God of our fathers.*[^85]

*Ode 8. Heirmos: "Him Whom the heavenly hosts glorify:"*

Pondering the meeting of Thy dread Second Coming, O Lord, I tremble at Thy threat, I fear Thy wrath: from this hour, I cry: save me unto the ages!

When Thou, O God, shalt judge all things, who among the earthborn shall endure, being subject to passions? For the unquenchable fire then, and the intensely gnawing worm shall receive the condemned unto the ages.

When Thou shalt summon all breath to judge together, O Christ: great fear then, great distress, only deeds being of help unto the ages.

O Judge of all, my God and Lord, may I then hear Thy longed-for voice, may I behold Thy great light, may I see Thy dwellings, may I gaze upon Thy glory, rejoicing unto ages of ages.

O righteous Judge, Savior, have mercy, and deliver me from the fire and the threat which are righteously to be rendered unto me at the judgment: grant me remission before the end, through virtue and repentance.

When Thou shalt sit as Judge, as Thou art tender-hearted, and show forth Thy dread glory, O Christ: oh, what fear will be then, the furnace burning, and all fearing Thine unendurable judgment seat!

*We bless the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit: the Lord.*

*Trinity Hymn:*
I honor one God in essence, I praise three Hypostases distinct in personal definition, but not differing in nature: for the Godhead is one in three Persons: Father, Son, and divine Spirit.[^86]

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*
Having come forth from thy radiant womb, as a bridegroom from his chamber Christ shone forth, a great Light unto those in darkness: as the Sun of righteousness having flashed forth, O Pure One, He enlightened the world.

*We praise, we bless, and we worship the Lord, singing and exalting Him unto all ages.*

*Heirmos:*
*Him Whom the heavenly hosts glorify, and Cherubim and Seraphim tremble before, let every breath and creature sing, bless, and exalt unto all ages.*

*Ode 9. Heirmos: "The conception without seed:"*

The Lord comes to torment sinners, and to save the righteous: let us weep, and let us lament, and let us take heed of that day, wherein having hidden from men what is unsearchable and secret, He will render according to merit.

Moses was filled with awe and trembling when he saw Thee from behind:[^87] how then shall I, wretched one, stand, beholding Thy face then, when Thou shalt come from heaven? But spare me, O Merciful One, by Thy compassionate gaze.

Daniel was afraid of the hour of examination;[^88] and what shall I, wretched one, suffer from it, who am drawing near, O Lord, unto that dread day? But grant me before the end to serve Thee in a manner well-pleasing, and to obtain Thy kingdom.

The fire is prepared, the worm is made ready: gladness, glory, relief, light unwaning, the joy of the righteous; and who is the blessed one that will not desire to escape the torment of the former, and become an heir of the latter?

Let not the fury of Thy wrath turn me away from Thy face, O Lord; neither may I hear the voice of the curse sending me away into the fire; but may I also enter into the joy of Thine incorrupt bridal chamber then with Thy Saints.

The mind is wounded, the body is stricken with sores, the spirit languishes, speech has failed, life is deadened, the end is at the doors: therefore, O my wretched soul, what wilt thou do when the Judge comes to examine thy deeds?

*Glory, Trinity Hymn:*
O Father of the Only-begotten Son, Sole Begetter of the One, and sole Light of the one Light, Radiance of the Light; and sole Holy Spirit of the one God, truly existing Lord of the Lord: O holy Trinity, Unity! Save me who speak in theology of Thee.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*
The wonder of thy childbearing astonishes me, O all-immaculate Virgin; tell me, how dost thou conceive the Incomprehensible without seed, and how, having given birth as a virgin, art thou a Mother? Receiving in faith that which is beyond nature, worship the One born of thee: for whatsoever He wills, He also can do.

*Katavasia:*

*Katavasia:*
*The childbearing of the conception without seed is ineffable, the Fruit of the unwedded Mother is incorrupt: for the birth of God renews natures; therefore all generations, as the Virgin Bride and Mother of God, orthodoxly magnify thee.*

*Exapostilarion. Then the following. Model: "Let us go up with the disciples:"*
Pondering the dread day of judgment, and of Thine ineffable glory, I tremble greatly, O Lord, and shaking with fear I cry aloud: when Thou shalt come upon earth with glory to judge all things, O Christ God, deliver me from all torment, having accounted me worthy to stand at Thy right hand, O Master.

*Glory, Another. Model: "Give ear, ye women:"*
Behold, the day of the Lord Almighty comes, and who shall endure the fear of that coming? For it is a day of wrath, and a burning furnace, wherein the Judge shall sit, and render unto each according to the merit of his deeds.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*
Pondering the hour of examination, and of the dread coming of the Master Who loves mankind, I wholly tremble, and grieving, I cry unto Thee: O my most righteous Judge, and only abundant in mercy, through the prayers of the Mother of God receive me who repent.

*At the Praises, we set 4 Resurrectional stichera of the Octoechos, and 1 Anatolian; and 4 of the Triodion, Tone 6. Idiomela.*
*[Margin: Anatolian]*
*Verse: Praise Him with tuneful cymbals, praise Him with cymbals of jubilation: Let every breath praise the Lord.*

I ponder that day and hour, when we are all to stand naked and as condemned before the unendurable Judge; then the trumpet shall sound mightily, and the foundations of the earth shall be shaken, and the dead shall rise from the graves, and all shall be in one stature,[^89] and the secret things of all shall stand revealed before Thee; and they that never repented shall lament and weep, and shall go into outer fire: while the portion of the righteous shall enter into joy and gladness in the heavenly bridal chamber.

*Verse: I will praise Thee, O Lord, with my whole heart; I will show forth all Thy marvelous works.*

Oh, what an hour then, and a dread day, when the Judge shall sit upon the dread throne! The books are opened, and deeds are convicted, and the secret things of darkness are made manifest; Angels run about, gathering all the nations: come, give ear, ye kings and princes, slaves and free, sinners and righteous, rich and poor: for the Judge comes, intending to judge the whole inhabited earth; and who shall endure before His face, when the Angels stand accusing deeds, thoughts, and intentions, by night and by day? Oh, what an hour then! But before the end draws near, hasten, crying out, O soul: "O God, having turned me back, save me, as Thou alone art tender-hearted."

*Tone 8.*
*Verse: I will be glad and rejoice in Thee: I will sing unto Thy name, O Thou Most High.*

The Prophet Daniel, having been a man of desires,[^90] seeing the sovereign power of God, cried out thus: "The Judge sat, and the books were opened!" Take heed, O my soul: having fasted, despise not thy neighbor; having abstained from foods, condemn not thy brother, lest being sent away into the fire thou burn like wax; but that Christ may lead thee without stumbling into His kingdom.

*Tone 1.*
*Verse: Arise, O Lord my God, let Thy hand be lifted up; forget not Thy poor unto the end.*

Let us pre-purify ourselves, brethren, with the queen of virtues: for behold, she has come, bestowing upon us a wealth of good things: she quells the swellings of the passions, and reconciles transgressors unto the Master; therefore with gladness let us receive her, crying aloud unto Christ God: "O Thou Who didst rise from the dead, preserve us uncondemned, who glorify Thee, the only Sinless One."

*Glory: the same verse again.*

*Now and ever: "Thou art most blessed:" Great Doxology; and the dismissal. Then the customary Litiya in the narthex, wherein we chant: Glory, and now and ever: the Gospel sticheron. We also join the First Hour, in which is read the Catechesis of our venerable father Theodore the Studite.*[^91]

*At the Divine Liturgy, the Typika. And the Beatitudes of the Tone on 6; and from the canon of the Triodion, Ode 6 on 4. Prokeimenon, Tone 3: "Great is our Lord:" Verse: "Praise the Lord, for the psalm is good:" Epistle to the Corinthians, Pericope 140 (1 Cor. 8:8–9:2). Alleluia, Tone 8: "Come, let us rejoice in the Lord, let us shout with jubilation unto God our Savior." Verse: "Let us come before His presence with thanksgiving, and shout with jubilation unto Him with psalms." Gospel from Matthew, Pericope 106 (Matt. 25:31–46). Communion Hymn: "Praise the Lord from the heavens:" Another: "Rejoice in the Lord, O ye righteous:"*

*On Meatfare Sunday evening, at "Lord, I have cried," we chant as customary 3 stichera of the Octoechos, and 3 of the Menaion for the current Saint. Glory, and now and ever: Theotokion. But at the Aposticha the Octoechos is omitted, and we chant the Idiomelon of the day, both choirs together. Tone 8:*

Having yielded unto culinary gluttony, we incurred our first nakedness, overcome by bitter food, and were cast out from God; but let us be led back unto repentance, and let us cleanse our senses, against which is the warfare; making the entrance of the Fast, strengthening our hearts by the hope of grace, not by foods, in which they that walked were not profited; and the Lamb of God shall be eaten by us, in the holy and light-bearing night of the Resurrection, the slaughter brought for our sake, shared with the disciples at the evening of the mystery, and dispelling the darkness of ignorance by the light of His Resurrection.

*Verse: Unto Thee have I lifted up mine eyes, O Thou that dwellest in heaven: behold, as the eyes of servants look unto the hands of their masters, and as the eyes of a maiden unto the hands of her mistress; so our eyes look unto the Lord our God, until He have mercy on us.*

*And again the same idiomelon: "Having yielded unto culinary gluttony:"*

*Verse 2: Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us, for we are exceedingly filled with contempt; our soul is exceedingly filled with the reproach of them that are at ease, and with the contempt of the proud.*

*And we chant the Martyrion to the same Tone:*
O Martyrs of the Lord, ye sanctify every place, and heal every infirmity; and now we pray: entreat that our souls be delivered from the snares of the enemy.

*Glory, and now and ever, Theotokion, the same Tone:*
The heavenly hosts sing praise to thee, O Full of Grace, unwedded Mother; and we glorify thine unsearchable childbearing, O Mother of God: pray that our souls may be saved.

## CHEESEFARE MONDAY

*On Cheesefare Monday at Matins, at "God is the Lord," the Troparion of the Saint twice; Glory, and now and ever, Theotokion, according to the Tone.*

*After the first stichology, sessional hymn of the Octoechos. And we read the Homily of St. Basil the Great, "Take heed to thyself."*

*After the second stichology, we chant of the Triodion, Tone 1. Model: "When the stone had been sealed:"*
The vestibules of divine repentance have been opened: let us approach with zeal, having purified our bodies, making the putting-away of foods and passions, as obedient servants of Christ, Who called the world unto the heavenly kingdom, offering the tithes of the whole year unto the King of all,[^92] that we may also behold His Resurrection in love.

*Glory: the same again. Now and ever, Theotokion:*
Having stretched forth thy divine hands, wherewith thou didst carry the Creator, O most holy Virgin, incarnate in His Divinity: do thou make supplication that we may be delivered from temptations, and passions, and afflictions, who praise thee with love and cry unto thee: Glory to Him Who took abode in thee, glory to Him Who came forth from thee, glory to Him Who set us free by thy childbearing!

*We chant the canons as customary in the Octoechos, and to the Saint in the Menaion. At the end of the odes comes the triodion; if there are two heirmoi, we omit both canons of the Octoechos, and chant the canon in the Menaion with the heirmos on 6, and in the Triodion on 8: the canon of the Menaion, and the present triodion. The work of master Joseph.[^93] Ode 1, Tone 1.*

*Heirmos: "Let us all sing a song of victory unto God:"*
The radiant pre-feasts of abstinence, the radiant dawns of the Fast are today; therefore let us gather together in hope, brethren, and with great zeals.

I rivaled our forefather Adam in transgression, and I, wretched one, was cast out from delight; therefore I fall down before Thee in repentance and weeping: O Lord, save me!

The beginning of compunction and repentance is alienation from evil things and abstinence from passions; therefore let us hasten to make a cutting-off of all evil deeds.

*Theotokion:*
Darkened by the night of transgressions, unto thee who gavest birth unto Christ, the Sun of righteousness, for those in darkness, do I now flee with diligence: O Sovereign Lady, save me!

*Another triodion, the same heirmos.*
Behold, the door of repentance has opened beforehand, O lovers of God: come, then, let us hasten to enter through it, before Christ shuts it against us as being unworthy.

Announcing the prize, this present all-honorable pre-purifying week of the sacred fasts has drawn near,[^94] illuminating the bodies and souls of all.

*Glory, Trinity Hymn:*
Unconfused, uncreated, holy Trinity, all-good Unity, Father, Son, and consubstantial Spirit: save evermore those who faithfully worship Thee.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*
The bounds of nature were overcome in thee, O all-honorable Virgin: for having given birth unto God without a man, as thou wast pure before childbearing, thou remainest again uninjured.

*Then the Heirmos:*
*Let us all sing a song of victory unto God, Who worked marvelous wonders with an exalted arm, and saved Israel, for He has been glorified.*

*After Ode 3, sessional hymn: Glory, and now and ever, Theotokion. After Ode 6, Kontakion and Ikos of the Saint.*

*Ode 8. Heirmos: "Him before Whom the Angels tremble:"*
I squandered my entire life prodigally, I was in bitter and evil servitude to citizen-passions: but despise me not, O Christ, who desire now to turn back unto Thy compassions.

The ways of my life are shameful and grievous: do Thou, O Savior, Lover of mankind, grant the unbegrudging mercy of Thy tender-heartedness and the time of repentance unto me who ask and who sing praise to Thee in love.

I rivaled the wretched life of Cain, having truly put my soul to death in merit, and I tremble before Thy judgment, O Benefactor: condemn me not with these unto ages of ages.

*Theotokion:*
O all-immaculate Virgin, who art the firm help of the faithful unto God: deliver me from darkness, and from the impending torment of those who live wickedly.

*Another. Heirmos: "A hymn we offer unto Thee:"*
This is the time of repentance, therefore let us begin with good wisdom, brethren, crying aloud: "Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!"

Having renounced foods today, let us hasten by deed and worthily to repent of transgressions: "Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!"

*We bless the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit: the Lord. Trinity Hymn:*
Glory to Thee, O invisible holy Trinity, worshiped in Unity, Whom we faithfully glorify: save Thy servants from every harm!

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*
Rejoice, all-immaculate, pure Virgin; rejoice, handmaid of the Lord and Mother; rejoice, protection of the world, blessed Mother of God, Mary all-radiant!

*We praise, we bless, and we worship the Lord: Heirmos:*
*A hymn of the bodiless hosts we offer unto Thee, as the youths in the furnace, and singing we say: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!*

*Ode 9. Heirmos: "A light-bearing cloud:"*
With peaceful constancy, in pure love, let us faithful receive the most sacred season of the holy Fast, asking forgiveness for wherein each has sinned, that we may obtain the joy that is yonder.

Behold, the season of repentance, this pre-festal entrance of the fasts: arise, O my soul, be warmly reconciled unto the Benefactor and God, that thou mayest truly escape that righteous and dread judgment.

Let us not evilly defile the entrances and vestibules of the fasts with intemperance and drunkenness; but let us zealously enter unto purity of thoughts, receiving crowns of incorruption, and the fruits of labors worthily.

*Theotokion:*
Cease not to pray for us unto the Good One, Who alone knows our infirmity: that the city which honors thee may be delivered from famine, and pestilence, and earthquake, and every affliction, O Mother of God, the hope of the earthborn.

*Another. Heirmos: "The door seen by Ezekiel:"*
The season of repentance has been introduced, O my soul: be not negligent; give bread unto the hungry, pray unto the Lord on every day, and night, and hour, that He may save thee.

As we made an abstaining from meats and other foods, so let us likewise flee from all enmity toward neighbors, from fornication and falsehood, and from all malice.

*Glory, Trinity Hymn:*
I worship the one unoriginate Godhead in nature, and in three Persons I glorify the indivisible and co-enthroned Unity in Trinity.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*
Thou art the boast of the faithful, O Virgin, their hope and protection: with songs we who are mute glorify thee unceasingly, O Mother of God Mary: save thy servants!

*Heirmos:*
*The door seen by Ezekiel the Prophet, through which no one passed save God alone,[^95] do we honor in songs, O Virgin Mother of God.*

*Exapostilarion of the Octoechos: Glory, to the Saint, if there be one. If not: Glory, and now and ever, Theotokion.*

*At the Aposticha, Idiomelon sticheron, Tone 3:*
At all times fasting is profitable unto those who choose it and practice it: for neither does demonic temptation dare to assault the one who fasts, but the Angels, the guardians of our life, dwell more diligently with us who have purified ourselves by fasting.[^96]

*Verse: We were filled in the morning with Thy mercy, O Lord, and we rejoiced and were glad: in all our days we were glad, for the days wherein Thou didst humble us, for the years wherein we saw evil things; and look upon Thy servants, and upon Thy works, and guide their sons.*

*And we chant the same sticheron again.*

*Verse: And let the brightness of the Lord our God be upon us, and prosper Thou the works of our hands upon us, yea, the work of our hands do Thou prosper.*

*Martyrion:*
Come, all ye people, let us honor the memory of the holy Passion-bearers: for having become a spectacle unto Angels and men, they received crowns of victory from Christ, and they pray for our souls.

*Glory, and now and ever, Theotokion, the same Tone:*
Without seed thou didst conceive of the Holy Spirit, and glorifying, we sing praise unto thee: Rejoice, all-holy Virgin!

*Be it known that on Monday of Cheesefare Week we eat twice in the day.*[^97]

*On Cheesefare Monday evening, at "Lord, I have cried," stichera as customary. At the Aposticha, the idiomelon twice, Tone 8:*
Let us hasten to purify ourselves by fasting from the defilement of our transgressions, and through mercy and love for mankind toward the poor, to enter into the bridal chamber of Christ the Bridegroom, Who grants us great mercy.

*And we say the customary verses, as yesterday. Martyrion:*
O Martyrs of the Lord, pray unto our God, and ask for our souls a multitude of compassions, and purification from many transgressions, we pray.

*Glory, and now and ever, Theotokion:*
Let us piously sing praise unto the most glorious and most pure Mother of God, as the true Mother of God, saying unto her as the Angel: Rejoice, holy Mother of the incarnate Son of God; rejoice, dwelling-place of the Holy Spirit, who prayest unceasingly for us, that our souls may be saved.

*And the rest of the sequence.*

## CHEESEFARE TUESDAY

*On Cheesefare Tuesday at Matins. After the second stichology, sessional hymn, Tone 8. Model: "Of wisdom and the Word:"*
O all-good Word, Who with the Father and the Spirit didst create things visible together with things invisible, by Thine ineffable mercy, O Tender-hearted One, be pleased that Thy servants pass through the season of the radiant Fast in peace, dissolving the deception of bitter sin, granting compunction, and tears of healing, and forgiveness of transgressions, so that with an undoubting soul, fasting with a fervent spirit, we may sing praise with the Angels unto Thy sovereign power. Glory: the same. Now and ever, Theotokion:

Having ineffably conceived Wisdom and the Word in thy womb, O Mother of God, thou didst give birth unto Him Who holds the world, and in thine arms didst hold Him Who embraces all, the Nourisher of all and Creator and Lord; therefore I pray thee, O all-hymned Virgin, and in faith I glorify thee, that I may be delivered from my transgressions when I am to stand before the face of my Creator, O Sovereign Lady, pure Virgin; do thou grant me thy help then: for thou canst do whatsoever thou wilt, O All-immaculate One.

*And we read the Homily of St. Basil the Great on Thanksgiving.[^98] Then Psalm 50. We chant the canons of the Octoechos and the Menaion as was indicated on Monday, leaf 30: likewise follow in the rest. And the triodion of master Joseph.*

*Ode 2, Tone 2. Heirmos:*
*As the rain upon the grass, and as snow upon the hay, so let my words descend upon the earth.*

As the morning dawn has shone forth upon us, the rays of repentance, the vestibules of radiant abstinence.

Deliver me, O Christ, from the burning of darkness, by the multitude of Thy mercy, as Thou art alone merciful.

Snatch me from the fire, O Savior, and from the sleepless worm, being cleansed by diligence in repentance.

*Theotokion:*
O all-pure Virgin, be thou for us the way of repentance, leading unto the doors of salvation.

*Another. Heirmos, Tone 2: "Give ear, O my people:"*
The season of repentance has arrived: let us hasten, O lovers of Christ, to purify ourselves from all transgressions, and appear blessed unto the Master.

Let us hasten to accomplish a pure, sinless fast unceasingly now, that we may find forgiveness of transgressions.

For Thou, O God of all, art abundant in mercy, O Christ, ever receiving unto repentance; therefore we all ever glorify Thee.

*Glory, Trinity Hymn:*
Let us glorify the Trinity in Unity: unsevered, unconfused, undivided in essence, yet divided in Persons: God.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*
O pure Virgin Mother, entreat the Word Whom thou didst incarnate as man, O Virgin, that He may save thy servants from afflictions.

*Heirmos:*
*Give ear, O my people, unto my law: incline your ear unto the words of my mouth: for I called upon Thy name, O Lord.*

*Ode 8. Heirmos: "Begotten of the unoriginate Father:"*
It is the season of remorse: hasten, O my soul, arise, to show forth fruits of repentance worthy of God, and cry aloud with diligence in fastings and prayers: "Sing, bless, and exalt Christ unto all ages!"

Let us pre-purify our spiritual senses, brethren, and let us now cleave unto the Lord with images of compunction, crying out purely with pure repentance: "Sing, bless, and exalt Christ unto all ages!"

Let us hasten by diligent prayer to put to death the snaring enemy who through gluttonous memories and intemperance inflames the sense with brief pleasure, singing, blessing, and exalting Christ unto all ages.

*Theotokion:*
O Maiden who didst make heavenly our earthly substance, by the showers of thy compassions show forth the furrow of my soul, which has grown evil and barren, to be fruitful in virtues as it cries out and exalts Christ unto all ages.

*Another. Heirmos: "In the bush unto Moses:"*
Let us pre-purify ourselves now not with foods alone, but also with deeds, and let us faithful begin with fervent contemplation: that we may appear radiant unto the Creator unto all ages.

In this manner it is fitting for us to fast: not in enmity and strife, not in envy and contention, not in vainglory and hidden deceit, but as Christ did, in humility of mind.

"They that show mercy unto the poor," He said, "lend unto the Savior wisely."[^99] Oh, incomprehensible joy! For He richly bestows rewards of good things unto all ages.

*We bless the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit: the Lord. Trinity Hymn:*
Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit: One among Gods, Three, with the Angels do we men unceasingly praise Thee, O all-holy Trinity, unto all ages.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*
Rejoice, pure Virgin, Mother of God Mary, cleansing-place of the world, horn of the Orthodox: pray that they who glorify thee may be delivered from unquenchable fire unto all ages.

*We praise, we bless, and we worship the Lord: Heirmos:*
*Unto Him Who prefigured the wonder of the Virgin unto Moses in the bush on Mount Sinai of old,[^100] sing, bless, and exalt Him unto all ages.*

*Ode 9. Heirmos: "Thee, the unburnt bush:"*
Open unto us the all-pure bowels of Thy mercy, O Thou Who didst grant repentance unto men for salvation, O only Savior abundant in mercy.

Woe is me, what a dread, that unendurable judgment seat, whereon we are to give an account naked of the things we did evilly in life!

Rain down upon us, O Benefactor, a drop of tender-heartedness that drowns all our defilement, granting us causes of repentance.

Having all gathered together radiantly with a fervent heart at the vestibules of the holy Fast, let us offer thanksgiving songs unto Christ.

*Theotokion:*
Piously singing praise unto thee, the mighty protection and sure hope, we pray: entreat thy Son, O Virgin, that we may be saved.

*Another. Heirmos: "Thy virginity, O immaculate Mother of God:"*
Now let us pre-purify ourselves in fasting and tears, and in cell-corrections, that we may find great mercy.

Now let us imitate the wise virgins, O lovers of Christ, and hasten to meet Christ with radiant lamps.

Now let us imitate Elijah who fasted and fled from wicked Jezebel, that we may thus be lifted up from the earth.

*Glory, Trinity Hymn:*
Holy, Holy, Holy, Thrice-holy, Father Almighty, and Son consubstantial with the Spirit: one Godhead.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*
In thee do we boast, and unto thee do we flee, O Pure One, ever-virgin, all-honorable: deliver us all from torment.

*Heirmos:*
*Thy virginity, O immaculate Mother of God, which the divine fire did not burn, do we magnify.*

*At the Aposticha, Idiomelon sticheron, Tone 3:*
Lovingly, O ye people, let us embrace the Fast: for the beginning of spiritual struggles has arrived: let us leave bodily voluptuousness, let us increase spiritual gifts; let us suffer together as servants of Christ, that we may also be glorified together as children of God; and the Holy Spirit, having taken abode in us, shall enlighten our souls.

*Verse: We were filled in the morning with Thy mercy: The same sticheron again.*

*Verse: And let the brightness: Martyrion:*
The warriors of Christ rejected the fear of kings and torturers, and boldly and courageously confessed Him, the Lord God and King of all; and they pray for our souls.

*Glory, and now and ever, Theotokion:*
O Mother of God, protection of all who pray, in thee do we trust, and in thee do we boast, in thee is all our hope: pray unto Him Who was born of thee for thine unprofitable servants.

*On Cheesefare Tuesday evening, from the beginning of Vespers we begin the prostrations.[^102] At "Lord, I have cried," stichera as customary.*

*At the Aposticha, Idiomelon, Tone 1:*
Joyfully let us faithful receive the God-inspired injunction of the Fast, even as the Ninevites did of old; and again, the harlots and publicans,[^101] which is the preaching of repentance from John; through abstinence let us prepare ourselves for migration into the Zion of eternal sacred ministry, with tears let us pre-purify ourselves for the divine washing therein, let us pray to behold here in figure the fulfillment of Pascha, and the manifestation of the truth; let us prepare ourselves for the adoration of the Cross and the Resurrection of Christ God, crying out unto Him: Put us not to shame from our expectation, O Lover of mankind!

*Verse: Unto Thee have I lifted up mine eyes: And the same sticheron again.*

*Verse: Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us: Martyrion:*
Oh, what a good bargain was yours, O Saints! For ye gave blood, and inherited the heavens; and having been tested for a time, ye rejoice unto ages: truly good was your purchase! For having left corruptible things, ye received things incorruptible, and keeping festival with the Angels, ye sing unceasingly unto the consubstantial Trinity.

*Glory, and now and ever, Stavrotheotokion.*
*Model: "O all-praised martyrs:"*
The immaculate Virgin, beholding of old upon the Tree Him Whom she bore from her seedless womb, not enduring the maternal wounding, tearing her hair, said: "O Thou Who upholdest all creation by Thy nod, how art Thou lifted up upon the Cross as one condemned, Who willest by all means to save mankind?"

*Now dismiss: After the Trisagion, troparia: "O Mother of God and Virgin, rejoice:" One prostration. Glory: "O Baptist of Christ:" One prostration. Now and ever: "Supplicate for us:" One prostration. "Beneath thy tender mercy do we flee, O Mother of God:" Without a prostration. "Lord, have mercy," 40. Glory, and now and ever: "More honorable than the Cherubim:" "In the name of the Lord, bless, father." Priest: "Blessed is Christ our God Who is:" And we say the prayer: "O Heavenly King:" And three great prostrations, with the prayer of St. Ephrem: "O Lord and Master of my life:" and the rest, 12. Again having completed the prostrations, we say the above-written prayer: "O Lord and Master of my life:" and one great prostration. Trisagion. After "Our Father:" "Lord, have mercy," 12. Glory, and now and ever: "Lord, have mercy," thrice. "Bless." And the dismissal.*

*We chant Great Compline with prostrations. After "It is truly meet," the troparia of the day and of the temple. And the lesser dismissal. Likewise do we also perform on Friday.*

## CHEESEFARE WEDNESDAY

*On Cheesefare Wednesday, Midnight Office with 24 prostrations. At Matins:*

*We chant Alleluia in the current Tone of the Octoechos, and the Triadica of the Tone, and the customary two kathismata.*

*For on Wednesday and on Friday of Cheesefare Week we chant Alleluia, and make prostrations evening and morning, see as was said above, and perform the Fast according to rule, even if it happen to be of any Saint who has troparia: but the Inter-Hours we do not chant.[^103] If, however, it be the feast of the Meeting of the Lord, or the temple feast of any Saint, we chant the troparia, and make no prostrations, save only three great prostrations.*

*After the first stichology, sessional hymns of the Octoechos, of the Cross.*

*After the second stichology, sessional hymn of the Triodion:*
*Tone 2. Model: "Thou art a well of compassion:"*
Be pleased, O Christ God, by Thine ineffable love for mankind, that we humble ones may pass through the pre-purification of the fasts in peace: overthrow the wiles of the enemy, and by Thy Cross save all, O Thou Who alone knowest the secrets of the heart.

*Glory: the same. Now and ever, Stavrotheotokion. Model:*
Standing before Thy Cross, she that bare Thee without seed, unable to endure beholding Thee suffering unjustly, wailed with weeping, and cried unto Thee: "How dost Thou suffer, Who art impassible in nature, O sweetest Son? I praise Thine utter goodness!"

*Here we read the Homily on Fasting of St. Basil the Great, of which the beginning is: "Comfort ye, comfort ye:"[^104] and Psalm 50.*

*Canons in the Octoechos to the Cross, with the heirmos on 6; and in the Menaion to the Saint on 4; and in the Triodion on 4. At the end of the odes comes the triodion, and we chant the canon of the Triodion with the heirmos on 6; and the triodion on 8, and at the end the heirmos of the triodion. In these odes the canon of the Octoechos and of the Menaion is omitted. And we chant the Menaion in the upper odes thus: Ode 1 of the canon of the Octoechos with the heirmos on 6; and in the Menaion of the Saint, Odes 4 and 6 on 6; and in the Triodion on 6. In like manner we chant Ode 8 with Ode 6, and Ode 9 with Ode 7. Canon of the Triodion.*

*Ode 1, Tone 4. The work of master Andrew of Crete.[^105] Heirmos:*
*I will sing unto Thee, O Lord my God, for Thou didst lead Thy people out of Egyptian bondage, and didst cover the chariots of Pharaoh and his power.*

The Lord, fasting after the manner of men for our model,[^107] overcomes the tempter, showing forth what is ours, and prescribing bounds for us.

Divine Moses on Sinai was accounted worthy by abstinence to speak with God face to face: let us faithful emulate him!

Purify Thy people, O Lord, and having looked down as God with a merciful eye, visit all by the multitude of Thy mercy.

*Theotokion:*
Unto thee do we all flee, O Mother of God, as a firm protection, and moving thee unto prayer, that thou mayest deliver thy flock from every affliction.

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
*My heart is established in the Lord my God: therefore the weak have girded themselves with power.*

Marvelous Enoch by abstinence was translated from the earth:[^106] imitating his example, let us be translated from corruption unto life.

By prayers and fastings let us entreat the Redeemer: for the Creator rejoices together at the repentance of His creations.

Prepare thyself, O soul, and pre-purify thyself before the Passion of Christ, that through the Resurrection thou mayest keep spiritual feast with Him!

*Theotokion:*
As thou gavest birth unto God, pray unceasingly for us: for unto thee, O Mother of God, do we sinners flee.

*Then the triodion of Joseph. Ode 3, Tone 2. Heirmos: "Upon the rock of faith:"*
Thou didst stretch forth Thy palms upon Thy Cross, Thou didst put the curse to death by Thy mortification, Thou didst give life unto men by Thy Passion; therefore we sing of Thy divine crucifixion, O Jesus, Lover of mankind, our God.

Having been put to death by the eating of the tree, by the Tree of Thy Cross we were made alive; this then we offer unto Thee in prayer: send down grace and mercy upon us, O Benefactor and Master abundant in mercy.

The vestibules of fasting have been opened, the racecourse of abstinence draws near; let us rise up with fervent zeal, receiving the God-given gift that quenches the burning heat of transgressions.

The blessed season of the Fast, emitting a ray of repentance, has shone forth; let us approach honorably, dispelling the deepest darkness of sluggishness, all of us rejoicing.

Fasting of the saints philosophically, let us preach abstinence from passions; let us cry aloud in tears, saying: Grant us, O Lord, grace that works together toward Thy desires, O Thou abundant in mercy.

Having received the gifts of the Fast, let us glorify Him Who gave them for salvation, and let us accomplish this laboriously, that we may receive forgiveness of our sins from the hand of the Creator.

*Theotokion:*
Calm the disturbance of my passions, heal the wounds of my soul, raise me up from the sleep of despondency by thine intercession and mediation, O most holy Sovereign Lady, Virgin Mother.

*Another. Heirmos, the same Tone: "My barren mind:"*
When Thou, O Savior, wast willingly lifted up upon the Cross, all earthly creation was shaken, and the veil of the temple was torn in twain.

Thou wast wounded upon the Cross, O my Jesus, for my sake, and pierced in the ribs, O God: whence in faith I worship Thy divine power.

*Glory, Trinity Hymn:*
Bowing my knees to the earth, I worship the Father, I glorify the Son, and I hymn the Spirit, co-enthroned Principle and Tri-hypostatic.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*
Incomprehensible is the mystery of thy childbearing, O Pure One: for without knowing man dost thou, O Mary, give birth unto God, and remainest incorrupt.

Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee!

Having sanctified the fasting season by Thy power, O Christ, save us all from the snares of the enemy, who worship Thee.

*Heirmos:*
*Show my barren mind to be fruitful, O God, Cultivator of good things, Planter of blessings, through Thy tender-heartedness.*

*Sessional hymn of the Menaion to the Saint. Glory, and now and ever: Stavrotheotokion.*

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
*I heard report of Thee, and was afraid; I understood Thy works, and was filled with awe, O Lord.*

Abraham through virtue and hospitality received the Trinity, having come in the likeness of Angels.[^108]

The gift of abstinence is an unstealable treasure, and he who is enriched with it shall be enriched with the Godhead.

*Glory:*
Come, let us weep together in tears, crying aloud in faith: "O God, cleanse us who have greatly sinned."

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*
O Mother immaculate, blessed, pure Virgin, pray for peace unto Thy Son and our God.

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
*Thou Who didst cause the light to shine forth, and didst enlighten the morning, and didst show the day: glory to Thee, glory to Thee, O Jesus, Son of God.*

Moses, having fasted of old on Mount Sinai, was shown to be a beholder of God; and Elijah was taken up on a fiery chariot.[^109]

Through fasting of old the wise Isaiah touches the coal with tongs, when it touched his lips.[^110]

*Glory:*
Daniel fasted before, and the three Youths together, having broken the jaws of the lions, trod down the burning flame.[^111]

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*
O pure Birthgiver of God, who didst bear God incorruptibly in thy womb, preserve thy flock and keep it unharmed.

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
*As Thou didst deliver the Prophet Jonah from the sea monster, O Christ God: so also lead me up from the depth of transgressions, and save me, O only Lover of mankind.*

Honorable fasting saved Jonah of old in the sea monster; let us therefore fast from the heart, and flee the corruption of Gehenna.[^112]

The Ninevites again turned away the wrath of God by fervent repentance and love; let us all now lovingly emulate them.

*Glory:*
The present fast summons us unto repentance; let us therefore run with love, and let us understand what the gift of abstinence is.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*
O thou who didst ineffably give birth unto the Savior of the world, Christ our God, cease not to entreat Him to save the whole race of those who praise thee.

*Kontakion of the Saint; if the Saint has no kontakion, we say the Martyrion of the Tone, which is also the Sessional Hymn.*

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
*O God of our fathers, put us not to shame, but grant us with boldness to cry aloud unto Thee: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers.*

Let us also be as that Daniel, who of old by fasting subdued the roaring lions in the pit.

Let us emulate the three Youths with fear, that we may flee the fire of Gehenna, even as they fled the Babylonian furnace.

*Glory:*
Let us also fast with a pure heart, and let us cleanse the body, and in every way dedicate our whole spirit unto God.

*Now and ever:*

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*
O Virgin, pure Mother, cease not to entreat the pre-eternal Word incarnate of thee, that our souls may be saved.

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
*Christ the King, Whom the captive Youths confessed in the furnace, saying with a great voice: All ye works, sing unto the Lord.*

Joseph, having fasted before, escaped mingling with the unlawful woman, and obtained a kingdom; therefore let us also quench by fasting the inflamed darts of the enemy Beliar.[^113]

By fasting David set up victory over the foreigner, and found a kingdom; therefore let us also through abstinence receive victory over enemies, and be crowned unto the Lord.

Let us also preserve their virtues: the fortitude of Job, the guilelessness of Jacob, the faith of Abraham, the chastity of Joseph, and the courage of David.

*Theotokion:*
Christ the King, Whom the Virgin Mary bore for us, and after childbearing remained a pure Virgin: all ye works of the Lord, sing unto the Lord, and exalt Him unto the ages.

*Then another triodion. Heirmos: "Into the fiery furnace:"*

Moses, raising his palms cruciformly on the mountain, conquered enemies; and Thou, O Savior, having stretched forth Thy hands upon the Cross, didst put to death the all-ruinous tyranny of hades.[^114]

Nailed with nails upon the Cross, and pierced in the ribs, O Christ my Savior, Thou didst deliver the earthborn from the curse, and didst show them to be partakers of unending joy; therefore we bless Thy love for mankind.

The season of abstinence having shone forth, spiritually enlightens the senses of the soul, and dispels the mist of the passions; therefore let us embrace it from the heart, exalting Christ unto the ages.

Fasting puts to death the all-destroying passions of the soul and deadly pleasures, and truly establishes the impulses and movements of the heart in steadfastness; let us therefore receive it lovingly in faith.

Knowing this present holy day not as the beginning of the Fast, O ye faithful, let us honor it with pure intention, calling it the entrance and arrival at the vestibule of the Fast.

The most noble fast, venerable in pre-purifying honors, gently receives the suffering soul with foretastes, being joined as steps and a ladder unto this present day.

*Theotokion:*
Open unto us who knock and invoke thy mercy, O swift refuge of men, steadfast helper of all, O Virgin, and certain protectress of those in distress.

*Another. Heirmos: "In the bush unto Moses:"*

O Master of all, Who wast lifted up upon the Cross, Thou didst call back Adam with Eve, and didst lead them into Paradise, O Christ Savior, who praise Thee unto all ages.

When Thou, O Christ, wast willingly lifted up upon the Cross, the rays of the sun were darkened with fear, and the day departed; therefore the thief confessed Thee as God unto all ages.[^115]

*We bless the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, the Lord.*

*Trinity Hymn:*
We have believed the Son and the Holy Spirit to be equal to the Father, the Holy Trinity in one Godhead; Whom we worship in faith, ever trampling underfoot the teaching of Arius.[^116]

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*
How shall I praise thee as is fitting, O Virgin Mother of God, who am now darkened with foul sins? But, O Most Holy One, forgive my boldness in my poor singing.

Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee!

O Cross, hope of the faithful, weapon of kings, glory of priests, strength of monastics: by thy power save unto the ages all who glorify thee.

*We praise, we bless, and we worship the Lord.*

*Heirmos:*
*Unto Him Who of old prefigured a wonder unto Moses in the bush on Mount Sinai, sing, bless, and exalt Him unto all ages.*

*And "More honorable" is chanted.*

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
*We all magnify Thy love for mankind, O Christ our Savior: the glory of Thy servants and crown of the faithful, Who hast magnified the memory of her who gave Thee birth.*

Moses, parting the sea in Egypt, led the people through, and nourished them in the impassable wilderness, working wonders by fasting.[^117]

Joshua the son of Nun sanctified the people through abstinence, and inherited the promised land, having first crossed the Jordan.

That Gideon, with only three hundred water-lapping men, conquers the foreigners through abstinence and prayer; emulating him, let us also be made like him.[^118]

*Theotokion:*
Rejoice, all-honorable Pure One, boast of virginity, confirmation of Angels, helper of men, joy of the world, Mary, both Mother and handmaid of our God.

*Then the triodion. Heirmos: "From God, God the Word:"*

Having stretched forth Thy divine palms upon the Cross, Thou didst gather together those who before were scattered, O Redeemer; and through mediation Thou didst offer human nature, once condemned, as a gift unto the Father; therefore we sing of Thy most pure crucifixion.

The grace of the holy fast, having shone forth, sends down upon us rays that pre-purify the flow of thoughts, and dispel the darkness of the pupils of the eyes, O faithful; therefore let us receive it with zeal.

Luminous fasting, having drawn for us a cup of divine gifts, offers it today unto all; let us who desire to partake of it for the profit of the soul pray unto the Master of all to work together with us.

With the nails of Thy divine hands, O Compassionate One, Thou didst nail our sins upon the Cross; and with the spear of Thy ribs Thou didst tear up the wicked handwriting of our transgressions and grievous falls; therefore we sing of Thy most pure crucifixion.

The most noble path of virtues is opened, the racecourse of divine fastings, this is beautifully adorned for all; ye who desire to strive lawfully, ask Christ to grant us a peaceful season from on high.

*Theotokion:*
By thy most swift prayer, by thy generous protection, by thy sovereign help, O pure Lady, preserve now thy faithful servants from every assault of the adversary, and save us from passions, transgressions, and afflictions.

*Another. Heirmos: "Supernaturally in the flesh:"*

Having been willingly nailed upon the wood of the Cross, Thou didst deliver us all from the curse of the Law; therefore as is due we magnify Thee, O Christ.

We all worship Thy passions, O Savior, which Thou didst willingly receive, that Thou mightest deliver the human race from the bondage of the enemy.

*Glory, Trinity Hymn:*
The Father co-eternally and incorruptibly begot the Son, and the Spirit is consubstantial with the Father and the Son, an undivided Trinity.

*Now and ever:*

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*
Pray, O most blessed Mary, unto the Savior incarnate of thee, to grant forgiveness of transgressions unto us sinners.

Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee!

Account those who kiss thee worthy, O Cross, by thy power to pass through the fasting season in peace, and deliver them from the bondage of the enemy.

*Heirmos:*
*Her who supernaturally conceived in her womb in the flesh the Word Who shone forth agelessly from the Father, in unceasing hymns let us, the faithful, magnify.*

*Photagogicon in the Octoechos of the Tone, thrice: Trinity Hymn.*

*At the Aposticha, the Idiomelon of the day, Tone 1:*
Fasting from foods, O my soul, and not being cleansed from passions, why dost thou vainly rejoice in not eating? For if it be not an occasion of amendment for thee, thou shalt be hated of God as false, and shalt be likened unto the evil demons, who never eat, yet never cease from sinning, and thou shalt make the fast useless; but abide unshaken against improper impulses, imagining thyself to stand before the crucified Savior, or rather to be crucified together with Him Who was crucified for thy sake, crying aloud unto Him: "Remember me, O Lord, when Thou comest into Thy kingdom."

*We say this twice. Then the Martyrion:*
Neither tribulation, nor distress, nor famine, nor persecution, nor peril, nor the fury of wild beasts, nor the sword, nor threatening fire, were able to separate you from God, O all-praised Martyrs; but rather through love for Him, as if striving in alien bodies, ye forgot nature, despising death; therefore also according to the worth of your sufferings ye received the reward, and became heirs of the heavenly kingdom; pray ye for our souls.[^119]

*Glory, and now and ever: Stavrotheotokion. Model: "Of the heavenly ranks:"*
When the immaculate Virgin beheld the Lamb lifted up upon the Cross, weeping she cried aloud: "O my sweetest Child, what is this new and glorious sight? How, O Thou Who holdest all things in Thy palm, art Thou nailed in the flesh upon the tree?"

*Then: "It is good to give praise:" Trisagion. And after "Our Father:" And the troparion: "Standing in the temple of thy glory:" Lord, have mercy, 40. Glory, and now and ever: "More honorable than the Cherubim:" In the name of the Lord bless, father. Priest: "Blessed is Christ our God, the Existing One, always, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen." Then: "O Heavenly King:" And we make 3 great prostrations, with the prayer of Saint Ephrem: "Lord and Master of my life:" And other 12 prostrations, quietly for the sake of weariness, saying secretly to ourselves at each prostration: "O God, cleanse me a sinner." And again having finished the prostrations, we say the whole prayer written above: "Lord and Master of my life:" And one great prostration.*[^120] *And we join also the First Hour. The superior, or the ecclesiarch, or the presiding monk begins: "Come, let us worship," thrice. 3 prostrations, and the First Hour, in which we read also the Catechesis of Theodore the Studite. At the First Hour, Troparion: "In the morning give ear unto my voice:" Quickly, without chanting. "Order my steps:" and "Let my mouth be filled:" After the Trisagion, troparion: "Speedily anticipate:" Lord, have mercy, 40. And the prayer: "Thou Who at every season:" Lord, have mercy, thrice. Glory, and now and ever: "More honorable than the Cherubim:" "In the name of the Lord:" And the customary prostrations. Trisagion. Lord, have mercy, 12. "O Christ, the True Light:" And the Dismissal. And the exit into the narthex. And the litiya for the reposed.*

*On the same Cheesefare Wednesday, we chant the Hours, the Third and the Sixth, with prostrations and with the Lenten troparia; at the Hours they do not strike the bell.*

*At the Sixth Hour, troparion of the prophecy, Tone 3:*
O holy King, All-powerful, Whom all things fear and tremble before, save us: for Thou art able to forgive sins, as Thou art tender-hearted.

*Glory, and now and ever: the same.*

*Prokeimenon, Tone 6:*
Save, O Lord, Thy people, and bless Thine inheritance.
*Verse: Unto Thee, O Lord, will I cry:*

*Reading from the Prophecy of Joel (Chapter 2):*[^121]
