Thus says the Lord: "Turn ye unto Me with all your heart, in fasting, and in weeping, and in mourning; and rend your hearts, and not your garments, and turn unto the Lord your God: for He is merciful and compassionate, long-suffering and plenteous in mercy, and repents of evils. Who knows if He will turn, and repent, and leave behind Him a blessing, and a sacrifice, and a libation unto the Lord your God? Blow the trumpet in Zion, sanctify a fast, proclaim a healing, gather the people, sanctify the church, choose out the elders, assemble the infants sucking the breasts: let the bridegroom go forth from his chamber, and the bride from her bridal closet. Between the steps of the altar let the priests that minister unto the Lord weep, and let them say: 'Spare, O Lord, Thy people, and give not Thine inheritance unto reproach, that the heathen should rule over them, lest they say among the heathen: Where is their God?' And the Lord was jealous for His land, and spared His people. And the Lord answered His people, and said: 'Behold, I will send you wheat, and wine, and olive oil, and ye shall be satisfied with them, and I will no more give you for a reproach among the heathen. And him that is from the north I will drive far from you, and will cast him out into a waterless land, and I will destroy his face toward the former sea, and his hinder parts toward the latter sea; and his rot shall come up, and his stench shall come up, because he has magnified his deeds. Fear not, O land; be glad and rejoice, for the Lord has magnified His doing. Be of good courage, ye beasts of the field, for the pastures of the wilderness have sprouted, for the tree has borne its fruit, the vine and the fig tree have yielded their strength. And ye children of Zion, rejoice and be glad in the Lord your God, for He has given you food unto righteousness, and He will rain upon you the early and the latter rain, as before. And your threshing floors shall be full of wheat, and the vats shall overflow with wine and oil. And I will restore unto you the years that the locust has eaten, and the cankerworm, and the caterpillar, and the palmerworm, My great army which I sent among you. And ye shall eat in plenty, and be satisfied, and praise the name of the Lord your God, Who has dealt wondrously with you; and My people shall never be put to shame.'"

*Prokeimenon, Tone 7:*
The Lord will give strength unto His people; the Lord will bless His people with peace.
*Verse: Bring unto the Lord, ye sons of God:*

*Then: "Speedily let them anticipate:" Trisagion. And the rest according to the custom of the Fast. And the prayer: "Thou Who at every season, and Lord of hosts:" Together we also chant the Ninth Hour, and the prayer: "O Master, Lord Jesus Christ our God:" We chant the Typika, and the Beatitudes: "In Thy kingdom:" Quickly, without chanting. Glory, and now and ever: "Remember us, O Lord:" and three prostrations. Another choir: And the rest. And after "Our Father:" Kontakion of the church, and to the Saint. Glory, kontakion: "With the Saints give rest:" And now and ever, kontakion: "Steadfast Protectress of Christians:" Lord, have mercy, 40. Glory, and now and ever: "More honorable than the Cherubim:" Three great prostrations, and other 12. The other choir begins Vespers: "Come, let us worship:" thrice, and the psalm: "Bless the Lord, O my soul." And the rest.*

*On Cheesefare Wednesday evening, at "Lord, I have cried," stichera as usual. Glory, and now and ever: Theotokion. Prokeimenon, Tone 5:*
O God, in Thy name save me, and in Thy strength judge me.
*Verse: O God, give ear unto my prayer, give ear unto the words of my mouth.*

*Reading from the Prophecy of Joel (Chapter 3):*[^122]
Thus says the Lord: "Let all the nations arise and go up to the Valley of Jehoshaphat, for there will I sit to judge all the nations round about. Put ye in the sickles, for the harvest of the vineyard is at hand: come, tread ye, for the winepress is full, the vats overflow, for their wickedness is multiplied. Voices have sounded in the field of judgment, for the day of the Lord is near in the valley of judgment. The sun and the moon shall be darkened, and the stars shall withdraw their shining. And the Lord shall cry aloud from Zion, and utter His voice from Jerusalem; and heaven and earth shall be shaken, but the Lord shall spare His people, and the Lord shall strengthen the children of Israel. And ye shall know that I am the Lord your God, Who dwell in Zion, on My holy mountain; and Jerusalem shall be holy, and foreigners shall pass through it no more. And it shall come to pass in that day that the mountains shall drop down sweetness, and the hills shall flow with milk, and all the springs of Judah shall flow with water, and a fountain shall come forth out of the house of the Lord, and shall water the torrent of the shittim trees. Egypt shall be a desolation, and Idumea shall be a wilderness of desolation, for the oppression of the children of Judah, because they have shed innocent blood in their land. But Judah shall be inhabited for ever, and Jerusalem from generation to generation. And I will avenge their blood, and will not leave it unpunished; and the Lord shall dwell in Zion."

*Prokeimenon, Tone 6:*
Let Israel hope in the Lord, from henceforth and unto all ages.
*Verse: Lord, my heart is not exalted, nor are mine eyes lifted up. And: "Vouchsafe, O Lord:"*

*At the Aposticha, the Idiomelon of the day, Tone 3:*
The spring of the fast has shone forth, the flower of repentance; let us therefore cleanse ourselves, brethren, from every defilement, singing unto the Giver of Light let us say: "Glory to Thee, O only Lover of mankind."

*And we say the verse: "Unto Thee have I lifted up:" And we repeat the idiomelon. Then the verse: "Have mercy on us, O Lord:" And the Martyrion:*
O Martyrs of the Lord, having been established by faith, confirmed by hope, spiritually united by the love of Thy Cross, ye destroyed the tyranny of the enemy, and having obtained crowns, ye pray with the bodiless hosts for our souls.

*Glory, and now and ever, Theotokion:*
O pure Foremost Lady, who art the boast of the heavenly ranks, the song of the Apostles, the fulfillment of the Prophets, O Sovereign Lady, receive our prayers.

*Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart: After the Trisagion, troparion of the Saint; Glory, and now and ever: his Theotokion. If there be none, then the troparion of the day. Glory, and now and ever: Theotokion, according to the tone of the troparion. Litany: "Have mercy on us, O God:" 3 great prostrations. "Blessed be the name of the Lord:" "I will bless the Lord:" "It is truly meet." And the Dismissal. And the exit into the narthex. And the customary litiya for the reposed takes place.*

*Be it known that in Palestine, which is in the land of Judea, we have not received from the holy fathers to celebrate the full Divine Liturgies on Wednesday and Friday of Cheesefare Week, nor the Presanctified; for on those two days we chant Alleluia with prostrations, evening and morning, as was stated above.*[^123]

*After Vespers on these two days we eat cheese and eggs, observing also the rule of our father among the saints Nicephorus, Patriarch of Constantinople the Confessor, who says: "It is fitting for monastics to fast on Wednesday and Friday of Cheesefare." This rule overturns the Jacobite tradition and the Tetradite heresy.*[^124]

*On Cheesefare Wednesday evening, we chant Small Compline. And we chant the canon which is in the Menaion in order, of the Saint who is to fall on Saturday.*[^125]

*On Cheesefare Thursday at Matins, after the 1st kathisma psalmody, Sessional hymns of the Octoechos, Alleluia.*

*After the 2nd kathisma psalmody, Sessional hymn of the Triodion, Tone 5. Model: "Co-beginningless:"*
The Forty Days, the pre-purifying season, all the Apostles today crown, and they sanctify the fasting season before Christ the Redeemer, and herald unto all His reception, and pray unto the Lord that our souls may find mercy.

*Glory: the same. And now and ever, Theotokion, the same model:*
Unto those who possess unwavering hope in thee, O pure Virgin, being a protection against diverse temptations, tribulations, and grievous afflictions, deliver them, praying unto thy Son with His Apostles, and save all who praise thee.

*Then we read the discourse of Saint Anastasius, Abbot of Mount Sinai, and Psalm 50.*

*The canons we chant of the Octoechos and the Menaion. But in those odes in which we chant triodia, we omit such odes of the Octoechos. Triodion. Composition of Lord Joseph, Tone 4. Ode 4. Heirmos: "The Prophet heard:"*
Thy disciples, O Lord, shone forth in the world as a ray of divine knowledge, and darkened the deceit of delusion, having dispelled the darkness; by their prayers, O Compassionate One, save those who praise Thee.

The vestibules of the Fast receive those who run watchfully, crowned with the fair fruits of ascetic labors; with hymns and mystical songs, O faithful, let us all assemble diligently.

Having received the garments of mortification, I, wretched one, clothed myself in the boldness of intemperance; but do Thou, O Son of God, clothe me in the radiant garment of regeneration.

My life has been consumed in malice and all manner of uncleanness; but unto Thee, the All-compassionate, do I flee; anticipating me, therefore, save me, O Christ God, by Thy goodness.

*Theotokion:*
Thou didst conceive beyond word, and didst give birth beyond nature, O Birthgiver of God, unto the Sovereign Master of creation; Whom entreat unceasingly, that we who call thee blessed may be delivered from all wrath.

*Another, Tone 2: Heirmos: "Thou hast come from the Virgin:"*
Having dispelled the mist of intemperance, O Apostles, by the splendors of your teachings, ye enlightened all sinners and righteous through abstinence, as all-praised ones.

As radiant pearls of the Word, O Apostles, ye adorned all the ends of the earth with abstinence, truly beautifying the nobility of our souls.

Having quenched the furnace of passions by the dew of fasting, O Apostles, ye taught all men to possess this unstealable city and dwelling of sanctification.

*Glory:*

I, wretched one, have sinned more than all men, and have not repented, having sinned as Manasseh; grant me manners of repentance, O Lord, before death looses me.[^126]

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*
We all, the faithful, know thee as a harbor of salvation and an unbreakable wall, O Lady Mother of God: for by thy prayers thou dost deliver our souls from afflictions.

*Then the Heirmos:*
*Thou hast come from the Virgin, neither a mediator nor an Angel, but Thyself incarnate, O Lord, and hast saved me, the whole man; therefore I cry unto Thee: Glory to Thy power, O Lord.*

*Ode 8. Heirmos: "Great works, O Master:"*
The whole earth, O Lord, was filled with Thy praise: for the divine utterance of Thy divine disciples traversed it all, turning it from the depth of ignorance unto knowledge, singing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord.

The divine grace of repentance has appeared, bringing salvation unto those who enjoy it, victory over struggles, sweats, and sicknesses; run therefore, O my soul, unto thy Master, seeking to receive forgiveness of thy many transgressions.

The racecourse of God-given abstinence has been opened; let us who need mercy brightly run to meet it: for the Tender-hearted One thirsts for our salvation, and reaches forth to give forgiveness unto those who seek Him zealously and serve Him with love.

By the fast of oblivion, living peaceably in good works, nourish the Lord, O soul, by doing good of virtue, offering unto Him beautiful things as sweet-smelling sacrifices, and crying aloud: Bless the Lord unceasingly, all ye works.

*Theotokion:*
O holy Mother of God, Sovereign Lady, who excellest in all things, receiving the supplications of thy servants, deliver me from darkness and unquenchable fire, cleansing the multitude of my evils through thine intercession and thy single divine prayer.

*Another. Heirmos: "The Youths were terrified:"*
Christ, having appeared as light, gave Apostles unto the ends of the whole inhabited earth, saying: "Go, teach among the nations, that ye may see Me living in the flesh by abstinence, and trampling down all the power of the enemy, and showing men how to sing rightly."

Thou didst take, O Christ, the coming abstinence as a purification for men, and a cutting off of passions; therefore Thine Apostles were well-pleasing, and appeared as bright luminaries upon earth, proclaiming the Lord in three Persons, and in one Essence, unto all who sing of Him.

Ye were sent forth as preachers unto the nations by Christ the Teacher, O disciples, by divine teachings to enlighten their thoughts, to restrain passions and warfare, to desire abstinence, and to know this Lord, Creator, Maker of all, and Benefactor.

*We bless the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, the Lord.*

Even as Cain of old, the murderer, I did not offer the unblemished sacrifice of my soul, O Christ, being held by an unclean mind; despise me not as I draw near unto Thee by fasting, O Savior all-good, but look down upon the gifts which I bear unto Thee with love, O my God, in the season of fasting.[^127]

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*
Blessed was the womb of the Mother of God, for it received the Word, Who was mingled hypostatically with human form through the grossness of flesh from her; and she was shown to be the city of God, wherein the Most High was well-pleased to dwell, even the Lord God; therefore we cry unto thee: Rejoice, O full of grace, pure Mother of God!

*We praise, we bless, and we worship the Lord.*

*Heirmos:*
*The fire that was nourished in measureless matter and unwearied shrank back, terrified at the pious Youths, their undefiled body conforming to their soul; and unto the ever-living flame a song of ages was sung: Sing unto the Lord, all ye works, and exalt Him unto all ages.*

*And "More honorable" is chanted.*

*Ode 9. Heirmos: "For He hath done to me:"*
Ye were sent as an immaterial flame unto the world, delivering it from the depth of sins; with joy we praise Him Who strengthened you as His Apostles.

As salt unto the whole world that had grown foolish of old, Christ sent you forth, O wise ones, to bring it unto knowledge of Him; we praise you in faith.

Because a multitude of grievous transgressions holds me fast, with tears I fall down before Thee, O Christ, begging forgiveness, that a seasonable time be granted me during the Fast.

Bound as with unbreakable chains of my passions, I groan and cry aloud unto Thee, O Savior: deliver me, that rejoicing exceedingly I may sing of Thy tender-heartedness.

*Theotokion:*
Since God showed thee, O pure Virgin, as a help unto the human race, cease not diligently to entreat Him for us, the faithful.

*Another. Heirmos: "The Incomprehensible God:"*
The fast showed forth the choir of the Apostles, shining unto the whole inhabited earth, and enlightening the world with divine splendor.

The choir of Thy disciples, O Jesus, Lover of mankind, taught the gentile nations to treasure up the wealth of abstinence.

The twelve-stringed utterance, the harmony of Thy disciples, bestows upon men the wealth of abstinence and a fountain of salvation.

*Glory:*
With the voice of the Prodigal I cry aloud unto Thee, O Lord: "Father, I have sinned, save me, O Compassionate One, that Thou mayest not separate me from Thy glory."

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*
Having borne God in thy womb as a man, and having poured forth life unto the world, we praise thee, O all-holy Virgin.

*Heirmos:*
*Her who contained in her womb the Incomprehensible God, and brought forth joy unto the world, we praise thee, O Virgin Mother of God.*

*Exapostilarion of the Tone.*

*At the Aposticha we chant the Idiomelon of the day, Tone 3:*
The beauty of abstinence has shone forth, dispelling the ancient mist; the fair season of the fast has arrived, bringing healing of the passions of the soul; Daniel of old and the Youths in Babylon were fenced about by this: he indeed bridled the mouths of the lions, while they quenched the furnace flame; with them save us also by the same, O Christ God, as Thou art the Lover of mankind.

*And we repeat this with the verse: "We were filled:" Then the verse: "And let the brightness:" And the Martyrion:*
As luminaries ye shine in the world, and after death, O holy Martyrs, having fought the good fight, possessing boldness: entreat Christ that our souls may find mercy.

*Glory, and now and ever, Theotokion:*
O holy Mother of God among women, unwedded Mother, pray unto the King and God Whom thou didst bear, that He may save us, as He is the Lover of mankind.

*Then: "It is good to give praise:" We join also the First Hour, as usual. And the Dismissal.*

*On the same Cheesefare Thursday evening:*
*From the beginning we begin prostrations, and the rest of the whole service, as was also indicated above for Cheesefare Tuesday.*

*At "Lord, I have cried," stichera as usual; Glory, and now and ever: Theotokion. "O Gladsome Light:" And the Prokeimenon of the day.*

*At the Aposticha, the Idiomelon of the day, Tone 2:*
The Cross of the Lord, unto those who worship it without delusion, is the sprouting of every pleasure and the law of abstinence: for they who gaze unceasingly upon Him Who was nailed upon it crucify the flesh with its passions and lusts;[^128] of whom let us also strive to be, and by a pure fast let us be joined unto the love of mankind of Him Who condescended unto us through suffering, and bestowed upon our nature His dispassion, Who possesses great mercy.

*We repeat this with the verse: "Unto Thee have I lifted up mine eyes:" Verse: "Have mercy on us, O Lord:" And the Martyrion:*
Not having desired earthly pleasure, the passion-bearers were accounted worthy of heavenly good things, and became companions of the Angels: O Lord, by their prayers have mercy on us and save us.

*Glory, and now and ever: Stavrotheotokion. Model: "When from the tree:"*
When the pure Lady beheld the ripe Cluster, Whom she bore untilled in her womb, hanging upon the tree, weeping she exclaimed and cried aloud: "O Child, pour forth sweetness, whereby all intoxication of passions is removed, O Benefactor, for the sake of me who bore Thee, with divine consolations, as Thou art tender-hearted."

*Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart: "O Virgin Mother of God:" And the rest, making great prostrations. Then the Dismissal.*

*Compline we chant Great with prostrations, as was indicated for Tuesday: fol. 35.*[^129]

*On Cheesefare Friday at Matins, after the Six Psalms we chant Alleluia, to the tone of the Trinity Hymn of the Tone.*

*After the 1st kathisma psalmody, Sessional hymns of the Cross of the Octoechos.*

*After the 2nd kathisma psalmody, Sessional hymn of the Triodion, Tone 7. Model: "As having:"*
Exalt the horn of the Church, O precious Cross, cast down heretical pride by thy power, and exalt the choirs of the Orthodox: grant us all to anticipate thy fore-announcement, to worship Thee, the footstool of Christ: for in Thee do we boast, O blessed Tree.

*Glory: the same. And now and ever, Stavrotheotokion:*
As thou hast compassion upon our lowliness, and lookest upon earthborn men prone to stumbling, have mercy, O blessed Mother of God, continue praying that we may not perish grievously: pray, as the all-pure one, unto the God of reconciliation, that our souls may be saved, O most holy Virgin.

*Then we read the discourse of the great Basil on fasting, of which the beginning is: "Blow the trumpet at the new moon:"*[^130]

*Then Psalm 50. And the canons of the Octoechos, of the Menaion, and of the Triodion. In those odes in which we chant triodia, such odes of the Octoechos and of the Menaion are omitted: for the triodia have two heirmoi.*

*Canon of the Triodion. Work of sir Joseph.*

*Ode 1, Tone 8. Heirmos: "Crossing the water:"*

The divine time of abstinence has shone forth upon all, the illumination of repentance, taking away the darkness of transgressions; let us receive it with an eager heart.

Behold, the beauty of repentance enlarges the souls by the arrival of fasting; having entered into it soberly, let us, the faithful, receive the remission of transgressions.

*Glory:*

Principalities, Authorities, and Cherubim, and all ye Powers, pray that we may complete the fasting season in repentance and every purity.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*

Holy Virgin, sole protection of the faithful, grant thy prayer as a helper unto all during the time of fasting, who know thee as the pure Mother of God.

*Heirmos: "Crossing the water:"*

*Ode 3. Heirmos: "Of the heavenly vault:"*

Let us flee all-destroying passions of the soul by the bestowal of the fast, and let us show forth fruits of compunction, having formerly provoked the tender-hearted God by our sins.

Having all now taken up torches with the oil of good deeds, let us eagerly be diligent, that we may enter with the wise virgins into the radiant bridal chamber rejoicing.[^131]

*Glory:*

O divinely speaking Prophets, God-beholding Martyrs, and divine disciples of the Savior, pray Him, let us all beseech them, that we may well begin and well-pleasingly finish the course of fasting.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*

As thou art the cause of all good things, O Sovereign Lady, we all diligently entreat thee: that through thy mediation we may enter together into the fasting struggle, and that a saving end may be granted unto it.

*Heirmos:*
*Creator of the vault of heaven, O Lord, and Builder of the Church: do Thou establish me in Thy love, O summit of desires, confirmation of the faithful, O only Lover of mankind.*

*Then the Sessional hymn of the Menaion, and the Stavrotheotokion.*

*Ode 4. Heirmos: "I heard, O Lord, of Thy dispensation:"*

As the dawn leaning down, the grace of fasting now sets before us the season of repentance, releasing the darkness of debts.

Let us feed the poor, receiving mercy through mercy; and let us wash away the defilements of the soul with the divine water of fasting.

*Glory:*

Heavenly Angels, entreat the Giver of grace that He may receive our contrite repentance through His boundless compassions.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*

Pure mercy seat of sinners, holy Sovereign Lady, through thy mediation tear up the handwriting of my transgressions.[^132]

*Heirmos:*
*I heard, O Lord, the mystery of Thy dispensation; I understood Thy works, and I glorified Thy Godhead.*

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
*Why hast Thou cast me off from Thy presence, O Light unwaning, and alien darkness has covered me, the wretched one? But turn me back, and guide my paths unto the light of Thy commandments, I pray Thee.*

Making the present day the beginning of purity of life, let us, the faithful, eagerly prepare ourselves for ascetic struggles, offering bodily afflictions and spiritual fruitfulness unto the Master of all.

Fasting showed Moses to be a partaker of the divine vision of God; therefore, O my soul, emulating him, receive the fast, having arranged divine ascents in thyself, that thou mayest behold the brightness of God.[^133]

By the supplications of the holy Apostles and hieromartyrs, account us worthy, O compassionate Jesus, we pray, to pass through the season of fasting in repentance and in every cessation of sin.

*Theotokion:*

Desiring to enter through the door of fasting, we pray thee, O Door of God, to enter together with thy servants, O Sovereign Lady, and to broaden all our intentions and thoughts to do saving desires.

*Then the Triodion of sir Joseph.*

*Ode 5, Tone 6. Heirmos: "With Thy divine light, O Good One:"*

Having nailed Thy hands to the Cross, pierced in the ribs with a spear, O Lover of mankind, Thou didst tear up the handwriting of fallen Adam; therefore, O Giver of life, we glorify Thee with hymns.[^134]

By deceit the subtle serpent, having cast upon me passions of the soul, drove me out of paradise; but Thou, having nailed Thy palms upon the Cross, didst draw me unto the height of imperishability, O Savior.

The divine season of the fast, purifying the passions of the soul and washing away bodily wounds, has now come and arrived; let us assemble, ye faithful, and receive it with philosophical wisdom.

A good season has appeared, clothing every face in the divine gladness of the soul; come, let us receive it joyfully, pre-purifying ourselves by fasting and prayer.

Fasting, tears, prayer, and a humble disposition let us offer unto Him Who humbled Himself for our sake, that in the day of abstinence He may grant remission of our transgressions.

*Theotokion:*

With thy radiant beamings, O good Sovereign Lady of the world, drive away the darkness of my soul and the night of my sin, that I may eagerly hymn and bless thee.

*Another canon, Tone 8. Heirmos: "Why hast Thou cast me off:"*

I worship Thy Cross, O Lord, Lover of mankind, whereby Thou didst save me, and I hymn Thy saving and divine Passions, O Master, through which I was delivered from painful passions, O Word, passing across unharmed unto life.

Trusting in the Cross, we turn away from the deceit of the adversaries; rooted in it, we the faithful are made known unto God, as chosen newborn lambs, and we drank the heavenly milk.

*Glory, Trinity Hymn:*

We all glorify the Father, and the Word, and the Holy Spirit in one nature, setting forth a radiant confession: worshipping Both, and distinguishing the Persons, serving them unconfusedly and unalterably.[^135]

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*

Thou art the hope of the ends of the earth, the joy of thy servants, O pure Virgin; preserve those who honor thine image with love, O all-pure one; and by thy prayers deliver us all from the alien one, as thou art most merciful.

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*

Make straight Thy right path, O Lord, for all Thy servants who honor it with love, establish the course of the fast, and account us worthy of being led unto what is better in Thy holy kingdom.

*Heirmos: "Why hast Thou cast me off:"*

*Ode 6. Heirmos: "Cleanse me, O Savior:"*

Having fasted, the Redeemer determined the present time for us as a purifier of the defilements of the soul; let us the faithful draw near with a fervent heart, that we may receive remission.

Having accepted the sighing of the publican, O Christ, and the weeping offered from the soul of the harlot: receive our supplications as the Lover of mankind, granting us cleansing.

*Glory:*

By the entreaties of Thy heralds, and prophets, martyrs, and Thine Apostles, venerable ones, and hierarchs, and all Thy righteous ones, O Christ, send down cleansing of transgressions upon our souls.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*

O pure one, who alone didst establish the weak state of human nature by thy divine Childbearing, appear as a helper unto me as I enter into the divine course of the fast.

*Heirmos:*
*Cleanse me, O Savior, for many are mine iniquities, and lead me up from the depth of evils, I pray Thee: for unto Thee have I cried, and do Thou give ear unto me, O God of my salvation.*

*Kontakion of the Saint.*
*If the Saint has no kontakion, we say the Martyrion of the Tone.*

*Ode 7. Heirmos: "The Hebrew children in the furnace:"*

Of old Elijah was carried upon a fiery chariot, having been enlightened by fasting, O my soul; emulating him, put to death the lusts of the flesh by abstinence.[^136]

Behold the season of abstinence, showing forth unto thee the light of salvation; neglect it not, O my soul, while God is long-suffering, but eagerly cry aloud: O Good One, have compassion on me.

*Glory:*

Fasting, having fenced about the Children, preserved them unconsumed by the fire; O Jesus, by their prayers deliver me from eternal fire through Thy manifold tender mercy.[^137]

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*

O only Help of men, be a helper unto us thy servants in the time of abstinence, that pleasing God through repentance, we may receive the heavenly kingdom.

*Heirmos:*
*The Hebrew Children in the furnace boldly trod down the flame, and turned the fire into dew, crying aloud: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto the ages.*

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
*The Chaldean tyrant furiously kindled the furnace sevenfold for the godly; but seeing them saved by a superior power, he cried aloud unto the Creator and Redeemer: Ye children, bless; ye priests, hymn; ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages.*

Let us eagerly kindle the furnace of repentance, and let us burn therein all bodily pleasures; and that we may not experience the future fire, let us ask of Him Who is rich in mercy, crying aloud: Ye priests, bless; ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages.

May the threshold-season of the fast become for us the cause of putting away all sin, that we may not bend downward, nor run despondently, so that in brief and few days we may wash away many defilements through compunction of heart, hymning our only God.

Ranks of Angels, gathering of martyrs, holy choir of divine Apostles, assembly of venerable ones, hierarchs and prophets, entreat Thee, O good Lover of mankind: grant true repentance unto Thy servants in the season of abstinence now being introduced.

*Theotokion:*

All-pure Birthgiver of God, unto thee we flee: have compassion on us through thy good prayer, and grant Thy Son and Lord to be well-reconciled unto all of us in the season of the fast now being introduced, unto the salvation of the faithful who hymn thee unto all ages.

*Triodion. Heirmos: "For the laws of the fathers:"*

Having not kept our paternal inheritance, we have been enslaved unto sinful laws; but stretching forth Thy palms upon the divine Cross, Thou didst grant freedom unto them all: have mercy on us, O Merciful One, who come unto Thee with faith in these holy days, supremely exalting Thee unto all ages.

By Thy Cross tearing down the partition and the middle wall of the fence, and renewing rich peace unto those living peacefully at the ends of the earth: grant us, O Christ, with steadfastness to pass through the coming fast, as we hymn the Lord unceasingly and supremely exalt Him unto all ages.[^138]

The grace of fasting today offers solar rays unto all, pre-cleansing darkness from sin; held fast by diverse passions, having come to joy, let us receive the gift with philosophical wisdom, crying aloud: Hymn the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages.

When of old in paradise the first-formed man bitterly and irrationally ate, he was rejected and condemned, and cast out from delight; but nailed with nails upon the Tree, Thou didst nail the evil handwriting of his sin; therefore we hymn Thine abundant tender mercy unto all ages.[^139]

Having cast away the law of fasting, we slipped into the abyss of sin, and have need of the fast now being introduced; as we pass through it, O Compassionate One, send down grace and rich peace from heaven: Hymn the works of the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages.

*Theotokion:*

Restoration of the falling, mediatress for sinners, refreshment of strangers, consolation of the afflicted, O most holy Virgin: dissolve the sorrow of my soul, O pure one, and pray that consolation from on high be given me from God, as I eagerly hymn and supremely exalt thee unto all ages.

*Another canon. Heirmos: "Angels and heavens:"*

Seeing Thee nailed in the flesh upon the Cross, O Compassionate One, the nature of created things was altered: the light of day turned into darkness, the earth moved, and all things were shaken.

Having co-exalted human nature unto the height of the Cross, and from Thy divine ribs having poured forth the wealth of salvation, O Savior, unto those who with faith worship Thy most pure Passion.

*We bless the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, the Lord.*

*Trinity Hymn:*

One God is the Trinity: neither the Father departing into Sonship, nor the Son changing into procession; but personal properties are in both: Light, God; Three do I glorify unto the ages.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*

Tell us, how didst thou give birth unto Him Who was timelessly begotten of the Father before the ages, and Who is hymned with the Holy Spirit? Or even as He alone knows, Who was well-pleased to be born of thee unto the ages.

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*

Having accepted our repentance as Thou art good by nature, deliver us, O Lord, from the snares of the enemy, that with faith and love we may now hymn Thy holy property.

*We praise, we bless, we worship the Lord.*

*Heirmos:*
*Angels and heavens, bless, hymn, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages, Who sits upon the throne of glory and is unceasingly glorified as God.*

*And the "More honorable" is sung. Ode 9. Heirmos:*
*Heaven was struck with awe at this, and the ends of the earth were amazed, that God appeared unto men in the flesh, and thy womb became more spacious than the heavens; therefore the ranks of angels and men magnify thee as the Mother of God.*

Behold, the light-bearing time has arrived, the holy day has shone forth; flee from thy dark passions, O my soul, and receive the rays that guide thee unto the light; drinking compunction as wine, rejoice, and hate the intoxication of pleasures.

Truly most blessed is the time of fasting, O Christ, which Thou hast given unto all the faithful for the conquest of sins, and saving cleansing, and receptacle of gifts, wherein we pray Thee: make us all partakers of Thy good things, O Savior.

Thou Who customarily pourest forth Thy rich mercies upon us, O Compassionate One: give us tears that cleanse the defilements and thoughts of those who love Thee; faith and pure love, rich repentance, and complete adoption unto Thee, the only Multimerciful One.

Divine multitude of all the Angels, and praiseworthy choirs of the saints, diligently pray now unto the Good One: that He may strengthen us to run without stumbling this divine course of the present fast, and make us victorious.

*Theotokion:*

Blessed Virgin, who didst bear the good Savior: comfort all of us, O Sovereign Lady, who are maltreated by boundless passions and thoughts, and weighed down with intolerable burdens of sins; that we may fittingly magnify thee as the Mother of God.

*Another canon. Heirmos: "Every nature is at a loss:"*

Every nature of angels and men is at a loss to give thanks for Thy tender-heartedness, O Benefactor: for willingly in the flesh Thou didst become poor for our sake, and wast stretched out upon the Tree for us, having become a curse, that Thou mightest take away the first curse of mankind.[^140]

The radiant day of abstinence has arrived; with a radiant countenance, come, O my soul, let us meet the Master, asking that grace be sent down upon us from on high, and to find correction of our many transgressions, so that we may not be tried by the most fearful Gehenna there.

Unto those held fast in the darkness of sins, the saving entrances of repentance have now arrived, enlightening the souls of all; therefore, O my soul, turn away from the darkening of the surfeit of passions, make haste, that thou mayest enjoy eternal delights there.

Having willingly stretched out Thy hands upon the Tree, Thou didst gather together all that were scattered, O Giver of life; and having opened Thy ribs with a spear, O Long-suffering One, Thou didst right for us the corruption that sprouted from the rib; therefore with thanksgiving we hymn Thy tender-heartedness.[^141]

*Theotokion:*

Protection of all who trust in thee, being a vigilant protectress in tribulations, O Mother of God: deliver us from eternal Gehenna and from the impending bitter torments, that we may fittingly hymn thy greatness.

*Another canon. Heirmos: "Virginity is foreign to mothers:"*

We worship Thy wounds, O Giver of life, whereby we have been delivered from the passions of sin; by Thy precious Cross we are known to be sealed, unto salvation and protection from every assault of the enemy.

Illumine with the rays of Thy Cross, Thou Who didst willingly endure for the salvation of all, the souls of those who hymn Thy Passions, O All-Merciful One; and direct and guide our life onto the path of life.

We have sinned, having transgressed Thy commandments, and from the paths of Thy divine ordinances, O Savior, we have turned far aside through negligence, O Lover of mankind; but O Compassionate One, recall our souls from deceit.

*Glory, Trinity Hymn:*

Praise and honor befit the Trinity, and glory as unto one Lordship and one Kingdom: unconfusedly, indivisibly, a Monad worshipped in Godhead, undivided in nature, unceasingly magnified.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*

Be Thou reconciled through the prayers of Thine all-pure Mother, O All-Compassionate One, All-King of glory, when Thou shalt come to judge Thy servants, as Thou art merciful: for in Thee have we all believed, and Thee do we know as God.

*Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.*

The light-bearing fast now approaching accepts the table of ascetic struggles set forth; therefore, ye faithful, let us all soberly receive this precious chalice of cleansing tears, that we may not be tried there with incurable tears.

*Katavasia:*
*Virginity is foreign to mothers, and childbearing is strange to virgins: in thee, O Mother of God, both have been accomplished; therefore all the generations of the earth unceasingly magnify thee.*

*The Trinity Hymn Photogogic of the Tone, thrice. And the rest.*

*At the Aposticha, we chant the Idiomelon of the day, Tone 6:*

Before the Savior's Cross, when sin reigned and impiety held sway, bodily food brought delight unto men, and few cared little for the desires of the flesh; but since the mystery of the Cross was accomplished, and the demonic tyranny was quenched by the knowledge of God, heavenly virtue lives on earth; therefore fasting is honored, abstinence shines forth, prayer is directed aright, and the present time is a witness, given unto us by Christ God Who was crucified, unto the salvation of our souls.

*And we say the verses:*
*Verse: We were filled in the morning with Thy mercy, O Lord:*
*And we repeat the idiomelon. Then also the Martyrion:*
*Verse: And let the brightness of the Lord our God be upon us:*
O Lord, at the memory of Thy saints all creation keeps feast: the heavens rejoice with the Angels, and the earth is glad with men; by their prayers have mercy on us.

*Glory, and now and ever, Stavrotheotokion:*
When the all-pure one beheld Thee hanging upon the Cross, weeping she cried aloud in a mother's manner: "O my Son and my God, my sweetest Child, how dost Thou endure a shameful passion?"

*Then: "It is good to give praise:"*
*And the Trisagion. Troparion: "Standing in the temple:" "Lord, have mercy," 40.*
*And the verse is spoken by the priest:*
**Priest:** Blessed is He Who is, Christ our God, always, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.
*Choir: "O Heavenly King:"*
*And we make three great prostrations, and secretly say the prayer of our venerable Father Ephrem the Syrian:*
**"O Lord and Master of my life:"** *And the rest.*[^142]
*And we make the other prostrations. And we join also the First Hour, as usual; and after the customary prostrations, we read the catecheses of our venerable Father Theodore the Studite. Then the Dismissal.*[^143]

*On the same Cheesefare Friday we chant the Hours with prostrations, as was indicated also for Wednesday.*

*At the Sixth Hour we chant the Troparion of the Prophecy, Tone 8:*
Grant us help from sorrow, O Lord, and save us, O Thou Who wast born of the Virgin, Lover of mankind.
*And we repeat the same.*

*Prokeimenon, Tone 1:*
Let Thy mercy, O Lord, be upon us, according as we have hoped in Thee.
*Verse: Rejoice in the Lord, O ye righteous; praise is meet for the upright.*

*Reading from the Prophecy of Zechariah (Chapter 8):*[^144]
**Reader:** Thus says the Lord Almighty: Behold, I will save My people from the east country, and from the west country. And I will bring them (into their land), and they shall dwell in the midst of Jerusalem, and they shall be My people, and I will be their God in truth and in righteousness.
Thus says the Lord Almighty: Let your hands be strong, ye that hear in these days these words from the mouth of the prophets, since the day that the house of the Lord Almighty was founded, and from the time that the temple was built. For before those days there was no hire for man, nor any hire for beast; neither was there any peace to him that went out or came in because of affliction, and I will let loose all men, every one against his neighbor. But now I will not do unto the remnant of this people according to the former days, says the Lord Almighty. But I will show peace: the vine shall give her fruit, and the ground shall give her increase, and the heavens shall give their dew, and I will cause the remnant of this My people to inherit all these things. And it shall come to pass, that as ye were a curse among the nations, O house of Judah and house of Israel, so will I save you, and ye shall be a blessing: be of good courage, and let your hands be strong. For thus says the Lord Almighty: As I thought to punish you, when your fathers provoked Me to wrath, says the Lord Almighty, and I repented not: so have I prepared and thought in these days to do good unto Jerusalem and to the house of Judah; be of good courage. These are the words that ye shall do: Speak ye truth every one to his neighbor; judge truth and the judgment of peace in your gates. And let none of you imagine evil in your hearts against his neighbor; and love not a false oath: for all these things do I hate, says the Lord Almighty.

*Prokeimenon, Tone 3:*
Sing praises unto our God, sing praises; sing praises unto our King, sing praises.
*Verse: Clap your hands, all ye nations.*

*And all the rest, even as was indicated for Cheesefare Wednesday.*

*It should be known:*[^145]
*That on Saturday and Sunday of Cheesefare the Menaion is not chanted; but the service of the occurring saints is chanted at Compline, or whenever the superior wills.*

## CHEESEFARE SATURDAY

*We perform the commemoration of all holy, venerable, and God-bearing Fathers who shone forth in ascetic struggle.*[^146]

*On Friday evening at Lucernarium, after the introductory psalm, the customary psalmody: "Unto the Lord when I was afflicted:"*

*At "Lord, I have cried," we chant prosomoia stichera, setting 6 verses.*
*Tone 8, repeating twice:*
Come, all ye faithful, let us hymn the choirs of the venerable Fathers: Anthony the foremost, radiant Euthymius, and each and all together; and spiritually passing through their way of life as through another paradise of delight, beautifully let us cry aloud: "These are the trees which our God planted, these having blossomed forth the fruits of incorruptible life have offered them unto Christ, nourishing our souls;" unto whom let us cry: "Ye God-bearing blessed ones, pray that we may be saved!"[^147]

*Model:*
Rejoice, faithful Egypt; rejoice, venerable Libya; rejoice, chosen Thebaid; rejoice, every place and city and country that reared citizens of the kingdom of heaven, and nurtured them in abstinence and labors, and showed them forth unto God as men perfect in desires; these have appeared as luminaries of our souls; they themselves have shone forth spiritually unto all the ends of the earth by the radiance of miracles and the signs of deeds; unto them let us cry aloud: "All-blessed Fathers, pray that we may be saved!"[^148]

*Model:*
Who among the earthborn shall recount your marvelous lives, O ecumenical Fathers? And what tongue shall utter your sacred ascetic struggles in deed and your sweat, the sufferings of virtues, the mortifications of the flesh, the wrestlings with passions, in vigils, in prayers, and in tears? Ye truly appeared in the world as Angels; ye yourselves utterly cast down demonic powers, having performed marvelous and astounding signs; therefore pray with us, O Most Blessed ones, that we may obtain unending joy.

*Glory, Tone 6:*
Having preserved that which is according to the image unharmed, ascetically setting the mind as ruler over ruinous passions, ye ascended as far as possible unto that which is according to the likeness; for manfully compelling nature, ye were diligent to subject the worse unto the better, and to enslave the flesh unto the spirit; therefore ye appeared as the summit of monastics, desert dwellers, trainers of those running well, most exact rules of virtue, and now in the heavens, the mirrors having been dissolved, O all-venerable ones, ye purely behold the Holy Trinity, praying directly for those who honor you with faith and love.[^149]

*Now and ever, Theotokion of Tone 1, of the Octoechos for the day: "O Gladsome Light:"*

*Prokeimenon, Tone 7:*
God, Thou art my defender, and Thy mercy shall go before me.
*Verse: Deliver me from mine enemies, O God, and redeem me from them that rise up against me.*

*Reading from the Prophecy of Zechariah (Chapter 8):*[^150]
**Reader:** Thus says the Lord Almighty: The fast of the fourth month, and the fast of the fifth, and the fast of the seventh, and the fast of the tenth, shall be to the house of Judah joy and gladness, and cheerful feasts; therefore rejoice, and love truth and peace. Thus says the Lord Almighty: Yet shall there come many people, and inhabitants of many cities: and the inhabitants of five cities shall come together into one city, saying: Let us go to pray before the face of the Lord, and to seek the face of the Lord Almighty; I will go also. Yea, many people and strong nations shall come to seek the face of the Lord Almighty in Jerusalem, and to pray before the face of the Lord. Thus says the Lord Almighty: In those days ten men shall take hold out of all languages of the nations, even shall take hold of the skirt of him that is a Jew, saying: We will go with you, for we have heard that God is with you.

*Prokeimenon, Tone 6:*
Let Israel hope in the Lord, from henceforth and unto the ages.
*Verse: Lord, my heart is not exalted, neither have mine eyes been lifted up.*

*Vouchsafe, O Lord, this evening:*

*At the Aposticha, the Idiomelon, Tone 2:*
Let us cleanse ourselves, brethren, from all defilement of flesh and spirit; let us enlighten the lamps of our souls through love of the poor, not devouring one another with slander; for the time has drawn near when the Bridegroom will come to reward all according to their deeds; let us enter with Christ with the wise virgins, seeking that voice of the thief unto Him: "Remember us, O Lord, when Thou comest into Thy kingdom."[^151]

*And we say the verses:*
*Verse: Unto Thee have I lifted up mine eyes:*
*And again the same idiomelon.*
*Then the verse: Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us:*
*And the Martyrion:*
As the holy martyrs pray for us and hymn Christ, every deceit has ceased, and mankind is saved through faith.

*Glory, Tone 8:*
The multitudes of monastics honor you today as instructors, O venerable Fathers: for through you we have known how to walk the truly straight path; blessed are ye who have labored for Christ and cast down the power of the enemy, companions of Angels, fellow-dwellers with the righteous and the saints: with whom pray ye unto the Lord, that our souls may find mercy.

*Now and ever, Theotokion.*

*Model: "O marvelous wonder:"*
Rejoice, treasure of purity; rejoice, pure dwelling of immaterial light; rejoice, principal cause of our salvation; rejoice, preaching of the Apostles; rejoice, praise of the martyrs; rejoice, fulfillment of the prophets, O all-immaculate one; rejoice, adornment of ascetics and monastics, and salvation of the faithful.

*Then: "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart:" And after the Trisagion we say the Troparion, Tone 4:*
O God of our fathers, Who dealest ever with us according to Thy meekness, remove not Thy mercy from us; but by their supplications direct our life in peace.

*Glory, and now and ever:*
*Theotokion, the same Tone: "The mystery hidden from all ages:"*
*We say the same also at "God is the Lord," and at the end of Matins.*
*After this, the litany: "Have mercy on us, O God:" and 3 great prostrations.*
**"Blessed be the name of the Lord:"** *thrice.* **"I will bless the Lord:"**
*"It is truly meet:" and the Dismissal. And the meal takes place according to custom, even as was indicated for Cheesefare Wednesday.*
*At Compline we chant the regular dead canon of the tone, in the cemetery chapel.*[^152]

*On Cheesefare Saturday at Matins, after the Six Psalms and the first psalmody of the kathisma, Sessional hymns, Tone 8.*
*Model: "That which was commanded secretly:"*
Illumined by our fathers' prayers, entering now as into a fair paradise, let us delight in the torrent of sweetness; and gazing in awe upon their valor, let us emulate their virtues, seeking the Savior: by their prayers, O God, make us partakers of Thy kingdom.

*Glory, model:*
With one accord let us all hymn Paul, the leader of monastics, with wise Anthony and Euthymius, together with the rest of the Fathers; and let us entreat them, that they may unceasingly pray unto Christ for us who celebrate their divine and all-radiant memory, glorifying the Savior and Lord in hymns.[^153]

*Now and ever, Theotokion. Model:*
We give thanks unto thee, O Ever-Virgin, and we magnify thee, O pure one, and we worship thee, hymning thy Childbearing, O Full of grace, crying out unceasingly: save us, O all-merciful Virgin, as thou art good, and snatch us from fearful demonic dispute at the hour of trial, that we thy servants may not be put to shame.

*After the 2nd psalmody of the kathisma, Sessional hymn, Tone 4. Model: "Speedily of pastoral:"*
Together let us all praise in hymns Anthony and Euthymius with all the rest of the God-bearing Fathers, celebrating their memory; for they pray unto the Lord for the whole world, that we may be delivered from the ancient curse, being set free from torment.

*Glory:*
*Another Sessional hymn, Tone 8. Model: "That which was commanded:"*
Passing about among the God-bearing ascetics as in a blossoming paradise of virtues, we are filled with sweet fragrance; for by sufferings of assaulting temptations, they servilely subjected the body unto the spirit through abstinence, having lived an angelic life on earth; therefore they were accounted worthy of glory.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*
By the prayers of Thine incorporeal ministers, O Christ, of Thy Forerunner, disciples, prophets, and martyrs, of all the saints and the venerable ones, besought by Thine unwedded and holy Mother: grant us to walk in Thy light, and make us worthy to attain Thy Kingdom, for the sake of the riches of Thy mercy.

*Then we read in Saint Ephrem the words concerning the departed Fathers, at page 203. Psalm 50. Canon of the holy patron of the monastery to 6; and of the saints to 8. We chant the stichologia, and sing unto the Lord:*

*Ode 1, Tone 8. Heirmos: Let us send up a song, O ye peoples:*

All of us in spiritual songs, let us with one accord praise our divine Fathers who shone forth in ascetical struggles: whom Egypt, the Thebaid, and Libya brought forth, every place, city, and land.[^154]

Rejoice, Anthony most glorious, first instructor of monastics; God-bearing Ammon, glory of Nitria; and Arsenius the angel, stronghold of silence; Pachomius bearer of the Spirit.[^155]

In truth the vessel of God, Agathon, is adorned in holy beauty: Achillas and Ammon, flowers cut down; Poemen and Paësius; Pambo and Isaiah, radiant pearls of the virtues.[^156]

Beacons of discernment unto us, the one indeed the marvelous Heras, and the great Dioscorus; and of obedience the radiant Zeno and Acacius; with whom Isaac shines forth together as a certain morning star.

As a mountain of lofty life appeared Apsinthius, and the struggler of purity the great Abraham; with whom Aphrodisius, a pillar of continence, appeared with Athenodorus.

Ammonius shines as a star in heaven among the ascetics, and the divine Ischyrion; and with these the great Antiochus shines, and Agapitus the mighty, and whosoever else blazes forth with them.

With siren songs let us praise the great Athanasius, who fasted radiantly on Mount Idion, the great luminary of the whole universe, by whose prayers we all are saved.[^157]

Ye have appeared in truth, O most wise Fathers, as an Eden of God-adorned life for the Church; having shown forth all according to name, offer up unceasing prayer unto the Lord for us.

*Martyrikon:*
Come, faithful lovers of the martyrs, let us honor the martyrs with honorable songs and chants, singing and crying out with faith unto Christ our God: Let us sing unto Thee, the only Master.

*Glory, Triadikon:*
Three consubstantial Persons I hymn, of one essence: the unbegotten Father, the begotten Son, and the Holy Spirit; one unoriginate Kingdom, dominion, and Godhead.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*
Rejoice, all-holy temple, bedewed fleece, sealed fountain of the stream of immortality; preserve thy city, O Lady, unshaken from diverse adversaries.

*Heirmos:*
*Let us send up a song, O ye peoples, unto our marvelous God, Who freed Israel from bondage, singing a song of victory and crying aloud: We sing unto Thee, the only Master.*

*The second ode we do not chant in the Psalter, but we chant the refrain:*
*Venerable Fathers, pray to God for us.*

*Ode 2. Heirmos:*
*See, see that I am your God, born of the Father before the ages, and conceived in these latter times without a man from the Virgin, and having dissolved the sin of the forefather Adam, as Lover of mankind.*

We are filled now with the knowledge of God, running as into another paradise of the planted ascetic virtues: which blossomed forth in continence and tears, bearing diverse fruit of life unto God, O most venerable ones.

Great Hilarion, who lived a bird-like life as an angel, a new Job again, the steadfast Benjamin; but also Helladius the beacon, saving unto God the Master; and divine Eulogius, and glorious Bacchyllus with them let be hymned.[^158]

By the height of life, as an eagle wast thou, O Benedict! and the house of wisdom, the pastor Cassian; but also Bassian received a certain crown of obedience: for taking up his abode alive in the tomb, he shows unto us the radiance of obedience.[^159]

A hymn to Gelasius, this ever-memorable king of the passions; praise to Gerasimus, unto whom the wild beast was subject, for it came unto him for the perfection of his virtue; glory also to Father Germanus, with Gaius, wise servants of Christ.[^160]

The grandfather, glory and praise of Thessalonica, let the God-pleasing David be praised, great in miracles both in deed and word; Daniel of the Skete; and Dius and Dalmatus, chiefs of monastics, confirmation of the faith.[^161]

Subjection of the starlight, loving higher things, showed as two beacons shining unto us, the God-wise Dometian and Dometius; and with them let the nameless ones also be gloriously hymned.

*Martyrikon:*
The inexhaustible wealth of the faithful, who have taken in hand the reliquary of those who suffered for the sake of the Lord: come piously, ye faithful, let us praise them in martyr-like manner, receiving through faith the fruit of healing for souls and bodies.

*Glory, Triadikon:*
All-most-perfect Unity, transcendent in Godhead, in three hypostases, unbegotten Father, and only-begotten Son, Spirit proceeding from the Father, yet made manifest through the Son: one Essence and Nature, Dominion and Kingdom, save us all.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*
Thou alone didst bring a marvelous birth unto humanity; thou alone didst not render the mystery according to nature, having borne a seedless and incorruptible Childbearing; therefore as Birth-giver of God we faithful duly glorify thee, O pure Virgin.

*Katavasia: See, see:*

*Ode 3. Heirmos: There is none holy as the Lord:*

Entering into another paradise of the divine Fathers' virtues, tasting of the ever-bestowing, living delight of this flower, faithfully praising them.

Let Euthymius be honored, the most radiant star; Thalassius the morning star; Ephrem inspired by God, with mighty Eulogius, who by deeds and miracles illumined the ends of the earth.[^162]

Let the marvelous Zosimas be sung with hymns, and all-honorable Zacharias, and Zenon, and Zoilus; and let great Isaiah and glorious Elijah be honored with them.

I hymn all-glorious Theodore of Therme, and all-lauded Ennathas; and with them Theodulus, crying aloud with Theonas, and I honor marvelous and great Theodosius.[^163]

Praised be Theoctistus, the most excellent shepherd, and lofty Thalassius; and great Theodore called the Sykeote, who was revealed as lofty upon the earth through signs and wonders.[^164]

Other stars shine forth: again the most radiant cluster, John, with three light-bearers in the Ladder, and with Chariton the angels, who shone forth gloriously.[^165]

*Martyrikon:*
Let us honor with songs and spiritual hymns, having assembled, O ye who love the feasts, the all-honorable and annual memory of the martyrs: for they pray unceasingly unto Christ for our race.

*Glory, Triadikon:*
O consubstantial Trinity and super-divine Unity, union in division, and possessing one nature across the persons: unite us into the one desire of Thy commandments.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*
Moses described thee beforehand as the tabernacle fashioned by God, covered by the Seraphim, the Holy of Holies, prefiguring thy pure childbirth, O Virgin, when Christ was inscribed in the flesh.

*Heirmos:*
*There is none holy as the Lord, and none righteous as our God, Whom all creation hymns: there is none righteous beside Thee, O Lord.*

*Sessional hymn, Tone 5. Model: Speedily anticipate:*
As rays of the Sun of righteousness, Christ sent you forth, enlightening the earth, O holy teachers; therefore by your divine prayers enlighten with the divine light of the knowledge of God my soul darkened by wickedness, O God-blessed ones.

*Another Sessional hymn, Tone 8. Model: Of Wisdom:*
The meekness and purity of Anthony, the greatness and marvel of Euthymius, the simplicity and stillness of Paul and Arsenius, the glory of Theoctistus, and the ranks of all the other venerable ones, let us faithful glorify and together extol in songs, and with them Euphrasia the virgin let us sing with all the God-wise women, and with one accord cry aloud: Pray ye unto Christ God, that He grant remission of transgressions unto those who celebrate your holy memory with love.[^166]

*Glory, model:*
Having loosed the bonds of passions, ye were joined unto the love of the Master, and in Christ were clothed in transcendent glory, finding rest from your labors, having attained the higher life through the labors of abstinence; therefore ye worthily rejoice eternally with the heavenly powers, O our God-bearing Fathers; entreat remission of sins for those who celebrate your holy memory with love.

*Now and ever, Theotokion. Model:*
I have sunk into the mire of sins, and there is no standing in me; terribly hath the tempest of my transgressions overwhelmed me; but as thou hast borne the Word, the only Lover of mankind, look upon me thy servant, I pray thee, deliver me from sin and soul-corrupting passions, and from every affliction of the avenger, O Lady, that rejoicing I may sing: Pray unto Christ God, to grant me remission of transgressions, for thee have I thy servant as my hope.

*Ode 4. Heirmos: From the overshadowing mountain, O Word:*

A beacon pouring forth myrrh is the divine Hilarion, a spiritual mountain the great Hesychius; with them let Hierax be honored, and Icnesion the eminently glorious, with Joseph.

And Jeremiah shone forth in life, and Ischyrion was revealed as great strength; with them shines Carion, Copres, Castor, Cassian, most noble through the ages.

I marvel at the blessings of Callistus, I praise the good deeds of Laurence, and the beneficence of Longinus I extol; I honor the virtues of Lotus.

I hymn Leucius, the initiate of theology; and I praise Maximus, an abyss of teachings; Marcian the ornament, and Mark the well-obedient and God-hearkening.[^167]

The honor of the virtues, great Macarius; and of the city's piety, Jovian; with them is proclaimed Mark the mighty, and with Dalmatus, Moses the Ethiopian.[^168]

I magnify the courses and struggles of Martinian and Malachias for purity; and Marcellus the chief shepherd of virtue I honor, and Miles who raised the dead.[^169]

*Martyrikon:*
Martyrs of Christ, offer up unceasing prayers unto the Fashioner and Creator, for the peace of the world, and for those who honor your memory in songs.

*Glory, Triadikon:*
Strange it is that the Godhead is both one and three, entirely undivided in three Persons, for there is the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, worshiped in one nature.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*
Rejoice, spacious Dwelling of God; rejoice, Ark of the New Covenant; rejoice, holy Urn from which the super-heavenly Manna was given unto all men.

*Katavasia:*
*From the overshadowing mountain, O Word, the prophet, having perceived with divine vision that Thou wast to be incarnate of the only Birth-giver of God, with fear gave glory to Thy power.*

*Ode 5. Heirmos: The gloom of passions:*

Come, let us behold the ever-living flowers of Eden's paradise, the God-sprouted wonders of the Fathers, of which the Lord is the only Husbandman.

Every rational soul is watered by the verbal streams of Nilus; it shines with the lives of Naucratis and Nicon; and with Nathanael, Nistheron adorns them.[^170]

Xenophon with those who heard him was stamped with virtues and enlightens us, and great Porphyrius, and even more so Onuphrius: and who among earthborn men shall worthily utter their names?[^171]

Let Pambo both in deed and word be worthily blessed, as one lofty; and the continent in deacons, all-glorious Paphnutius, let bright Poemenphrius likewise be glorified.

With longsuffering let the truly all-glorious Paphnutius be honored; Pior, Patermuthius, Paul the Simple, and Pitirion the great and eminent Father.[^172]

Let Pachomius, the luminary among the radiant, be brightly praised; Palamon his fellow-sufferer, divine Petronius, and Patapius with them, let be sung in divine hymns.[^173]

*Glory, Triadikon:*
Three Hypostases, even if one Godhead by nature, in Whom we have been baptized and in Whom we believe: Father, Word, and co-essential Spirit.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*
O all-pure one who by the Word gavest birth unto the Word beyond all word, praying unto Him cease not to make entreaty, that thy flock may ever be delivered from perils.

*Katavasia:*
*The gloom of passions, as if from deep night delivering me, vouchsafe my spirit to keep morning vigil, I pray Thee, unto the light of the day of Thy commandments, O Christ.*

*Ode 6. Heirmos: Held fast am I, receive me:*

All-honorable Fathers our guides, whose are the divine sufferings, whose the roots, whose the healings: for who more than these hath shown the power of wonders?

Wonderful Rabbula, and Rufus together, and Sisoës together equal-to-angels let be praised, with whom are divine Eradius and Silvanus.[^174]

As a fourfold beacon appeared on earth the twice-two holy Simeon-kindred: three who are upon pillars, and one fool-for-Christ.[^175]

In the midst of the stars as the sun, among the leaders holy Sabbas shone forth, with whom Serapion also illumines by deeds, together with Silvanus.[^176]

Sarmatas, Timothy, Tithes together with Hyperechius, and Pharmuthius, Phocas, Chariton, Chaeremon, Psoes let be sung, and Hor the most wise.[^177]

Holy and glorious company of the Fathers, both remembered and nameless, deliver from perils those who celebrate your memory with love.

*Glory, Triadikon:*
Thee, O unoriginate Trinity and divine Unity, Light and Lights I hymn, Life and Lives: Mind, Word, and Holy Spirit, and Holy, the One God.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*
From thy root sprouted the Flower of life; leap for joy, O righteous Jesse: Christ God, Who saves the world from the pure Maiden.

*Heirmos:*
*Held fast am I by many sins, receive me, O Lover of mankind, falling down before Thy compassions, as the prophet, O Lord, and save me.*

*Kontakion, Tone 8. Model: As firstfruits:*
As preachers of piety and muzzlers of impiety, Thou hast made radiant the council of the God-bearers who enlighten the inhabited earth; in perfect peace preserve, through their prayers, those who praise and magnify Thee, who sing unto Thee, O Lord: Alleluia.

*Ikos:*
Looking upon the fair lives, contemplating in thoughts that which has come to pass, and measuring their afflictions, I lamented the life of men; and which ones alone I called blessed: those who chose the good portion, to desire Christ, and to abide with Him, and to sing unceasingly with the Prophet David: Alleluia.

*Synaxarion.*
*Verses:*
To the righteous souls whose memory ever abides,
I offer words as sacrifices of praise.

On this day we celebrate the memory of all the saints who have shone forth in ascetic fasting, both men and women: for since the God-bearing Fathers, having instructed us through the introductory feasts, prepared us beforehand for the stadium, having removed us from luxury and satiety, and having admonished us with fear of the future judgment, and having duly pre-purified us through Cheesefare Week, gracefully set two periods of fasting in the midst, that little by little they might lead us unto it. Lo, also all the venerable ones who lived thus, and in other manners, through many afflictions and labors, both men and women together, they set before us in the midst: that through the memory of their struggles they might make us stronger for the stadium, having their life as a certain pattern and way. And that receiving from them assistance and help, we may be drawn unto spiritual struggles, considering that they also shared the same nature with us. For even as commanders encourage their armed hosts already standing in battle array, by words, examples, and commemorations of ancient men who fought eminently and acted valiantly, and thereby being fortified, the soldiers arm themselves with whole soul in the hope of victory: so also now the God-bearing Fathers wisely act: by those who lived venerably in the male and female sex, fortifying us for spiritual struggles, they thus go before unto the stadium of fasting, that looking upon their archetypal, unenvious life, we may work diverse and manifold virtues, as each has strength. Having love as our forerunner, and that which occurs with understanding, the turning away from dishonorable deeds and actions. And this fast is not of foods only, but also of the tongue, and of anger, of the eyes, and simply to speak, cessation and estrangement from every evil. For this reason the holy Fathers instituted here the present commemoration of all the saints, instructing us by the presentation of those who pleased God by fasting and other good deeds, by the example of these unto the stadium of the virtues, and to arm ourselves valiantly against the passions and against demons: and setting forth a certain pattern, that if we also offer equal diligence unto them, there shall be no obstacle to accomplish all that they also accomplished, and to be accounted worthy of the same honors: for these also shared the same nature with us. And concerning the eating of cheese, some say that Emperor Heraclius instituted this, having previously been observed in few places: for having waged war against Chosroes and the Persians for six years, the Emperor promised unto God that if he should prevail over them, he would propose this, and leave it in the midst between fasting and food, which he also did. But I deem rather that even if this occurred, it was also devised by the holy Fathers for the sake of a certain pre-purification, that being led from meats and much eating straightway into extreme non-eating, we might not be terrified. And in another manner, we are harmed by bodily custom, but having gently and little by little instructed us, and holding us back from delicacies, like unbridled horses running unto food, we may receive the bridle of the Fast. For as they did with parables concerning the soul, so also they prudently ordered concerning the body, cutting off little by little the stumbling blocks unto the Fast. By the prayers of all Thy venerable ones, O Christ our God, have mercy on us. Amen.

*Ode 7. Heirmos: The Hebrew children:*

Come, let us duly offer hymns unto the women who lived venerably and equal-to-the-angels, by whose prayers let us cry aloud: O God, save us all.

Christ-bearing Bryaene, with divine Febronia let be honored, and with Thomaïs and Heria; and let Platonis be sung, and with them Melania the faithful.[^178]

Unto angel-minded Euphrasia, with the two Theodoras and the all-wealthy Anastasias, praise, singing, and unceasing glory, who wonderfully served God.[^179]

Mary the Egyptian, a light in the world; and she who was named Marinus appeared as a star to the universe; Euphrosyne, a sun radiating with virtues.[^180]

Theodula who cast herself into fire in her life; and in fasting Theodote and Isaura shine forth, and Isidora all-wealthy radiates with deeds.[^181]

Let Marina the heavenly-minded again be honored, with great Matrona; and Syncletica and Sarah, with Justina, as wise let be praised with songs.[^182]

Pelagia, the angel of the Lord; Thaïs, luminary of repentance, let be sung; and if any other woman shone forth in ascetic fasting.[^183]

*Glory, Triadikon:*
With the Son we worship the Father, and the Holy Spirit, glorifying with one mind, crying aloud in faith: Glory to Thee, Trinity, Unity, our God.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*
Birth-giver of God, Virgin who bore the Savior and Master of the world, O blessed one: entreat Him ever to make wise our souls.

*Katavasia:*
*The Hebrew children in the furnace, and Thou Who didst change the flame into dew, who bore Thee after childbirth: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers.*

*Ode 8. Heirmos: On the holy mountain:*

Shepherds and wise teachers, hierarchs of Christ's Church, with the venerable ones let us all hymn, singing unto the Lord and exalting Him unto all ages.

Duly let Basil the Great and with him truly much-suffering Athanasius be sung in hymns, with Gregory who is first in theology among all.[^184]

The golden-speaking mouth of John, with the Cyrils the God-wise pillars let us glorify, and likewise Hesychius the second theologian, with the age-marvelous and divine Meletius.[^185]

Glory to Gregory of Nyssa, with the two wonderworking Fathers; and let most wise, divine Epiphanius, with Amphilochius the bright beacons, be sung unto the ages.[^186]

The glory of priests Metrophanes, with Nectarius, Atticus, Gennadius, and with them let us hymn Anatolius, the living beacons, together with Eusebius and Proclus the most wise.[^187]

Nicholas the holy preacher, Sophronius truly honey-tongued, with Eulalius I hymn; and Diadochus together with Eustathius and Euphecalius, fathers of the Church.[^188]

*We bless the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, the Lord.*

*Triadikon:*
As Unity in essence I hymn Thee, as Trinity in Persons I honor Thee, O Father, Son, and all-holy Spirit: the unoriginate dominion of Thy Kingdom I glorify unto the ages.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*
Thou hast appeared as the Mountain of God, O Birth-giver of God, in which Christ having dwelt, made those who sing divine temples: Sing unto the Lord, and exalt Him unto all the ages.

*We praise, we bless, we worship the Lord:*

*Katavasia:*
*Unto Him Who was glorified on the holy mountain, and in the bush revealed unto Moses by fire the mystery of the Ever-Virgin: sing unto the Lord, and exalt Him unto all the ages.*

*And More honorable than the Cherubim is chanted:*

*Ode 9. Heirmos: That which was manifested on the mountain to the lawgiver:*

Who shall declare the boldness of Ambrose? And how shall one utter the wisdom of Hierotheus, and of these God-wise Alexanders the steadfastness in faith?[^189]

Divine Felix, God-bearing Spyridon, with Antipater, Pambo, Palladius and Nonnus, Jerome and all-honorable Germanus, let be hymned as divine beacons.[^190]

Great Dionysius among the divine let be honored, as an initiate of heavenly mysteries; much-suffering Clement, Flavian, and great Paul, the first preachers of the confession.[^191]

Let Michael of Synnada be sung with Tarasius; Nicephorus again with Theodore most earnestly; and Theophanes of sacred name in truth, defenders of Christ's icons.[^192]

Peter and Ignatius truly God-bearers, as Christ's Apostles and hieromartyrs, let be sung together with Polycarp and Cyprian the Christ-martyrs.[^193]

Venerable Fathers and sacred rulers of the Lord, with the hieromartyrs and holy women, all ye named and unnamed, pray that our souls may be saved.

*Glory, Triadikon:*
One God in Trinity, glory to Thee unceasingly: for though each is God, yet art Thou one by nature: Father, Son, and Spirit, in three-rayed properties.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*
The bush burning with fire and unconsumed, Moses foresaw of old on Mount Sinai: thy God-receiving womb, O Virgin, receiving the unconsumed fire.

*Katavasia:*
*That which was manifested on the mountain to the lawgiver in fire and the bush, the Childbearing of the Ever-Virgin for the salvation of us the faithful, with unceasing hymns we magnify.*

*Exapostilarion. Model: Give ear, ye women:*
Having renounced the world and taken up the cross, O multitude of venerable Fathers, with the choirs of martyrs, assembly of hierarchs, and company of women: make us glad, that we may worthily sing your all-radiant memory.

*Glory, and now and ever: Model: With the disciples let us ascend:*
The God-bearing Fathers who shone forth in asceticism, and the chief hierarchs, together with the venerable women, and choirs of hieromartyrs, in hymns let us brightly extol: that being enlightened both by their supplications and the prayers of the Birth-giver of God, we may easily complete the course of the Fast.

*At the Praises we set 4 stichera, and chant stichera, Tone 8. Model: In Eden a paradise:*

All the multitude of the Fathers who have fasted rightly, let us faithful magnify in hymns, and the hierarchs of Christ let us praise in songs, God-wisely with one accord, O brethren; for they lived in continence and in holy fasting, and clarified for us the Gospel of Christ; with them let us sing of the God-bearing and bright women, zealously emulating their life in the soul: that we may find forgiveness of transgressions there.

Those who have shone forth brightly in asceticism, and have lived venerably, let us praise gloriously, O brethren: as having lived well, and having piously passed over unto joy in eternal life: unto the imperishable and blessed rest; having run thither rightly in virtue and honesty, let us worthily honor them, that we may obtain mercy from God by their supplication, and eternal glory and joy: and be delivered from inexorable torments there.

Ranks of all hierarchs, assembly of the righteous, of ascetics and venerable women who lived piously: besought by grace, pray ye the only Good and all-compassionate Lord, to make us also wise: that we also may be delivered from condemnation there by your prayers, O wise ones, and may enjoy future reception, rejoicing unceasingly unto ages of ages, unceasingly seeking a song of praise unto the Giver of life.

Having kindled a divine celebration today, ye faithful, abundantly in the memory of the saints, hierarchs, and ascetics, hieromartyrs, venerable women, and the pious: for such temporary things they truly despised, and counted them as cobwebs and as dung: that they might gain Christ, and His kingdom, and those divine things which eye hath not seen, nor ear ever heard; by whose prayers, O God, deliver our souls from corruption.[^194]

*Glory, idiomelon, Tone 6:*
Venerable Fathers, into all the earth went forth the proclamation of your righteous deeds; therefore in the heavens ye found the reward of your labors: having destroyed the demonic host, ye attained the angelic ranks: whose blameless life having emulated, having boldness before the Lord, ask peace for our souls.[^195]

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*
O Virgin Birth-giver of God, thou art the true vine:

*The Great Doxology. And the Dismissal.*

*At the Liturgy, the Typika. And from the canon, Ode 3 and 6. Prokeimenon of the Epistle, Tone 7: The venerable ones shall boast in glory, and shall rejoice upon their beds. Verse: The high praises of God shall be in their throat. Epistle of the day, to the Romans, section 115 (Rom. 14:19–26). Another, of the venerable ones, to the Galatians, section 213 (Gal. 5:22–6:2).
