Even as the angelic ranks now in heaven, and with fear the assemblies of men upon earth, we offer the song of victory unto Thee, O Good One: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, our God, by the prayers of all Thy saints have mercy on us!

*Both now:*
Daring to glorify in Cherubic manner Thine unoriginate Father, and Thee, O Christ God, and Thy Most Holy Spirit, we say: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, our God, through the Theotokos have mercy on us!

*Exaposteilarion, Tone 4:*
O Thou that causest light to shine upon Thy world, cleanse my soul that is in darkness from every sin: *(Add:)* and save me!

*[Ornamental Divider Band]*

*Trinity Hymns, Tone 5:*
It is the time for singing and the hour for prayer; fervently let us cry aloud unto the One God: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, our God! *(Add:)*

*Glory:*
Daring to depict Thy spiritual hosts, O unoriginate Trinity, with unworthy lips we cry aloud: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, our God, by the prayers of all Thy saints have mercy on us!

*Both now:*
O Thou Who wast contained in the virginal womb and wast not separated from the Father's bosom, receive us also, O Christ God, who cry unto Thee with the Angels: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, our God, through the Theotokos have mercy on us!

*Exaposteilarion, Tone 5:*
O Giver of Light, O Lord, send down Thy light, and enlighten my heart: *(Add:)* and save me!

*[Ornamental Divider Band]*

*Trinity Hymns, Tone 6:*
The Cherubim standing before Thee with fear, and the Seraphim trembling with dread, offer the Thrice-Holy Hymn with unceasing voice; with them also we sinners cry aloud: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, our God! *(Add:)*

*Glory:*
With bodiless lips and unceasing glorifications the six-winged cry aloud unto Thee the Thrice-Holy Hymn, O our God; and we upon earth send up praise unto Thee with unworthy lips: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, our God, by the prayers of all Thy saints have mercy on us!

*Both now:*
The Godhead of the Trinitarian Unity we glorify in unconfused union, and we cry aloud the angelic hymn: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, our God, through the Theotokos have mercy on us!

*Exaposteilarion, Tone 6: on Monday:*
By the intercessions of Thy bodiless hosts, O Lord, send down Thy co-eternal Light upon our souls!

*Here in the Sixth Tone, at the beginning of the Exaposteilarion, instead of "By the intercessions of Thy bodiless hosts, O Lord: and the rest,"*
*If it be Tuesday, it is said thus:*
By the prayers of Thy Forerunner, O Lord: *and recite the rest unto the end.*

*On Wednesday and Friday, instead of "By the intercessions of Thy bodiless hosts, O Lord,"*
*At the beginning say thus:*
By the power of Thy Cross, O Lord, send down Thy co-eternal Light upon our souls!

*And on Thursday thus:*
By the prayers of Thy holy Apostles, O Lord, and of the Hierarch Nicholas, send down Thy co-eternal Light upon our souls!

*At the second, on "Glory", say at the beginning of the Exaposteilarion:*
By the prayers of all the saints, O Lord, send down Thy co-eternal Light upon our souls!

*And at the third, on "Both now", say at the beginning of the Exaposteilarion thus:*
By the prayers of the Theotokos, O Lord, send down Thy co-eternal Light upon our souls!

*[Ornamental Divider Band]*

*Trinity Hymns, Tone 7:*
Hymned by the Higher Power in Cherubic manner, and worshipped with divine glory in Angelic manner, receive us also upon earth who send up praise unto Thee with unworthy lips: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, our God! *(Add:)*

*Glory:*
Putting away sluggishness like sleep, O my soul, show forth amendment unto praise before the Judge, and cry aloud with fear: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, our God, by the prayers of all Thy saints have mercy on us!

*Both now:*
Sending up the Seraphic Thrice-Holy Praise unto the Inaccessible Godhead in the Trinity as Unity, with fear let us cry aloud: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, our God, through the Theotokos have mercy on us!

*Exaposteilarion, Tone 7:*
Raise me up, O Lord, unto Thy hymnody, and teach me to do Thy will, O Holy One, *(Add:)* and save me!

*[Ornamental Divider Band]*

*Trinity Hymns, Tone 8:*
Having our hearts on high, let us emulate the angelic rank, and with fear let us fall down before the Judge, seeking after the song of victory: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, our God! *(Add:)*

*Glory:*
Not daring to gaze upon Thee, the Cherubim fly, crying aloud with exultation the divine song of the Thrice-Holy voice; with them also we cry unto Thee: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, our God, by the prayers of all Thy saints have mercy on us!

*Both now:*
Bent down by the multitude of our transgressions, and not daring to look up unto the height of heaven, bowing soul and body, with the Angels we cry the hymn unto Thee: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, our God, through the Theotokos have mercy on us!

*Exaposteilarion, Tone 8:*
Being Light, O Christ, enlighten me through Thyself: *(Add:)* and save me!

*[Woodcut Headpiece Band: Intricate foliate lace ornament.]*

*COMPUNCTIVE STICHERA*[^1244]

*Chanted on Sunday evening, at "Lord, I have cried": and the Sessional Hymns, with the Martyria, chanted at Matins; unto this also the Praises Stichera, with those at the Aposticha, chanted on Saturdays, from the Oktoechos, according to the Tone.*

*At "Lord, I have cried", Penitential Stichera, Tone 1:*
Great is the abyss of my transgressions, O Savior, and grievously am I submerged by mine iniquities; reach out Thy hand unto me, as unto Peter, and save me, O God, and have mercy on me!

Seeing that in wicked thoughts and in deeds Thou hast condemned me, O Savior, grant me the thought of repentance, O God, that I may cry unto Thee: Save me, O Good Benefactor, and have mercy on me!

Another age awaits thee, O my soul, and the Judge desires to expose thy secret and grievous deeds; remain not therefore in the things of this world, but anticipate the judgment, crying aloud unto the Judge: O God, cleanse me and save me!

Despise me not, O my Savior, who am held fast by sinful sloth; raise up my thoughts unto repentance, and show me to be an approved laborer of Thy vineyard, granting me the reward of the eleventh hour, and great mercy!

*Then three from the Triodion, and three for the Saint from the Menaion.*

*ON MONDAY AT MATINS*
*After the first stichology, Compunctive Sessional Hymns, Tone 1:*
In iniquities was I conceived, prodigal that I am, and I dare not look up unto the height of heaven; yet daring upon Thy love for mankind, I cry: O God, cleanse me and save me!

*Verse: O Lord, rebuke me not in Thine anger, nor chasten me in Thy wrath.*[^1245]
If the righteous scarcely be saved, where shall I appear, a sinner? I have not borne the burden and the heat of the day; yet number me with the laborers of the eleventh hour, O God, and save me!

*Glory, both now, Theotokion:*
Beholding in thee the miracle of miracles, O Full of Grace, the creation rejoices; for thou hast conceived without seed, and hast given birth ineffably unto Him Whom the ranks of Angels cannot behold: Him, O Theotokos, entreat for our souls!

*At the Sixth Ode, the Martyricon is said, if the Menaion hath no kontakion; but if it hath one, this is said together with the sessional hymns.*
*Martyricon, Tone 1:*
With the praise of suffering and with the honor of crowns, the glorious passion-bearers have been clothed by Thee, O Lord; for by the endurance of wounds they vanquished the lawless, and by divine power received victory from heaven: by their prayers grant us, O God, Thy great mercy!

*Tone 1.*

*ON TUESDAY AT MATINS*

*After the first stichology, Compunctive Sessional Hymns, Tone 1:*

Haste Thou to open Thy Fatherly embrace unto me, for prodigally have I spent my life, looking upon the inexhaustible wealth of Thy compassions, O Savior; despise not now my heart grown poor, for unto Thee, O Lord, in compunction do I cry: I have sinned against heaven and before Thee!

*Verse: O Lord, rebuke me not in Thine anger, nor chasten me in Thy wrath.*[^1246]

Thy judgment seat is fearful, and Thy judgment is just, and my deeds are grievous; but do Thou Thyself, O Merciful One, anticipate and save me, and deliver me from torment; rescue me, O Master, from the portion of the goats, and count me worthy to stand at Thy right hand, O most righteous Judge!

*Glory, both now, Theotokion:*

Having conceived without being consumed the Fire of the Godhead, and having given birth without seed unto the Lord, the Fountain of life: O Full of Grace, Theotokos, save those who magnify thee!

*At the Sixth Ode, Martyricon:*

As noble soldiers, of one mind having believed, not having feared the threats of the tyrants, O holy ones, ye approached eagerly unto Christ, taking up the precious Cross, and having finished your course, ye received victory from heaven: glory to Him Who strengthened you; glory to Him Who crowned you; glory to Him Who through you works healings for all!

*ON WEDNESDAY AT MATINS*

*After the first stichology, Cross Sessional Hymns, Tone 1:*

The weapon of the Cross in battles was shown forth of old unto the pious Emperor Constantine as an invincible victory over enemies for the sake of the faith, at which the adverse powers tremble; this has become salvation unto the faithful, and the boast of Paul.

*Verse: Exalt ye the Lord our God, and worship the footstool of His feet, for He is holy.*[^1247]

*The same verse is also said on Friday:*

Before the Tree of Thy Cross do we bow down, O Lover of mankind, for upon it wast Thou nailed, O Life of all; Thou hast opened paradise, O Savior, unto the thief who approached Thee with faith, and hast accounted that penitent worthy of delight, who confessed unto Thee: "Remember me, O Lord!" Receive also us as that thief, who cry aloud: We all have sinned; in Thy tender compassion despise us not!

*Glory, both now, Stavrotheotokion:*

Beholding upon the Tree the Lamb, enduringly crucified with two thieves, Thee, O Word, and pierced in the ribs with a spear, the Ewe-lamb cried out, weeping with motherly voice: What is this strange and terrible mystery, O my Savior? How does a tomb cover the uncontainable God? Unspeakable is that which is accomplished; forsake me not who bore Thee, O my sweetest Son!

*At the Sixth Ode, Martyricon:*

By the sufferings of the saints which they endured for Thy sake, be Thou entreated, O Lord, and heal all our sicknesses, O Lover of mankind, we pray Thee!

*Sessional Hymns of the Oktoechos*

*ON THURSDAY AT MATINS*

*After the first stichology, Apostles' Sessional Hymns, Tone 1:*

By the net of the word, casting apart the rhetorical intricacies of the philosophers with the rod of the Cross, the fishermen enlightened the nations in piety to glorify Thee, the true God; therefore unto Thee Who didst strengthen them do we cry aloud: Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and glory to the consubstantial Spirit; glory unto Him Who through them enlightened the world!

*Verse: Their sound has gone forth into all the earth, and their words unto the ends of the world.*[^1248]

O most wise fishers of the universe, having received mercy from God, pray now for us who cry aloud: O Lord, save the Emperor,[^1249] and Thy city, and deliver our souls through the Apostles from the afflictions that encompass us!

*Glory, both now, Theotokion:*

Him Who in heaven is without a mother, beyond thought and hearing, upon earth hast thou borne without a father; Him, O Theotokos, entreat for our souls!

*At the Sixth Ode, Martyricon:*

O martyrs of Christ, we all entreat you, for they pray for our salvation; and let us all approach unto them with faith; these pour forth the grace of healings, these drive away the legions of demons, as guardians of the faith.

*ON FRIDAY AT MATINS*

*After the first stichology, Cross Sessional Hymns, Tone 1:*

When Thou wast crucified, O Christ, tyranny was destroyed, and the enemy's power was trampled down; for neither an Angel nor a man, but Thou Thyself, O Lord, hast saved us: glory to Thee!

*Verse: Exalt ye the Lord our God, and worship the footstool of His feet, for He is holy.*

The weapon of the Cross in battles was shown forth of old unto the pious Emperor Constantine as an invincible victory over enemies for the sake of the faith, at which the adverse powers tremble; this has become salvation unto the faithful, and the boast of Paul.

*Glory, both now, Stavrotheotokion:*

Having thine intercession, O Most Pure One, and by thy prayers being delivered from grievous ills, guarded everywhere by the Cross of thy Son, as is our duty we all piously magnify thee!

*At the Sixth Ode, Martyricon:*

With the praise of suffering:

*Written on Monday at Matins: (see fol. 456).*[^1250]

*Tone 1.*

*ON SATURDAY AT MATINS*

*At the Praises, Stichera of the Martyrs, Tone 1:*

Passion-bearers of Christ, come, all ye peoples, let us honor them with songs and spiritual hymns: the luminaries of the world and preachers of the faith, ever-flowing fountains whence healings flow forth unto the faithful; by their prayers, O Christ our God, grant peace unto Thy world, and unto our souls great mercy!

These soldiers of the Great King resisted the commands of the tyrants, valiantly took no account of tortures, and trampled down all delusion; having been worthily crowned, they ask of the Savior peace for our souls, and great mercy!

Neither tribulation, nor distress, nor famine, nor persecution, nor wounds, nor rage of wild beasts, nor sword, nor threatening fire were able to separate you from God, O all-praised martyrs; but through love toward Him, having striven as if in bodies not your own, ye forgot nature and despised death; therefore also worthily did ye receive the reward of your labors, having become heirs of the kingdom of heaven: pray ye unto Christ for our souls!

Rejoice in the Lord, O martyrs, for ye have fought the good fight; ye resisted kings, and vanquished tyrants; ye feared not fire nor sword, nor savage beasts that devoured your bodies; sending up hymnody unto Christ with the Angels, ye received crowns from heaven: ask that peace be granted unto the world, and unto our souls great mercy!

*Glory, for the Departed:*

In deed, O my Savior, dost Thou show forth that Thou art the Resurrection of all; by a word, O Word, Thou didst raise Lazarus from the dead, when the dead arose from their tombs, and the gates of Hades were shattered; then unto men death was shown to be sleep; but do Thou Who camest for the salvation of Thy creation and not for condemnation, give rest unto those whom Thou hast chosen, as the Lover of mankind!

*Both now, Theotokion:*

Rejoice from us, O holy Theotokos Virgin: pure vessel of the whole universe, unquenchable lamp, tabernacle of the Uncontainable One, undefiled church; rejoice, from whom was born the Lamb of God, Who takes away the sins of the whole world!

*At the Aposticha, Stichera for the Departed:*

*Tone 1, Podoben: "O All-Praised Martyrs" (Прехва́льнїи мч҃ницы):*

Unto Thee, O Savior, do we pray: vouchsafe those who have departed to partake of Thy sweetness, and settle them in the mansions of the righteous, together with Thy saints, and in heavenly habitations, in Thy tender compassion overlooking their transgressions, and granting them rest!

*Verse: Blessed are they whom Thou hast chosen and taken to Thyself, O Lord.*[^1251]

Higher than visible things are Thy promises, O Savior, which eye has not seen, nor ear heard, neither have they ever entered into the heart of man;[^1252] we pray Thee therefore, O Master, count those who have departed unto Thee worthy to obtain Thy sweet communion, and grant them life eternal!

*Sessional Hymns of the Oktoechos*

*Verse: Their souls shall dwell among good things.*[^1253]

Manifestly rejoicing in Thy Cross, in hope Thy servants have departed unto Thee, O Lover of mankind; unto them do Thou now grant Thy Cross and the Blood poured out for the life of the world as the redemption of their transgressions, in Thy tenderheartedness pardoning their falls into sin, and enlightening them with the light of Thy countenance!

*Verse: And their memory is from generation to generation.*[^1254]

No one is sinless, no one among men has ever been, save Thee alone, O Only Immortal One; therefore place Thy servants (as Thou art a compassionate God) in the light, together with Thine angelic choirs, in Thy tender compassion overlooking their iniquities, and granting them forgiveness!

*Glory, both now, Theotokion:*

Entreat Christ, Thine Offspring, O Virgin Mother, to grant forgiveness of transgressions unto thy servants who have piously proclaimed thee as Theotokos and been taught by the true word; account them worthy of the joy of the radiance of the saints in Thy kingdom!

*ON SUNDAY AT VESPERS*

*At "Lord, I have cried", Penitential Stichera, Tone 2:*

I have sinned against Thee, O Savior, as the prodigal son; receive me, O Father, as I repent, and have mercy on me, O God!

I cry unto Thee, O Christ Savior, with the voice of the publican: Cleanse me as him, and have mercy on me, O God!

Thinking upon the improper evils which I have committed, I flee unto Thy compassions, resembling the publican, and the harlot who wept, and the prodigal son; therefore also I fall down before Thee, O Merciful One: before Thou judgest me, spare me, O my God, and have mercy on me!

Overlook mine iniquities, O Lord Who wast born of the Virgin, and cleanse my heart, making it a temple for Thy Holy Spirit; cast me not away from Thy presence, Thou Who hast boundless and great mercy!

*Then three from the Triodion, and three for the Saint from the Menaion.*

*ON MONDAY AT MATINS*

*After the first stichology, Compunctive Sessional Hymns, Tone 2:*

As the waves of the sea have mine iniquities risen up against me, and like a small ship in the deep, I alone am tossed by a tempest of many transgressions; but guide me, O Lord, by repentance into the calm haven, and save me!

*Verse: O Lord, rebuke me not in Thine anger [nor chasten me in Thy wrath]:*[^1255]

I am a barren tree, O Lord, bringing forth no fruit of compunction whatsoever; and I fear the felling, and am terrified of that unquenchable fire; therefore I pray Thee: before that extremity, turn me and save me!

*Tone 2.*

*Glory, both now, Theotokion:*

Being the Fountain of tenderheartedness, count us worthy of compassion, O all-hymned Theotokos; look down upon a people that has sinned; show forth as ever thy power; for hoping in thee, we cry aloud unto thee: "Rejoice!" even as of old did Gabriel, the supreme commander of the bodiless hosts.

*At the Sixth Ode, Martyricon:*

Having Thee, Who dost clothe heaven with clouds, as their raiment in the world, the holy ones endured the torments of the lawless, and abolished the delusion of idols; by their prayers deliver us also from the invisible foe, O Savior, and save us!

*ON TUESDAY AT MATINS*

*After the first stichology, Compunctive Sessional Hymns, Tone 2:*

"Have mercy on me," said David, and I also cry unto Thee: I have sinned, O Savior; having cleansed my sins by repentance, have mercy on me!

*Verse: O Lord, rebuke me not in Thine anger [nor chasten me in Thy wrath]:*

Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me! For two sins did David weep:[^1256] yet for ten thousand transgressions do I cry unto Thee; he drenched his bed with tears, while I have not even a single drop; despairing, I pray: Have mercy on me, O God, according to Thy great mercy!

*Glory, both now, Theotokion:*

O Theotokos, despise me not who need thy protection; for in thee has my soul hoped: have mercy on me!

*At the Sixth Ode, Martyricon:*

Thou Who didst enlighten Thy holy ones more than gold, and didst glorify Thy venerable ones, in that Thou art Good: being entreated by them, O Christ God, bring peace unto our life, as the Lover of mankind, and set forth our prayer as incense, O Thou Who alone restest in the saints!

*ON WEDNESDAY AT MATINS*

*After the first stichology, Cross Sessional Hymns, Tone 2:*

The life-creating Cross of Thy goodness, which Thou hast granted unto us who are unworthy, O Lord, we offer unto Thee in prayer: save the Emperor, and Thy city which prays unto Thee, through the Theotokos, O only Lover of mankind!

*Verse: Exalt ye the Lord our God, and worship the footstool of His feet, for He is holy.*

Even as the enemy took Adam captive through the tree of eating, O Lord, so likewise hast Thou taken captive the enemy through the Tree of the Cross and by Thy Passion; for unto this didst Thou come as the second Adam, to seek out the straying and make alive him that was slain: O God, glory to Thee!

*Sessional Hymns of the Oktoechos*

*Glory, both now, Stavrotheotokion:*

Thy Virgin Mother, O Christ, beholding Thee stretched out dead upon the Tree, weeping bitterly, said: What is this fearful mystery, O my Son? Thou Who grantest eternal life unto all, how dost Thou die of Thine own will upon the Cross an ignominious death?

*At the Sixth Ode, Martyricon:*

O passion-bearers of the Lord, blessed is the earth that was watered by your blood, and holy are the dwellings that received your bodies; for in the stadium ye vanquished the enemy, and with boldness proclaimed Christ; entreat Him as the Good One, we pray, that our souls may be saved!

*ON THURSDAY AT MATINS*

*After the first stichology, Apostles' Sessional Hymns, Tone 2:*

Thou Who didst make the fishermen wiser than rhetoricians, and didst send them as preachers unto all the earth by Thine unspeakable love for mankind, O Christ God: through them confirm Thy Church, and send down Thy blessing upon the faithful, O only Merciful One and Lover of mankind!

*Verse: Their sound has gone forth into all the earth, and their words unto the ends of the world.*

Having caught the nations, the fishermen, and taught the ends of the earth to worship Thee through Thine unspeakable love for mankind, O Christ God: through them confirm Thy Church, and send down Thy blessing upon the faithful, O Thou Who alone restest in the saints!

*Glory, both now, Theotokion:*

Thee do we magnify, O Theotokos, crying aloud: Rejoice, Cloud of the unwaning Light, who didst bear in thy womb the Lord of glory!

*At the Sixth Ode, Martyricon:*

Apostles, martyrs, and prophets, hierarchs, venerable ones, and righteous, who have fought the good fight and kept the faith, having boldness toward the Savior, entreat Him as the Good One for us, we pray, that our souls may be saved!

*ON FRIDAY AT MATINS*

*After the first stichology, Cross Sessional Hymns, Tone 2:*

We worship Thine immaculate icon, O Good One, asking forgiveness of our transgressions, O Christ God; for of Thine own will Thou wast pleased to ascend the Cross in the flesh, that Thou mightest deliver those whom Thou hast created from the bondage of the enemy; therefore with thanksgiving we cry aloud unto Thee: Thou hast filled all things with joy, O our Savior, Who camest to save the world!

*Verse: Exalt ye the Lord our God, and worship the footstool of His feet, for He is holy.*

Thou hast worked salvation in the midst of the earth, O Christ God; upon the Cross Thou didst stretch out Thine all-pure hands, gathering together all the nations, who cry: O Lord, glory to Thee!

*Tone 2.*

*Glory, both now, Stavrotheotokion:*

Most glorified art thou, O Theotokos Virgin, we hymn thee; for by the Cross of thy Son Hades was overthrown, and death was put to death; we that were dead have risen, and have been accounted worthy of life; we have received paradise, our ancient delight; therefore with thanksgiving we give glory, as unto Christ our mighty God, and the only Plenteous in mercy!

*At the Sixth Ode, Martyricon:*

Having been founded upon the immovable rock, O holy ones, ye fought valiantly against the tyrants, and obtained crowns of martyrdom; through them, O God, save us!

*ON SATURDAY AT MATINS*

*At the Praises, Stichera of the Martyrs, Tone 2:*

Having suffered for Christ even unto death, O passion-bearing martyrs, your souls indeed are in the hand of God in heaven, and throughout all the world your relics are venerated; hierarchs and kings bow down, and all the peoples rejoicing, with one accord cry out: Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His venerable ones![^1257]

Every city and country honors your relics, O passion-bearing martyrs; for having suffered lawfully, ye received crowns from heaven; and therefore are ye the boast of hierarchs, the victory of kings, and the beauty of the churches.

Having taken up the Cross of Christ as an invincible weapon, the holy martyrs abolished all the power of the devil, and received heavenly crowns; they have become a wall for us, ever praying for us.

*For the Departed:*

Woe is me! What a struggle has the soul when parting from the body! Woe is me, how much it weeps then! And there is none who has mercy on it; lifting up its eyes unto the Angels, it prays in vain; stretching forth its hands unto men, it has none that helps; therefore, my beloved brethren, knowing our brief life, let us ask rest from Christ for the departed, and for our souls great mercy!

*Glory, both now, Theotokion:*

Come, all ye, let us with unceasing hymns glorify (crying aloud) the Mother of the Light; for she gave birth unto our salvation; and let us offer unto her: "Rejoice!" as the only one who bore God Who is before the ages, the Sovereign of all; rejoice, thou who hast rebuilt Eve who bore us; rejoice, all-pure Virgin who knewest not wedlock!

*At the Aposticha, Stichera for the Departed:*

*Tone 2, Podoben: "When from the Tree" (Е҆гда̀ ѿ дре́ва):*

The onslaught of death and corruption hast Thou overthrown by Thy life-bearing death, O Master; and unto all hast Thou poured forth eternal life, and granted resurrection unto the dead; therefore we pray Thee, O Savior: give rest unto those who have departed unto Thee in faith, and count them worthy of Thine immortal glory, O Lover of mankind!

*Verse: Blessed are they whom Thou hast chosen and taken to Thyself, O Lord.*

That Thou mightest make men partakers of Thy divine kingdom, O Christ, Thou didst endure crucifixion, and of Thine own will accepted death; therefore we pray Thee: in Thy tender compassion show those who have departed unto Thee in faith to be partakers of Thy kingdom, *Sessional Hymns of the Oktoechos*

and account them worthy of Thy sweet beauty, O Lover of mankind!

*Verse: Their souls shall dwell among good things.*

Desiring to save Thy creation, and the truly fearful mystery of Thine economy, Thou didst accomplish rejoicing, as the All-Good One; and by a price hast Thou redeemed the whole world, even by Thy precious Blood; therefore we pray Thee: count those who have departed unto Thee in faith worthy of redemption together with all the saints!

*Verse: And their memory is from generation to generation.*

Standing before Thy terrible, awesome, and fearful throne, O Christ, the dead from the ages await Thy righteous judgment, and receive Thy divine justice; then do Thou, O Savior, give rest unto Thy servants who have departed unto Thee in faith, where are the choirs of the saints, and joy is unspeakable!

*Glory, both now, Theotokion:*

When my soul is about to be separated from the bond of the flesh and from life, then do thou stand before me, O Sovereign Lady, and tear asunder the counsels of the bodiless enemies; and shatter their jaws who seek to devour me unsparingly, that I may pass without hindrance past the princes of darkness standing in the air,[^1258] O Bride of God!

*ON SUNDAY EVENING*

*At "Lord, I have cried", Penitential Stichera, Tone 3:*

An evening hymn do we offer unto Thee, O Christ, with incense and spiritual songs: have mercy and save our souls!

Save me, O Lord my God, for Thou art salvation unto all; the tempest of passions troubles me, and the burden of mine iniquities submerges me; give me a helping hand, and lead me up unto the light of compunction, as Thou alone art merciful and the Lover of mankind!

Gather my scattered mind, O Lord, and cleanse my frozen heart; give me repentance as unto Peter, sighing as unto the publican, and tears as unto the harlot, that with a great voice I may cry unto Thee: O God, save me, as Thou alone art Tenderhearted and the Lover of mankind!

Many a time while performing psalmody, I am found fulfilling sin, uttering hymnody indeed with my tongue, yet pondering improper things in my soul; but amend both, O Christ God, through repentance, and save me!

*ON MONDAY AT MATINS*

*After the first stichology, Compunctive Sessional Hymns, Tone 3:*

At the fearful judgment seat, without accusers am I exposed, without witnesses am I condemned; for the books of conscience are unfolded, and hidden deeds are laid bare; before Thou art to examine in that assembly before all the people what has been committed by me, O God, cleanse me and save me!

*Tone 3.*

*Verse: O Lord, rebuke me not in Thine anger [nor chasten me in Thy wrath]:*

How long, O my soul, dost thou abide in transgressions? How long dost thou accept the putting off of repentance? Take to mind the judgment to come, and cry aloud unto the Lord: O Knower of hearts, I have sinned; before Thou judgest me, have mercy on me!

*Glory, both now, Theotokion:*

Whithersoever one is saved, thither does he rightly flee; and what other refuge is there such as thee, O Theotokos, who shelterest our souls?

*At the Sixth Ode, Martyricon:*

Who will not marvel at the invincible struggles of the holy martyrs? Who will not be astonished at their continual steadfastness? For by fire and sword, by wild beasts and slaughterings, they vanquished the adversary foe, having abhorred the flatteries of kings and shaken off the threats of tyrants; therefore also they received crowns from Christ God, Who grants unto the world great mercy!

*ON TUESDAY AT MATINS*

*After the first stichology, Penitential Sessional Hymns, Tone 3:*

Living upon earth, O my soul, repent! The dust in the grave does not sing praise, nor does it deliver from transgressions; cry aloud unto Christ God: O Knower of hearts, I have sinned; before Thou judgest me, have mercy on me!

*Verse: O Lord, rebuke me not in Thine anger [nor chasten me in Thy wrath]:*

At the hour of prayer I promise to repent, yet the enemy diligently suggests improper things to make me sin; but deliver me from this, O God, and have mercy on me!

*Glory, both now, Theotokion:*

Our refuge and strength, O Theotokos, mighty help of the world: by thy prayers shelter thy servants from every necessity, O only Blessed One!

*At the Sixth Ode, Martyricon:*

The courage of your endurance conquered the wiles of the author of evil, the enemy, O all-praised passion-bearers; therefore were ye accounted worthy of eternal blessedness; but pray ye unto the Lord to save the flock of the Christ-loving people, O martyrs of the truth!

*ON WEDNESDAY AT MATINS*

*After the first stichology, Cross Sessional Hymns, Tone 3:*

At Thine unsearchable power and voluntary crucifixion the angelic hosts marveled, beholding how the Invisible One was wounded in the flesh, wishing to deliver mankind from corruption; therefore as unto the Giver of life do we cry unto Thee: Glory, O Christ, to Thy kingdom!

*Verse: Exalt ye the Lord our God, and worship the footstool of His feet, for He is holy.*

*Sessional Hymns of the Oktoechos*

The Cross was planted upon the earth and touched the heavens, not as though a tree had reached that height, but because Thou upon it fillest all things: O Lord, glory to Thee!

*Glory, both now, Stavrotheotokion:*

Having acquired the rod of strength, the Cross of thy Son, O Theotokos, thereby do we overthrow the insolence of the enemies, unceasingly magnifying thee in love.

*At the Sixth Ode, Martyricon:*

The memory of Thy passion-bearers, O Lord, hast Thou beforehand revived as Almighty, for Thou didst strengthen them to emulate Thy Sufferings; for manfully did they conquer the power of Beliar; therefore also did they receive the gifts of healings: by their prayers, O Lover of mankind, grant peace unto our souls!

*ON THURSDAY AT MATINS*

*After the first stichology, Apostles' Sessional Hymns, Tone 3:*

Divine preachers of the Truth and teachers of the Church were ye shown forth, O eyewitness Apostles; for having trampled down the delusion of idols, ye clearly proclaimed the Trinity; entreat It, O blessed ones, to grant us great mercy!

*Verse: Their sound has gone forth into all the earth [and their words unto the ends of the world]:*

Come, all ye, let us hymn the Apostles as governors; for they drove away the deceit of idols, and led us up unto the light of life, and taught us to glorify the Trinity; therefore, all we faithful who celebrate their honorable memory, let us glorify the Savior!

*Glory, both now, Theotokion:*

As an uncultivated vine, O Virgin, hast thou put forth the most fair cluster of grapes, pouring out for us the saving wine which makes glad all men; therefore blessing thee as the cause of good things, ever with the Angel do we cry aloud: Rejoice, thou Full of Grace!

*At the Sixth Ode, Martyricon:*

Arming yourselves with the whole armor of Christ, and clothing yourselves with the armor of faith, ye suffered and cast down the regiments of the enemy; for eagerly in the hope of life did ye endure of old all the threats and wounds of the tyrants; therefore also did ye receive crowns, O patient-minded martyrs of Christ!

*ON FRIDAY AT MATINS*

*After the first stichology, Cross Sessional Hymns, Tone 3:*

Thou Who wast pleased to suffer the Cross and death, didst plant it in the midst of creation, when Thou wast well pleased, O Savior, that Thy body be nailed thereto; then also the sun hid its rays; beholding these things, the thief confessed Thee to be God, crying unto Thee: "Remember me, O Lord!" and having believed, that penitent received paradise.

*Verse: Exalt ye the Lord our God, and worship the footstool of His feet, for He is holy.*

Upon the cypress, the pine, and the cedar wast Thou lifted up,[^1259] O Lamb of God, that Thou mightest save those who in faith worship Thy voluntary crucifixion: O Christ God, glory to Thee!

*Tone 3.*

*Glory, both now, Stavrotheotokion:*

A reproachful death, O Compassionate One, didst Thou willingly endure by crucifixion; beholding which, She who bore Thee, O Christ, was wounded; by Her entreaties, in the tender mercy of Thy loving-kindness, O only Most Good Lord and Lover of mankind, have compassion and save the world, Thou Who takest away the sin of the world!

*At the Sixth Ode, Martyricon:*

Ye shine by faith as most radiant luminaries, O holy ones, physicians of piety, all-praised passion-bearers; for not having feared the wounds of the torturers, ye cast down the impious deceit of idols, having the true Cross as invincible victory.

*ON FRIDAY EVENING*

*At "Lord, I have cried," after the Idiomelon Sticheron, Martyrica, Tone 3:*

Great is the power of Thy Cross, O Lord; for it was set up in one place, yet it works in all the world, and made Apostles out of fishermen, and martyrs out of the Gentiles, that they may pray for our souls!

Great is the power of Thy martyrs, O Christ; for lying in their tombs they drive away spirits, and have brought to naught the power of the enemy, having fought the good fight through faith in the Trinity!

The Prophets and Apostles of Christ, and the martyrs, taught us to sing of the consubstantial Trinity, and enlightened the deceived nations, and made the sons of men partakers with the Angels!

Thy martyrs, O Lord, established by faith and strengthened by hope, spiritually united in soul by the love of Thy Cross, destroyed the tyranny of the enemy, and having obtained crowns, pray with the bodiless powers for our souls!

*ON SATURDAY AT MATINS*

*After the first stichology, Martyric Sessional Hymns, Tone 3:*

The courageous endurance of your patience conquered the wiles of the evil-originating enemy, O all-praised passion-bearers; therefore were ye accounted worthy of eternal blessedness; but pray ye unto the Lord to save the flock of the Christ-loving people, being witnesses of the truth!

*Verse: Marvelous is God in His saints, the God of Israel.*[^1260]

Ye shine by faith as most radiant luminaries, O holy ones, physicians of the ailing, all-praised passion-bearers; for not having feared the wounds of the torturers, ye cast down the impious deceit of idols, having the true Cross as invincible victory.

*Verse: Unto the saints that are in His earth, the Lord hath made marvelous all His desires in them.*[^1261]

Armed with the whole armor of Christ, and having put on the armor of faith, suffering valiantly ye cast down the regiments of the enemy; zealously in the hope of life ye endured all the threats and wounds of the torturers; therefore also ye received crowns, O long-suffering martyrs of Christ!

*Glory, for the Departed:*

When by Thy word we stand before Thy judgment seat that takes no bribes, O Lord, put not to shame those who have believed in Thee, O our Savior; for we all have sinned, yet from Thee have we not departed; therefore we pray Thee:

*Sessional Hymns of the Oktoechos*

In the dwellings of Thy righteous ones, O Christ, give rest unto those whom Thou hast received; for Thou alone art without sin.

*Both now, Theotokion:*

Thee who didst intercede for the salvation of our race do we hymn, O Virgin Theotokos; for having through the Cross accepted suffering in the flesh taken from thee, Thy Son and our God delivered us from corruption, as the Lover of mankind!

*At the Praises, Stichera of the Martyrs, Tone 3:*

The soldiers of Christ cast away the fear of kings and torturers, and with good courage and manfully confessed Him, the Lord God of all and our King, and they pray for our souls!

The hosts of the holy Angels were astonished at the suffering of the martyrs; for clothed in mortal flesh, they took no heed of tortures, having become imitators of the Sufferings of Christ the Savior, and they pray for our souls!

As luminaries in the world do ye shine even after death, O holy martyrs, having fought the good fight; and having boldness, entreat Christ that our souls may find mercy!

O men, why do we trouble ourselves in vain? Short is the path we run: our life is smoke, vapor, dust, and ashes; for a little while it appears, and quickly it perishes;[^1262] therefore unto Christ the immortal King let us cry aloud: Give rest unto those who have departed from us, where is the dwelling of all who rejoice!

Without seed didst thou conceive of the Holy Spirit, and glorifying do we hymn thee: Rejoice, O Most Holy Virgin!

*At the Aposticha, Stichera for the Departed, Tone 3, Podoben: "Great is the power of Thy Cross" (Вели́ѧ крⷭ҇та̀ твоегѡ̀):*

I glorify Thy precious Cross, through which life was granted, and the enjoyment of delight unto those who in faith and love hymn Thee, O only Plenteous in mercy; therefore we cry unto Thee, O Christ God: Give rest unto those who have departed from us, where the dwelling of all who rejoice is with Thee!

*Verse: Blessed are they whom Thou hast chosen and taken to Thyself, O Lord.*[^1263]

O only Merciful and Tender-hearted One, having an incomprehensible abyss of goodness, knowing human nature which Thou didst fashion: we pray Thee, O Christ God, give rest unto those who have departed from us, where the dwelling of all who rejoice is with Thee!

*Verse: Their souls shall dwell among good things.*[^1264]

Thou didst fall asleep in the tomb as man, but by invincible power as God Thou didst raise up those who sleep in the tombs, who offer unceasing songs unto Thee; therefore we pray Thee, O Christ God: Give rest unto those who have departed from us, where the dwelling of all who rejoice is with Thee!

*Glory, both now, Theotokion:*

Thee as a noetic lamp bearing the Light of the Godhead, united to the coarseness of human nature, O Theotokos, do we all know: entreat Thy Son and God to give rest unto those who have departed from us, where is the rejoicing of all who are glad!

*Tone 4.*

*ON SUNDAY EVENING*

*At "Lord, I have cried," Penitential Stichera, Tone 4:*

I desired with tears to wash away the handwriting of my transgressions,[^1265] O Lord, and for the rest of my life to be well-pleasing unto Thee through repentance; but the enemy deceives me and wars against my soul: O Lord, before I perish utterly, save me!

Who that is tempest-tossed and flees unto Thy haven, O Lord, is not saved? Or who that is ailing and falls down before Thy healing is not cured, O Creator of all and Physician of the sick? O Lord, before I perish utterly, save me!

Wash me with my tears, O Savior, for I have been defiled by many sins; therefore do I fall down before Thee: I have sinned, O God, have mercy on me!

A sheep am I of Thy rational flock, and unto Thee do I flee, O Good Shepherd; seek me out who have gone astray, O God, and have mercy on me![^1266]

*Then three of the Triodion, and three of the Menaion for the saint.*

*ON MONDAY AT MATINS*

*After the first stichology, Compunctive Sessional Hymns, Tone 4:*

Visit my humble soul, O Lord, which has spent its whole life in sins; in the same manner as the harlot,[^1267] receive also me, and save me!

*Verse: O Lord, rebuke me not in Thine anger [nor chasten me in Thy wrath]:*[^1268]

Sailing across the deep of this present life, I ponder the abyss of my many evils, and having no helmsman of my thoughts, I utter unto Thee Peter's cry: Save me, O Christ; save me, O God, as the Lover of mankind![^1269]

*Glory, both now, Theotokion:*

Unto her who was brought up in the temple in the Holy of Holies, clothed in faith and wisdom, and boundless virginity, the Archistrategos Gabriel brought greeting from heaven, even: "Rejoice, rejoice, O Blessed One; rejoice, O most glorified One: the Lord is with Thee!"[^1270]

*At the Sixth Ode, Martyricon:*

Today the angelic hosts have come to enlighten the minds of the faithful in memory of the passion-bearers, and to make radiant the universe with grace; being entreated by them, O God, grant us great mercy!

*Sessional Hymns of the Oktoechos*

*ON TUESDAY AT MATINS*

*After the first stichology, Compunctive Sessional Hymns, Tone 4:*

Quickly let us enter into the bridal chamber of Christ, that we all may hear the blessed voice of Christ our God: "Come, ye who love heavenly glory," having become partakers with the wise virgins, making radiant our lamps through faith![^1271]

*Verse: O Lord, rebuke me not in Thine anger [nor chasten me in Thy wrath]:*

Remember, O my soul, how we shall stand before the Judge in the fearful hour: the dread thrones are set, and the deeds of each are exposed; then the Judge is inexorable, and there the fire is sorely prepared for thee like a tempestuous raging sea, as though to cover all things; seeing all these things, O my soul, groan before the end!

*Glory, both now, Theotokion:*

Truly and in sovereign right, O Theotokos, we pray thee: as Mother possessing boldness before Thy Son and our God, preserve especially this city which flees unto thy protection, which has thee as its strength, which has recourse unto thee as a haven, a wall, the only intercession of the human race!

*At the Sixth Ode, Martyricon:*

Thy Church, adorned with the blood of Thy martyrs throughout the whole world as with purple and fine linen, cries through them unto Thee, O Christ God: Send down Thy compassions upon Thy people, grant peace unto Thy commonwealth, and unto our souls great mercy!

*ON WEDNESDAY AT MATINS*

*After the first stichology, Cross Sessional Hymns, Tone 4:*

Thou hast redeemed us from the curse of the law by Thy precious Blood; being nailed to the Cross and pierced with a spear, Thou didst pour forth immortality for mankind, O our Savior: glory to Thee![^1272]

*Verse: Exalt ye the Lord our God, and worship the footstool of His feet, for He is holy.*[^1273]

Speedily anticipate, before we are enslaved to the enemies who blaspheme Thee and threaten us, O Christ our God; destroy by Thy Cross those who war against us, that they may understand what the faith of the Orthodox can do, by the prayers of the Theotokos, O only Lover of mankind!

*Glory, both now, Stavrotheotokion:*

O all-immaculate Virgin, Mother of Christ God, a sword pierced thy most holy soul when thou didst see thy Son and God willingly crucified; cease not, O blessed one, to entreat Him to grant us forgiveness of transgressions![^1274]

*At the Sixth Ode, Martyricon:*

Thy martyrs, O Lord, in their sufferings received incorruptible crowns from Thee, our God; for having Thy strength, they cast down the torturers, and shattered the powerless insolence of demons: by their prayers, save our souls!

*Tone 4.*

*ON THURSDAY AT MATINS*

*After the first stichology, Apostles' Sessional Hymns, Tone 4:*

As luminaries unto the ends of the earth didst Thou reveal Thy disciples, O Christ, shining Thy understanding unto our souls in darkness, O Master; and having through them darkened the delusion of idols, Thou didst enlighten the world with the teachings of piety: by their entreaties, save our souls!

*Verse: Their sound has gone forth into all the earth, and their words unto the ends of the world.*[^1275]

As Moses guided Israel from bondage through the Red Sea, and by Thy right hand, O Master, drowned Pharaoh; so by miracles Thy most wise disciples parted the sea of bitter godlessness, and guided the people unto Thee, O Word without beginning and only Lover of mankind![^1276]

*Glory, both now, Theotokion:*

The Word of the Father, Christ our God, Who became incarnate of thee, have we known, O Virgin Theotokos, only Pure, only Blessed One; therefore unceasingly hymning thee, we magnify thee!

*At the Sixth Ode, Martyricon:*

Arming themselves with the Cross, Thy passion-bearers conquered the wiles of the evil-originating enemy, O Christ our God; they shone forth as luminaries, instructing mankind, and grant healings unto those who ask in faith: by their prayers, save our souls!

*ON FRIDAY AT MATINS*

*After the first stichology, Cross Sessional Hymns, Tone 4:*

The Jews nailed Thee to the Cross, O Savior, whereby Thou didst call us from the Gentiles, O Lord and Lover of mankind; Thou didst stretch out Thy palms upon it of Thine own will, and didst deign Thy ribs to be pierced with a spear: glory to the multitude of Thy compassions, O Long-suffering One!

*Verse: Exalt ye the Lord our God, and worship the footstool of His feet, for He is holy.*

Beholding now the light of our souls, O Christ, even Thy most pure Cross, and bowing down before it, radiantly do we cry unto Thee: Glory to Thee, Who wast pleased to be lifted up upon it; glory to Thee, Who thereby didst enlighten all creation; therefore unceasingly we glorify Thee with hymns!

*Glory, both now, Stavrotheotokion:*

When Thy most pure Mother saw Thee lifted up upon the Cross, O Word of God, weeping maternally She said: What is this new and strange wonder, O my Son? How dost Thou, the Life of all, taste of death, desiring to quicken the dead, as Thou art Compassionate?

*At the Sixth Ode, Martyricon:*

The honorable triumph of the passion-bearers has shown the Church to be heaven, and Angels dance together with men: by their prayers, O Christ God, save our souls!

*Sessional Hymns of the Oktoechos*

*ON FRIDAY EVENING*

*At "Lord, I have cried," after the Idiomelon Sticheron, Martyrica, Tone 4:*

Thou Who art glorified in the memorials of Thy saints, O Christ God, and art entreated by them, send down upon us great mercy!

Thou Who didst accept the endurance of the holy martyrs, accept also from us our hymnody, O Lover of mankind, and grant us through their prayers great mercy!

Having boldness before the Savior, O holy ones, pray unceasingly for us sinners, asking remission of transgressions and great mercy for our souls!

Living sacrifices, rational whole-burnt offerings, martyrs of the Lord, perfect victims unto God, sheep that know God and are known of God, whose sheepfold is inaccessible to wolves: pray ye also for us, that we may be shepherded with you beside the waters of rest![^1277]

*Glory, for the Departed:*

Where is attachment to the world? Where is transient fantasy? Where are gold and silver? Where is the multitude of servants, and clamor? All is dust, all is ashes, all is shadow! But come, let us cry aloud unto the immortal King: O Lord, account those who have departed from us worthy of Thine eternal good things, and give them rest in unfading blessedness!

*ON SATURDAY AT MATINS*

*After the first stichology, Martyric Sessional Hymns, Tone 4:*

Thy martyrs, O Lord, in their sufferings received incorruptible crowns from Thee, our God; for having Thy strength, they cast down the torturers, and shattered the powerless insolence of demons: by their prayers, save our souls!

*Verse: Marvelous is God in His saints, the God of Israel.*

Thy Church, adorned with the blood of Thy martyrs throughout the whole world as with purple and fine linen, cries through them unto Thee, O Christ God: Send down Thy compassions upon Thy people, grant peace unto Thy commonwealth, and unto our souls great mercy!

*Verse: Unto the saints that are in His earth, the Lord hath made marvelous all His desires in them.*

Arming themselves with the Cross, Thy passion-bearers, O Christ our God, conquered the wiles of the evil-originating enemy; they shone forth as luminaries, instructing mankind, and grant healings unto those who ask in faith: by their entreaties, save our souls!

*Glory, for the Departed:*

The souls whom Thou hast translated from temporal things, O Savior, give rest unto them, as Thou art compassionate, almighty, and the only Lover of mankind; as Thou art bountiful, forgive what they have committed; have mercy, O Merciful One, upon the works of Thy hands, by the prayers of the Theotokos, O only Lover of mankind!

*Both now, Theotokion:*

The mystery hidden from the ages and unknown to Angels, through thee, O Theotokos, has been revealed unto those on earth: God incarnate in unconfused union, willingly accepting the Cross for our sake, whereby having resurrected the first-created, He saved our souls from death![^1278]

*Tone 4.*

*At the Praises, Stichera of the Martyrs, Tone 4:*

Partakers with the Angels became ye, O holy martyrs, having manfully proclaimed Christ before the judgment seat; for all the fair things in the world ye abandoned as if they were not, and held fast unto faith as a firm anchor of hope; therefore, having driven away deceit, ye pour forth the gifts of healings unto the faithful, unceasingly praying that our souls may be saved!

How should we not marvel at your struggles, O holy martyrs? For clothed in mortal bodies, ye conquered the bodiless enemies; the threats of the torturers did not frighten you, nor did the assaults of torments terrify you: truly worthily were ye glorified by Christ!

Precious is the death of Thy saints, O Lord; for by sword and fire and with a contrite soul did they shed their blood, having hope in Thee to receive the reward of their labors; for they endured, and received from Thee, O Savior, great mercy![^1279]

Who is not struck with awe, O holy martyrs, beholding the good fight which ye fought: how being in the flesh ye conquered the bodiless foe, confessing Christ and arming yourselves with the Cross? Therefore worthily were ye shown forth as expellers of demons and conquerors of barbarians, unceasingly praying that our souls may be saved!

*Glory, for the Departed:*

In Thy place of rest, O Lord, where all Thy saints repose, give rest unto Thy departed servants, as Thou alone art the Lover of mankind!

*Both now, Theotokion:*

O only pure and most immaculate Virgin, who without seed didst bear God, entreat that our souls may be saved!

*At the Aposticha, Stichera for the Departed, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast given a sign" (Да́лъ є҆сѝ зна́менїе):*

Truly fearful is the mystery of death, how the soul is forcibly separated from the body, torn asunder by divine will from the harmony and jointure of the natural bond; therefore we pray Thee: give rest unto the departed in the tabernacles of Thy righteous ones, O Life-giver and Lover of mankind!

*Verse: Blessed are they whom Thou hast chosen and taken to Thyself, O Lord.*

Death appears as sleep unto those who believe in Thee, when Thou, Who rulest over all, wast laid in the tomb and didst destroy the dominion of death, bringing to naught its ancient tyranny; therefore we pray Thee: establish the departed in the joy of Thy saints, and in the brightness of the righteous!

*Verse: Their souls shall dwell among good things.*

Thou hast become for us righteousness and sanctification, and redemption for our souls; for having taken upon Thyself the penalty due unto us, Thou didst lead us justified and redeemed unto the Father; and now we pray Thee: give rest unto the departed in the joy and brightness of Thy saints, O Benefactor and Lover of mankind![^1280]

*Sessional Hymns of the Oktoechos*

*Glory, both now, Theotokion:*

Following the sayings of the God-proclaiming Prophets, we confess thee to be the Theotokos, O All-immaculate One; for thou didst bear God ineffably incarnate, Who delivered us who were captive from our sins: Him do thou now entreat, O Most Pure One, to enlighten Thy departed servants with His illumination!

*ON SUNDAY EVENING*

*At "Lord, I have cried," Penitential Stichera, Tone 5:*

O Lord, sinning I cease not; accounted worthy of Thy love for mankind, I understand not: overcome my perplexity, O only Good One, and have mercy on me!

O Lord, I both fear Thy terror and cease not doing evil! Who before the tribunal does not fear the judge? Or who, wishing to be healed, provokes the physician, as I do? O Long-suffering Lord, have compassion on my weakness, and have mercy on me!

Overlook the multitude of my transgressions, O Lord born of the Virgin, and cleanse all my sins, granting me the thought of turning back, as Thou alone art the Lover of mankind, I pray Thee, and have mercy on me!

Woe is me! Unto whom have I become like? Unto the barren fig tree,[^1281] and I fear the curse together with the cut of the axe; but O heavenly Husbandman, Christ God, make my frozen soul fruitful, and as the prodigal son, receive me and have mercy on me![^1282]

*Then three of the Triodion, and three of the Menaion for the saint.*

*ON MONDAY AT MATINS*

*After the first stichology, Compunctive Sessional Hymns, Tone 5:*

While the Judge sits, and the Angels stand by, the trumpet sounds, and the flame burns, what wilt thou do, O my soul, being led unto judgment? For then shall thy grievous deeds stand forth, and thy secret transgressions be exposed; therefore before the end cry aloud unto Christ God: O Knower of hearts, I have sinned, have mercy on me!

*Verse: O Lord, rebuke me not in Thine anger [nor chasten me in Thy wrath]:*

O soul, things here are temporary, but there they are eternal: I behold the tribunal, and the Judge upon the throne, and I tremble at the verdict; therefore, O my soul, turn back: the judgment is without forgiveness!

*Glory, both now, Theotokion:*

With the Angels in heaven and with men on earth, with the voice of rejoicing, O Theotokos, do we cry unto thee: Rejoice, gate wider than the heavens; rejoice, sole salvation of the earth-born; rejoice, O Pure One; rejoice, thou Full of Grace, who didst bear God incarnate!

*Tone 5.*

*At the Sixth Ode, Martyricon:*

Zealously emulating the cup of Thy Passion, O Lord, Thy passion-bearers left behind the beauty of this life and became partakers with the Angels: by their entreaties, grant unto our souls cleansing and great mercy![^1283]

*ON TUESDAY AT MATINS*

*After the first stichology, Compunctive Sessional Hymns, Tone 5:*

Lying upon the bed of my many sins, I am robbed of the hope of my salvation; for the sleep of my slothfulness procures torment for my soul; therefore spare me, O Christ God, as Thou alone art the Lover of mankind!

*Verse: O Lord, rebuke me not in Thine anger [nor chasten me in Thy wrath]:*

Let us all watch and meet Christ with abundance of oil and with bright lamps, that we may be accounted worthy to enter inside the bridal chamber; for he who is caught outside the doors will cry in vain unto God: "Have mercy on me!"[^1284]

*Glory, both now, Theotokion:*

The strange mystery of the Virgin was shown forth unto the world as saving; for of her wast Thou born without seed, and in flesh wast Thou revealed without corruption, O Joy of all: Lord, glory to Thee!

*At the Sixth Ode, Martyricon:*

Thou Who hast granted us the wonders of Thy holy martyrs as an impregnable wall, O Christ God: by their prayers destroy the counsels of the heathen, and strengthen the scepters of the realm, as Thou alone art Good and the Lover of mankind!

*ON WEDNESDAY AT MATINS*

*After the first stichology, Cross Sessional Hymns, Tone 5:*

Let us the faithful sing of and glorify our Savior and Redeemer, Who was willingly crucified as He knew best and as He was well pleased; for He nailed the sins of mankind to the Cross, delivering the human race from deception, and made them worthy of the Kingdom!

*Verse: Exalt ye the Lord our God, and worship the footstool of His feet, for He is holy.*

Having endured the Cross of Thine own will, Thou didst deliver mankind from corruption, O Savior; we the faithful hymn and worship Thee, for Thou hast enlightened us by the power of the Cross, and all of us glorify Thee, O bountiful Lover of mankind, as the Life-giver and Lord!

*Glory, both now, Stavrotheotokion:*

Standing by the Cross of the Lord, weeping the Theotokos cried aloud: Woe is me, O my Child! Woe is me, Light of mine eyes! How art Thou stretched upon the Cross, Who divinely didst stretch out the heaven as a skin,[^1285] and didst bring up the fountains of waters from the sea by Thy command?[^1286]

*Sessional Hymns of the Oktoechos*

*At the Sixth Ode, Martyricon:*

Thy passion-bearers, O Lord, hast Thou shown forth unto the universe as great intercessors, O Savior, by whom passions flee away: by their prayers, save our souls!

*ON THURSDAY AT MATINS*

*After the first stichology, Apostles' Sessional Hymns, Tone 5:*

As eyewitnesses of the Word and servants of Christ,[^1287] let all us earth-born praise the all-wise Apostles in spiritual songs and hymns; for they diligently entreat Christ for us who sing of their radiant memory and bow before their relics!

*Verse: Their sound has gone forth into all the earth [and their words unto the ends of the world]:*

Harmoniously let us praise the Apostles of the Lord as luminaries revealed unto the universe; for they caught the nations for piety, and having enlightened us, clearly proclaim to honor the Holy Trinity: united in essence, yet divided in Hypostases!

*Glory, both now, Theotokion:*

O unwedded Bride and Ever-Virgin, with the Angels unceasingly do we praise thee, for Thy Son and God has done great things for us through thee;[^1288] He Who before the ages is of the Father was well pleased to be contained in thy womb, to deliver our race from deception!

*At the Sixth Ode, Martyricon:*

At the righteous achievements of the holy martyrs, the heavenly powers were astonished above measure: how in mortal flesh, having fought valiantly by the power of the Cross, they invisibly conquered the bodiless enemy, and they pray unto the Lord that our souls may find mercy!

*ON FRIDAY AT MATINS*

*After the first stichology, Cross Sessional Hymns, Tone 5:*

The Place of the Skull has become paradise; for as soon as the Tree of the Cross was planted, straightway it budded forth the living Cluster of grapes, even Thee, O Savior, unto our gladness: glory to Thee!

*Verse: Exalt ye the Lord our God [and worship the footstool of His feet, for He is holy]:*

The Tree of Thy Cross, O our Savior, was shown forth as saving unto the world; for being willingly nailed upon it, Thou didst deliver the earth-born from the curse, O Joy of all: Lord, glory to Thee!

*Glory, both now, Stavrotheotokion:*

Beholding Thee upon the Cross, O Christ, willingly hanging between thieves, Thy Mother, torn in maternal compassion, said: O sinless Son, how art Thou wrongfully nailed to the Cross as an evildoer, desiring to quicken the human race, as Thou art Most Good?

*At the Sixth Ode, Martyricon:*

Today shines the memory of the passion-bearers, for it has radiance from heaven; the angelic choir keeps festival, and the human race celebrates together; therefore they pray unto the Lord that our souls may find mercy!

*ON FRIDAY EVENING*

*At "Lord, I have cried," after the Idiomelon Sticheron, Martyrica, Tone 5:*

Taking no heed of all earthly things, and having manfully dared to face torments, ye did not miss your blessed hopes; but ye became heirs of the heavenly Kingdom, O all-praised martyrs; having boldness toward God, the Lover of mankind, ask peace for the world, and great mercy for our souls!

Clothed with the shield of faith, and having strengthened yourselves with the sign of the Cross, ye manfully gave yourselves over to torments, and abolished the pride and deceit of the devil, O Thy holy ones, O Lord; by their prayers, as Almighty God, send down peace upon the world, and great mercy unto our souls!

Pray for us, O holy martyrs, that we may be delivered from our iniquities; for unto you has grace been given to pray for us!

With insatiable love of soul, ye did not deny Christ, O holy martyrs; ye endured grievous and diverse wounds of passions, and cast down the pride of the torturers; having preserved the faith unswerving and unharmed, ye were translated unto the heavens; therefore, having boldness toward Him, ask that great mercy be granted unto us!

*Glory, for the Departed:*

I remembered the Prophet crying aloud: "I am earth and ashes";[^1289] and again I looked into the graves, and I saw bare bones, and I said then: Who is he? King or soldier? Rich or poor? Righteous man or sinner? But give rest, O Lord, with the righteous unto Thy servants, as the Lover of mankind!

*Both now, Dogmaticon:*

*ON SATURDAY AT MATINS*

*After the first stichology, Martyric Sessional Hymns, Tone 5:*

O Lord, having emulated the cup of Thy Passions, Thy passion-bearers left behind the beauty of this life and became partakers with the Angels; by their entreaties grant peace unto our souls, O Christ God, and great mercy!

*Verse: Marvelous is God in His saints, the God of Israel.*[^1290]

The wonders of Thy holy martyrs hast Thou granted unto us as an indestructible rampart, O Christ God; by their prayers destroy the counsels of the nations, and establish the scepters of the kingdom, as the only Good One and Lover of mankind!

*Verse: Unto the saints that are in His earth, the Lord hath made marvelous all His desires in them.*[^1291]

Today shines the memory of the passion-bearers, for it has radiance from heaven; the angelic choir keeps festival, and the human race celebrates together; therefore they pray unto the Lord that our souls may find mercy!

*Glory, for the Departed:*

Give rest, O our Savior, with the righteous unto Thy servants, and establish them in Thy courts, even as it is written, overlooking all their transgressions, both voluntary and involuntary, and all things done in knowledge and in ignorance, as Thou art good, O Lover of mankind!

*Glory, both now, Theotokion:*

Rejoice, impassable gate of the Lord! Rejoice, rampart and protection of those who run to thee! Rejoice, haven unassailed by storms, who knewest not wedlock, who didst bear in the flesh thy Creator and God; cease not to intercede for those who hymn and worship thy childbearing!

*At the Praises, Martyrica, Tone 5:*

Blessed is the army of the heavenly King! For even though the passion-bearers were earthly-born, yet they hastened to attain the angelic dignity, taking no heed of bodies; and because of their sufferings they were counted worthy of the honor of the bodiless powers; therefore by their prayers, O Lord, save our souls!

Thy passion-bearers, O Lord, having made themselves like unto the angelic ranks, endured torments as though they were bodiless; and having unanimous hope, the enjoyment of the promised good things, by their prayers, O Christ God, have mercy on us!

The holy martyrs, having contended on earth, endured frost, and surrendered themselves to fire; water received them, and theirs is the voice: "We went through fire and water, and Thou broughtest us out into a place of rest";[^1292] by their prayers, O God, have mercy on us!

Being in the midst of torments, the holy ones cried aloud rejoicing: These things are our merchandise unto eternity! In place of the wounds inflicted on our bodies, radiant raiment shall blossom forth for us at the resurrection; instead of dishonor, crowns; instead of prison bonds, paradise; and instead of condemnation with evildoers, life with the Angels; by their prayers, O Lord, save our souls!

*Glory, for the Departed:*

Thou Who didst create me, O Lord, and didst lay Thy hand upon me, and gavest commandment unto me, saying: "Unto the earth shalt thou go again,"[^1293] direct me into Thy straight path, forgiving me my transgressions; pardon me and save me as I pray, as the Lover of mankind!

*Both now, Theotokion:*

We bless thee, O Virgin Theotokos, for from thee shone forth the Sun of righteousness, Christ,[^1294] Who hath great mercy!

*At the Aposticha, Stichera for the Departed, Tone 5, Podoben: "Rejoice, O container of ascetics" (Ра́дꙋйсѧ по́стникѡвъ):*

With the light of Thy countenance, O Christ, as the Compassionate One, enlighten those who have departed; settle them in a green place, beside the waters of Thy pure and divine rest, in the longed-for bosom of Abraham our forefather,[^1295] where Thy light shines purely, and the fountains of goodness pour forth; where the choirs of all the righteous dance clearly, rejoicing in Thy goodness; with them rank Thy servants, granting them great mercy!

*Verse: Blessed are they whom Thou hast chosen and received, O Lord.*[^1296]

Vouchsafe, O Compassionate One, that those who have departed from temporal things unto Thee, the Master of all and our God, may sing with unceasing voices and glorify Thy dominion, granting them to be enlightened by Thy beauty, and to receive and purely enjoy sweet and fair communion with Thee; where Angels dance around Thy throne, and the ranks of the saints stand rejoicing; with them grant rest unto Thy servants, and great mercy!

*Verse: Their souls shall dwell among good things.*[^1297]

Where is the choir of Prophets, the ranks of Apostles and martyrs, and all who from the beginning have been justified by Thy saving Passion and blood, by which Thou didst redeem captive man; there give rest with faith unto those who have fallen asleep, as the Lover of mankind, forgiving their transgressions; for Thou alone in truth didst live without sin upon earth, Thou alone art free among the dead;[^1298] therefore grant rest unto Thy servants, and great mercy!

*Glory, both now, Theotokion:*

From the law of sin hast thou freed us who were enslaved, O Lady, having conceived in thy womb Christ the Lawgiver and King, O only Virgin Mother, by Whose gift and grace we are justified; Whom do thou now entreat, that He may write the souls of those who acknowledge thee as the Mother of God in the Book of Life;[^1299] that being saved through thine intercession, O all-immaculate one, we may obtain the beloved redemption of thy Son, worshipping Him Who grants great mercy unto the world!

*ON SUNDAY AT VESPERS*

*At "Lord, I have cried," Penitential Stichera, Tone 6:*

At Thy dread coming, O Christ, may we not hear: "I know you not";[^1300] for in Thee, O Savior, have we placed our hope; and even though through our negligence we kept not Thy commandments, yet spare our souls, we pray Thee!

I have not acquired repentance, nor yet tears; therefore I pray Thee, O Christ God, before the end turn me, and grant me compunction, that I may be delivered from torment!

Finding me stripped of virtues, the enemy wounded me with the arrow of sin; but Thou, as Physician of souls and bodies, heal the wounds of my soul, O God, and have mercy on me!

Heal the sores of my heart that have grown within me from many transgressions, O Savior, as Physician of souls and bodies, granting forgiveness of transgressions unto those who ask; ever grant me tears of repentance, and bestow upon me the remission of my debts, O Lord, and have mercy on me!

*Then three from the Triodion, and three of the saint from the Menaion.*

*ON MONDAY AT MATINS*

*After the first stichology, Penitential Sessional Hymns, Tone 6:*

I consider the dread day, and I weep for my wicked deeds: How shall I answer the immortal King? Or with what boldness shall I, a prodigal, look upon the Judge? O compassionate Father, O only-begotten Son, O Holy Spirit, have mercy on me!

*Verse: O Lord, rebuke me not in Thine anger.*[^1301]

In the valley of weeping, in the place which Thou hast appointed,[^1302] when Thou shalt sit, O Merciful One, to execute righteous judgment, expose not my hidden secrets, neither put me to shame before the Angels; but spare me, O God, and have mercy on me!

*Glory, both now, Theotokion:*

The most glorious Mother of God, who is holier than the holy Angels, let us unceasingly hymn with heart and lips, confessing her to be the Theotokos, as having truly given birth unto God incarnate, and praying unceasingly for our souls!

*At the Sixth Ode, Martyricon:*

Light is ever with the righteous;[^1303] for the holy ones, having been enlightened by Thee, shine continually as luminaries, having quenched the lamp of the ungodly; by their prayers, O our Savior, Thou dost enlighten my lamp, O Lord, and save me!

*ON TUESDAY AT MATINS*

*After the first stichology, Penitential Sessional Hymns, Tone 6:*

Grant me the vigilance of the wise virgins, O Lord, and enlighten the lamp of my soul with the oil of Thy compassions,[^1304] that I may cry unto Thee the angelic hymn: Alleluia!

*Verse: O Lord, rebuke me not in Thine anger.*

Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us; for being destitute of all defense, this prayer do we sinners offer unto Thee as Master: Have mercy on us!

*Glory, both now, Theotokion:*

Open unto us the doors of loving-kindness, O blessed Theotokos, that hoping in thee we may not perish, but may be delivered by thee from tribulations; for thou art the salvation of the Christian race!

*At the Sixth Ode, Martyricon:*

Having endured the contest of suffering, O holy ones, and having received from Thee the prizes of victory, they brought to naught the wiles of the lawless, and received incorruptible crowns; through them, O God, grant us great mercy!

*ON WEDNESDAY AT MATINS*

*After the first stichology, Sessional Hymns of the Cross, Tone 6:*

Today the prophetic word has been fulfilled; for behold, we worship at the place where Thy feet stood, O Lord;[^1305] and having tasted of the Tree of salvation, we have obtained freedom from sinful passions, by the prayers of the Theotokos, O only Lover of mankind!

*Verse: Exalt ye the Lord our God.*[^1306]

Thy Cross, O Lord, is sanctified; for in it healings are bestowed upon those ailing in sins; falling down before Thee through it, have mercy on us!

*Glory, both now, Stavrotheotokion:*

The ever-virgin Maiden who bore Thee, O Christ, beholding Thee lifted up upon the Cross for our sake, had her soul wounded with the sword of sorrow,[^1307] and wept, lamenting as a mother; by her prayers have mercy on us, O Lord of mercy!

*At the Sixth Ode, Martyricon:*

Suffering endurance in the contest, the torturers' wounds upon the martyrs, and the ranks of the bodiless stood holding the prizes of victory; they astonished torturers and kings, being most wise; they cast down Belial by the confession of Christ; O Lord Who didst strengthen them, glory to Thee!

*ON THURSDAY AT MATINS*

*After the first stichology, Sessional Hymns of the Apostles, Tone 6:*

As Thou didst come into the midst of Thy disciples, O Savior, giving peace unto them, come also unto us, and save us!

*Verse: Their sound is gone out into all the earth.*[^1308]

Thy disciples, O Jesus, being sent unto the ends of the earth, catching the nations in piety like fish,[^1309] brought them unto Thy goodness, O Lord; and through them we cry aloud unto Thee, O Lover of mankind: Grant great mercy unto Thy people!

*Glory, both now, Theotokion:*

O holy Lady, pure Mother of our God, who didst ineffably give birth unto the Creator of all, entreat His goodness together with the holy Apostles ever to deliver us from passions, and to grant us remission of sins!

*At the Sixth Ode, Martyricon:*

The memory of Thy passion-bearers, O Lord, has been revealed as the paradise which is in Eden; for all creation rejoices in it; and by their prayers, O Christ, grant us peace and great mercy!

*ON FRIDAY AT MATINS*

*After the first stichology, Sessional Hymns of the Cross, Tone 6:*

No sooner was the wood of Thy Cross set up, O Christ, than the foundations of death were shaken, O Lord; for that which Hades eagerly swallowed down, it cast forth with trembling; Thou hast revealed Thy salvation unto us, O Holy One; and we glorify Thee, O Son of God: have mercy on us!

*Verse: Exalt ye the Lord our God.*

O Lord, the Jews condemned Thee unto death, the Life of all; they who passed through the Red Sea by the rod nailed Thee upon the Cross; and they who sucked honey out of the rock brought gall unto Thee;[^1310] but willingly didst Thou endure it, that Thou mightest deliver us from the bondage of the enemy; O Christ God, glory to Thee!

*Glory, both now, Stavrotheotokion:*

O Virgin Theotokos, entreat Thy Son, Who was willingly nailed upon the Cross, and delivered the world from deceit, Christ our God, that He may have mercy on our souls!

*At the Sixth Ode, Martyricon:*

Those who proclaimed Christ at the tribunal and feared not the threats of the lawless, the Lord has made marvelous; for by patient suffering they cast down the insolence of the lawless, and worthily received from Christ the grace of healings, unceasingly praying that our souls may be saved!

*ON FRIDAY EVENING*

*At "Lord, I have cried," after the Idiomelon Sticheron, Martyrica, Tone 6:*

Thy martyrs, O Lord, did not deny Thee, nor did they depart from Thy commandments; by their prayers have mercy on us!

They who suffered for Thy sake, O Christ, endured many torments, and received perfect crowns in the heavens, that they may pray for our souls!

Passion-bearing martyrs, citizens of heaven, having suffered upon earth, ye endured many torments; by their prayers, O Lord, and by their supplication, preserve us all!

Thy Cross, O Lord, became an invincible weapon unto the martyrs; for seeing death lying before them, and foreseeing the life to come, they were strengthened by their hope in Thee; by their prayers have mercy on us!

*Glory, for the Departed:*

Thy creative command was my beginning and foundation; for desiring to compose me as a living creature out of invisible and visible nature, Thou didst fashion my body from the earth, and gavest me a soul by Thy divine and life-creating inbreathing;[^1311] therefore, O Savior, give rest unto Thy servants in the land of the living, and in the tabernacles of the righteous!

*Both now, Dogmaticon:*

*ON SATURDAY AT MATINS*

*After the first stichology, Martyric Sessional Hymns, Tone 6:*

Having endured the contest of suffering, O holy ones, ye received from Him the prizes of victory; ye brought to naught the devices of the lawless, and received incorruptible crowns; being entreated by them, O God, grant us great mercy!

*Verse: Marvelous is God in His saints, the God of Israel.*

The courageous standing in the contest, and the torturers' wounds upon the martyrs; and the ranks of the bodiless stood holding the prizes of victory; the wise astonished the torturers, and kings, being most wise; they cast down the apostate by the confession of Christ; O Lord Who didst strengthen them, glory to Thee!

*Verse: Unto the saints that are in His earth, the Lord hath made marvelous all His desires in them.*

O Lord, the memory of Thy saints has today been revealed as the paradise which is in Eden, for all creation rejoices in it; and by their entreaties Thou dost grant us peace and great mercy!

*Glory, for the Departed:*

Truly all things are vanity, and life is but a shadow and a dream; for in vain does every earthly-born man trouble himself, even as the Scripture said: When we have acquired the world, then do we dwell in the grave, where kings and paupers are together;[^1312] therefore, O Christ God, give rest unto those who have departed, as the Lover of mankind!

*Both now, Theotokion:*

Thou Who didst call Thy Mother blessed, didst come unto Thy Passion by voluntary counsel, having shone forth upon the Cross, desiring to seek out Adam, saying unto the Angels: "Rejoice with Me, for the lost drachma is found";[^1313] Thou Who hast wisely ordered all things, O our God, glory to Thee!

*At the Praises, Martyrica, Tone 6:*

O Lord, in the memory of Thy saints all creation keeps festival: the heavens rejoice with the Angels, and the earth is glad with men; by their prayers have mercy on us!

O Lord, if we had not Thy saints as intercessors, and Thy goodness showing mercy upon us, how should we dare, O Savior, to hymn Thee, Whom the Angels unceasingly glorify? O Knower of hearts, spare our souls!

The memory of the martyrs is joy unto those who fear the Lord; for having suffered for the sake of Christ, they received crowns from Him; and now with boldness they pray for our souls!

Our God hath made marvelous His chosen saints; rejoice and be glad, all ye His servants; for He hath prepared crowns and His Kingdom for you; but we pray you, forget us not!

*Glory, for the Departed:*

Sickness came unto Adam through the tasting of the tree of old in Eden, when the serpent disgorged his venom; for on account of it all-generational death entered, devouring man; but the Master, having come, cast down the serpent, and granted us resurrection;[^1314] unto Him therefore let us cry aloud: Spare, O Savior, and give rest with the saints unto those whom Thou hast received, as the Lover of mankind!

*Both now, Theotokion:*

Thou art our God, Who in wisdom hast done all things and dost fulfill them; Thou didst send Prophets, O Christ, to foretell Thy coming, and Apostles to preach Thy mighty acts; and the former indeed prophesied Thy coming, while the latter enlightened the nations by baptism; and the martyrs obtained that which they desired; and the choir of both, together with Her who bore Thee, entreats Thee: Give rest, O Lord, unto the souls which Thou hast received, and make us worthy of Thy Kingdom, O Thou Who didst endure crucifixion for the sake of me who was condemned, O my Redeemer and God!

*At the Aposticha, Stichera for the Departed, Tone 6, Podoben: "Having laid aside all earthly hope" (Всѐ ѿло́жше):*

Thou Who hast incomprehensible loving-kindness toward us, and an inexhaustible fountain of divine goodness, O Most Merciful One, settle those who have departed unto Thee in faith in the land of the living, in the beloved and longed-for tabernacles, granting them an abiding possession that endures forever; for Thou, O Savior, didst shed Thy blood for all, and with a life-bearing price didst redeem the world!

*Verse: Their souls shall dwell among good things.*

Thou didst willingly endure life-creating slaying, and didst pour forth life, and gavest eternal food unto the faithful, wherein do Thou rank those who have fallen asleep in the hope of resurrection, forgiving all their transgressions by Thy grace, as the only Sinless One, and the only Good One and Lover of mankind, that Thy name, O Christ, may be hymned by all, and that we may glorify Thy saving love for mankind!

*Verse: Blessed are they whom Thou hast chosen and received, O Lord.*
