At Matins: At "God is the Lord," the troparion of the Forerunner, twice; Glory: Of Theodore; Both now: Theotokion: "All beyond comprehension." After the first Kathisma: Both sessional hymns of the Forerunner; Glory, both now: Theotokion; and a reading of the Forerunner. After the second Kathisma: Sessional hymn of Theodore; Glory, both now: Theotokion; and a reading of the Forerunner, or of Theodore. Polyeleos, and the sessional hymn of the Forerunner, twice; Glory, both now: Theotokion; and a reading of the Forerunner. The Anabathmoi, the first antiphon of Tone 4. Prokeimenon; "Let every breath"; Gospel of the Forerunner; Psalm 50; sticheron of the Forerunner. Canon of the Forerunner, with the heirmos on 6; and of Theodore, both canons, on 8. Katavasia: "I will open my mouth." Canticles 7 and 9 we say beforehand on Friday. After Ode 3: Kontakion, and Ikos, and sessional hymn of the Forerunner; Glory: Of Theodore; Both now: Theotokion; and a reading concerning Saint Theodore. After Ode 6: Kontakion of Theodore, and the Ikos; and we read the Prologue and Synaxarion. After Ode 9: Exapostilarion of the Forerunner; Glory: Of Theodore; Both now: Theotokion. At the Praises: Stichera of the Forerunner, podoben, 3; and of Theodore, podoben, 3. Then the refrain: "The righteous man shall be glad"; and we chant the automelon sticheron of the Forerunner, Tone 6: "The all-honorable head"; Glory: Of Theodore; Both now: "O Theotokos, thou art the vine." Great Doxology. Troparion of the Forerunner; Glory: Of Theodore; Both now: Theotokion; the litanies, and the dismissal. And the customary departure into the narthex, and the First Hour. At the Hours: Troparion of the Forerunner; Glory: Of Theodore; Both now: Theotokion of the Hours. The kontakia we say alternating. At the Liturgy: The Beatitudes of the Forerunner, Ode 3, on 4; and of Theodore, Ode 6, on 4. After the Entrance: Troparion of the Forerunner, and of Theodore; and his kontakion. Glory: Of the Forerunner; Both now: Of the Theotokos of the Temple, or: "Steadfast Protectress of Christians." Prokeimenon, Alleluia, and Communion verse: Of the Forerunner and of Theodore, one. The Apostle and the Gospel: First for Saturday, and of Theodore combined, then of the Forerunner.

*And if the Finding of the Precious Head of John the Forerunner occurs on the First Sunday of the Fasts:*[^1440]
His service is sung as indicated on the Third Sunday of the Fasts, except for the veneration of the Cross; only at the Litiya, Glory: Of the Forerunner, written at "Lord, I have cried"; Both now: Of the Triodion. At the Aposticha, Glory: Of the Forerunner; Both now: Of the Triodion. At "God is the Lord," the Resurrection troparion, twice; Glory: Of the Forerunner; Both now: "Thy pure icon." Katavasia of the Triodion.

*And if the Finding of the Precious Head of the Forerunner occurs on Monday of the Second, or Third, or Fourth Weeks of the Fasts:*[^1441]
On Sunday evening we chant: "Blessed is the man," the first antiphon. At "Lord, I have cried": Stichera on 10; of the Triodion of the day, on 4, repeating the first; and of the Forerunner, on 6; Glory: Of the Forerunner; Both now: The first Theotokion. Entrance, Great Prokeimenon of the Triodion; and the Old Testament readings of the Forerunner, 3. Then: "Vouchsafe, O Lord, in this evening"; and "Let us complete our evening prayer." At the Aposticha of the Triodion: Idiomelon of the day, twice; and the Martyr-hymn; Glory: Of the Forerunner; Both now: Resurrection Theotokion, according to the Tone. After the "Our Father": Troparion of the Forerunner; Glory, both now: Resurrection Theotokion. Litany: "Have mercy on us, O God"; and 3 great prostrations, and the dismissal. The Midnight Office we chant according to custom, with the Kathisma and the customary troparia. After "More honorable," 3 great prostrations.
At Matins: At "God is the Lord," the troparion of the Forerunner, twice; Glory, both now: Theotokion. After the first and second Kathismata we say the sessional hymns of the Triodion; the litanies are not said; and a reading in Ephrem. After the third Kathisma, the priest says the small litany; and both sessional hymns of the Forerunner; and a reading of the Forerunner. Polyeleos, and the sessional hymn of the Forerunner, twice; Glory, both now: Theotokion; and a reading of the Forerunner. The Anabathmoi, the first antiphon of Tone 4. Prokeimenon, and the Gospel of the Forerunner. Then Psalm 50; sticheron of the Forerunner. Canon of the Forerunner, with the heirmos on 8. Katavasia: "I will open my mouth." But where there is a triode: We chant the canon of the Forerunner, with the heirmos on 6, and the triode on 8. Katavasia of the Triodion. After Ode 3: Sessional hymn of the Forerunner, twice; Glory, both now: Theotokion; and a reading of the Forerunner. After Ode 6: Kontakion and Ikos, and the Prologue. Exapostilarion of the Forerunner, twice; Glory, both now: Theotokion. At the Praises: Stichera of the Forerunner, on 4; Glory: Of the Forerunner; Both now: His Theotokion. Then the superior or the reader says: "Glory to Thee Who hast shown us the light." After this, the litany: "Let us complete our morning prayer." Then at the Aposticha of the Triodion: Idiomelon of the day, twice; and the Martyr-hymn. Glory: Of the Forerunner; Both now:

Theotokion. After this: "It is a good thing to give thanks," we say once. After the "Our Father": Troparion of the Forerunner; Glory, both now: Resurrection Theotokion. Litany: "Have mercy on us, O God"; and 3 great prostrations, without dismissal, and the First Hour.
At the Hours we say the troparion of the Forerunner; and after the Trisagion, his kontakion; and at the end, 6 great prostrations. And after the prostrations, the Trisagion we do not say, but we say: "O Christ, the true Light"; and the dismissal. The Third, Sixth, and Ninth Hours we chant with Kathismata, at their appropriate time, with a reading. At the Sixth Hour, the Old Testament reading of the day is read, according to its order.
The prayers of Basil the Great after the Hours we say without change, namely: "O Master, God the Father," and "O God and Lord of hosts," and "O Master, Lord Jesus Christ." When we chant the Polyeleos, at the Hours we do not strike the bell. After the Kathisma: Alleluia, three times; then: "Lord, have mercy," three times; and the reader says: "Glory," the troparion of the Forerunner; "Both now," the Theotokion of the Hours. After the "Our Father": Kontakion of the Forerunner. After "More honorable," 3 great prostrations. After the Ninth Hour, the Beatitudes we say quickly without chanting. After "Remit, forgive": Kontakion of the Temple; Glory: Of the Forerunner; Both now: Of the Temple of the Theotokos. But if there is no Temple of the Theotokos: "Both now: Steadfast Protectress of Christians." After this: "Lord, have mercy," 40. Glory, both now: "More honorable than the Cherubim"; and 10 great prostrations. Then the prayer: "All-Holy Trinity." And we begin Vespers according to custom: The superior or reader says: "Come, let us worship," three times. And we chant Vespers with prostrations, according to the Lenten order. After the customary Kathisma, at "Lord, I have cried," stichera on 10: Idiomelon of the day from the Triodion, twice; and the Martyr-hymn; and podoben of the Triodion, 3; and of the Forerunner, 4. Glory: Of the Forerunner; Both now: The customary Theotokion according to the Tone. But if toward Wednesday or Friday, we say the Stavrotheotokion, according to the Tone of the Doxasticon. Entrance with the Gospel. "O Joyful Light"; and the Prokeimenon, and the readings of the day. "Let my prayer be set forth"; and 3 great prostrations. Small litanies we do not say. Prokeimenon, Apostle, Alleluia, Gospel of the Forerunner. Communion verse: "In everlasting remembrance"; and of the Forerunner. The Liturgy of the Presanctified according to custom.
At the dismissal, the priest commemorates first the celebrated saint, afterwards the saint of the coming day. Of the saint occurring in order, we chant the canon at Matins according to order; and his stichera that are written in the evening at "Lord, I have cried," we say them at the Praises.
And if, by reason of any great necessity, on the commemoration of great saints having a Polyeleos, it should not happen that the Presanctified Liturgy is celebrated, we chant the Hours as said above.[^1442] After the Ninth Hour, and after the prayer: "O Master, Lord Jesus Christ," we say also the psalm: "Bless the Lord, O my soul"; Glory: "Praise the Lord, O my soul"; Both now: "Only-begotten Son and Word"; and "In Thy Kingdom," quickly without chanting. At the Beatitudes we say of the Forerunner, Odes 3 and 6. Then the Apostle and the Gospel of the Forerunner. After this: "Remember us, O Lord." After "Remit, forgive," and after the "Our Father": Kontakion of the Temple; Glory: Of the Forerunner; Both now: Of the Theotokos of the Temple. But if there is no Temple of the Theotokos: "Steadfast Protectress of Christians." Then: "Lord, have mercy," 40. And 3 great prostrations, and at that time the paraecclesiarch tolls two bells.[^1443]
And after the three great prostrations we say: "Come, let us worship." And we chant VESPERS, with prostrations, and the customary Kathisma. At "Lord, I have cried": Stichera of the Triodion, podoben, 3; and of Saint Tarasios, 3.[^1444] Glory, both now: Theotokion. But if toward Wednesday or Friday, we say: Glory, both now: Stavrotheotokion. Then: "O Joyful Light"; Prokeimenon, and the reading of the Triodion of the day. At the Aposticha, of the day from the Triodion. After "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart," and after the "Our Father": Troparion: "O Theotokos Virgin, rejoice"; and the rest according to the Lenten order. After "More honorable," and after the prostrations, we say the Trisagion; "Lord, have mercy," 12; "All-Holy Trinity." Then: "Blessed be the name of the Lord," and 3 prostrations; and "I will bless the Lord"; "It is truly meet"; and the dismissal. At the dismissal he commemorates the saint of the coming day. After the dismissal we enter into the refectory, and eat two cooked dishes with oil, and drink wine. On Wednesday and Friday, however, we eat two cooked dishes without oil, and drink wine.

*And if the Finding of the Precious Head of the Forerunner occurs on one of the Fasting Days:*[^1445]
We chant his service thus: At the Hours, after "Remit, forgive," and after the "Our Father": Kontakion according to the Typikon. Then: "Lord, have mercy," 40; Glory, both now: "More honorable than the Cherubim"; and after the prostrations we say the Trisagion; "Lord, have mercy," 12; and "All-Holy Trinity." And immediately we begin Vespers; and the customary Kathisma. Small litanies are said after each antiphon. At "Lord, I have cried": Stichera on 10: Idiomelon of the day, twice; and the Martyr-hymn; and podoben of the Triodion, 3; and of the Forerunner, 4. Glory: Of the Forerunner; Both now: "Who would not call thee blessed." Entrance. Then the Prokeimenon, and the reading of the day; and of the Forerunner, 3 readings. Then we chant: "Let my prayer be set forth"; and 10 prostrations. And in order, the Liturgy of the Presanctified. And where there is no Presanctified, after "Remit, forgive," and after the great prostrations, the reader says: "Come, let us worship," three times, and 3 prostrations. Then the psalm: "Bless the Lord, O my soul"; and we chant Vespers without prostrations. After the customary Kathisma: Stichera on 6: Of the Triodion, podoben, 3; and of the Forerunner, 3. Glory: Of the Forerunner; Both now: Theotokion: "Who would not call thee blessed." Entrance, and "O Joyful Light"; Prokeimenon; and the reading of the day, and of the Forerunner; and immediately: "Vouchsafe, O Lord." Then: "Let us complete our evening prayer." At the Aposticha, of the Triodion; Glory: Of the Forerunner; Both now: Theotokion according to the Tone. "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart." After the Trisagion: Troparion of the Forerunner; Glory, both now: "The mystery hidden from the ages." Litany: "Have mercy on us, O God." After this, 3 great prostrations, and the prayer: "All-Holy Trinity"; and "I will bless the Lord"; "It is truly meet"; and the dismissal. We chant Great Compline without prostrations. After the first Trisagion: Troparion of the Forerunner; Glory, both now: Resurrection Theotokion according to the Tone. After the second Trisagion: The customary troparia: "Have mercy on us, O Lord." After "It is truly meet," and after the Trisagion: Kontakion of the Forerunner; and "O Lord of hosts, be with us," we do not chant. After "More honorable," three great prostrations;

prostrations; the Trisagion we do not say, but the small dismissal. The Midnight Office we chant according to custom, with the Kathisma, as prescribed on Monday of the Second Week of the Fast. Likewise also Matins, and the entire service of the Forerunner.

*If the Finding of the Precious Head of the Forerunner occurs on the Second or Third Saturday of the Fasts:*[^1446]
On Friday evening, the appointed Kathisma. At "Lord, I have cried": Stichera on 10; idiomelon of the Triodion, twice; and of the Octoechos, Martyr-hymns, 4. Glory: Of the Forerunner; Both now: The first Theotokion of the Tone. Entrance, Prokeimenon, and the reading of the day; and of the Forerunner, 3. "Let my prayer be set forth"; and the rest of the Presanctified. But if there is no Presanctified: At "Lord, I have cried," stichera of the Forerunner, on 6; Glory: Of the Forerunner; Both now: The first Theotokion of the Tone. Entrance, Prokeimenon, and reading of the day, and of the saint. Then: "Vouchsafe, O Lord." At the Aposticha: Idiomelon of the Triodion, twice; and the Martyr-hymn of the Octoechos, according to the Tone. Glory: Of the Forerunner; Both now: Theotokion. After "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart": Troparion of the Forerunner; Glory, both now: Resurrection Theotokion of the current Tone. Litany, and 3 prostrations. Then the prayer: "All-Holy Trinity"; "Blessed be the name of the Lord"; and Psalm 33: "I will bless the Lord"; "It is truly meet"; and the dismissal.
Compline is Great, at which we chant the four-ode canon of the Saturday. At Matins and at the Hours we chant of the Forerunner alone. At the Liturgy: The service of the day and of the Forerunner.

*If the Finding of the Head of John the Forerunner occurs on the Second Sunday of the Fasts:*[^1447]
On Saturday evening, at Small Vespers: Resurrection stichera, and of the Theotokos according to custom. At Great Vespers: At "Lord, I have cried," Resurrection stichera, 3; and Anatolian, 1; and of the Forerunner, on 6. Glory: Of the Forerunner; Both now: The first Theotokion of the Tone. Entrance, and the readings of the Forerunner. At the Litiya: The sticheron of the Temple; and the Aposticha of the Forerunner. At the Aposticha: Resurrection stichera, alphabetically. Glory: Of the Forerunner; Both now: Theotokion. At the Blessing of the Loaves: "O Theotokos Virgin," three times. And a reading in the Apostolic Epistles. At "God is the Lord": Resurrection troparion, twice; Glory: Of the Forerunner; Both now: Theotokion, according to the Tone of the troparion. After the Kathismata: Resurrection sessional hymns, and their Theotokia; and a reading in the Gospel. Polyeleos, and the sessional hymns of the Forerunner, both. Glory: Sessional hymn after the Polyeleos; Both now: Theotokion; and a reading of the Forerunner. The Anabathmoi, and the Prokeimenon of the Tone; and the Resurrection Gospel. Psalm 50. Glory: Sticheron, Tone 2: "Open unto me the gates of repentance"; and the rest. Resurrection canon, with the heirmos on 4; and of the Triodion on 4; and of the Forerunner on 6. Katavasia: "I will open my mouth." After Ode 3: Kontakion of the Triodion; then the kontakion of the Forerunner, and the Ikos, and his sessional hymn, twice. Glory, both now: Theotokion; and a reading of the Forerunner. After Ode 6: Kontakion and Ikos of the Forerunner, and the Synaxarion. At Ode 9 we chant "More honorable"; Resurrection exapostilarion; Glory: Of the Forerunner; Both now: Of the Triodion. At the Praises: Resurrection stichera, 4; and of the Forerunner, 4, with the Doxasticon, and his refrains. Then the refrain: "Arise, O Lord my God"; and we chant the automelon sticheron of the Triodion: Tone 6: "Daniel the prophet"; Glory: Of the Forerunner; Both now: "Most blessed art thou." Great Doxology, and the rest according to custom. At the Liturgy: The Beatitudes of the Tone, on 4; and of the Forerunner, Ode 3, on 4; and of the Triodion, Ode 6, on 4. After the Entrance: Resurrection troparion, and of the Forerunner. Glory: His kontakion; Both now: Of the Triodion. Prokeimenon, Apostle, Gospel, and Communion verse: First of the day, and of the Forerunner.

*If the Finding of the Precious Head of the Forerunner occurs on the Third Sunday of the Fasts, which is the Veneration of the Cross:*[^1448]
On Saturday at Small Vespers: Resurrection stichera, 4; and of the Theotokos according to custom. At the Aposticha: Resurrection sticheron, 1; and of the Cross, automelon, 3; Glory, both now: Of the Cross. Troparion of the Cross; Glory: Of the Forerunner; Both now: Theotokion of the Tone. At Great Vespers: "Blessed is the man," the entire Kathisma. At "Lord, I have cried": Resurrection stichera, 3; and of the Cross, podoben, 3; and of the Forerunner, podoben, 4. Glory: Of the Cross, Tone 3: "O Christ our God"; Both now: The first Theotokion of the Tone. Entrance, Prokeimenon, and the readings of the Forerunner, 3. At the Litiya: The sticheron of the Temple; and of the Cross, the automelon, Tone 2: "Hail, life-bearing Cross"; and of the Forerunner, 2; Glory: Of the Forerunner; Both now: Of the Cross. At the Aposticha: Resurrection stichera, alphabetically; Glory: Of the Cross; Both now: Theotokion according to the Tone. At the Blessing of the Loaves: Troparion of the Cross, twice; and of the Forerunner, once; and a reading in the Apostolic Epistles.
At Matins: At "God is the Lord," the Resurrection troparion, twice; Glory: Of the Cross; Both now: Of the Forerunner. After the Kathismata: Resurrection sessional hymns, and their Theotokia; and a reading in the Gospel. Polyeleos, and the sessional hymns of the Forerunner, all once each; Glory: Sessional hymn after the Polyeleos; Both now: Theotokion; and a reading of the Forerunner. The Anabathmoi, and the Prokeimenon of the Tone; and the Resurrection Gospel. "Having seen the Resurrection of Christ"; Psalm 50. Glory: "Open unto me the gates of repentance"; and the rest. Resurrection canon on 4; and of the Cross on 4; and of the Forerunner on 6. Katavasia of the Cross: "Moses the divine." After Ode 3: Kontakion of the Forerunner, and the Ikos; and the sessional hymn of the Cross; Glory: Of the Forerunner; Both now: Sessional hymn of the Cross. After Ode 6: Kontakion of the Cross, and the Ikos, and the Synaxarion. At Ode 9 we chant "More honorable"; Resurrection exapostilarion; Glory: Of the Forerunner; Both now: Of the Cross. At the Praises: Resurrection stichera, 4; and of the Cross, 3; and of the Forerunner with the Doxasticon, 4, with his refrains. Glory: Of the Cross; Both now: "Most blessed art thou." Great Doxology, and the procession of the Precious Cross according to custom. At the Liturgy: The Beatitudes of the Tone, on 4; and of the Cross, Ode 3, on 4; and of the Forerunner, Ode 6, on 4. Instead of the Trisagion: "Before Thy Cross." Prokeimenon, Apostle, Gospel, and Communion verse: First of the Sunday, then of the Cross, and of the Forerunner.

*Instruction concerning the Holy Forty Martyrs:*[^1449]
*If the commemoration of the Holy Forty Martyrs occurs on Saturday of the First, Second, Third, or Fourth Weeks of the Fasts:*
The entire service is sung as indicated above for the Finding of the Head of the Forerunner, without change.

*If the Holy Forty Martyrs occurs on Wednesday of the Fourth Week:*[^1450]
Their service is sung on Tuesday, on the eve, as indicated for the Finding of the Head of the Forerunner on fasting days; on Wednesday, however, we chant the service of the Cross.

*If the Holy Forty Martyrs occurs on Thursday of the Great Canon:*[^1451]
Their service is sung on Tuesday of that week; and on Wednesday evening we chant the Great Canon with its readings.

*If the Holy Forty Martyrs occurs on the Saturday of the Akathist:*[^1452]
Their service is sung on the Fifth Sunday of the Fasts, as indicated for the Second Sunday of the Fasts.

*Instruction concerning the Forefeast of the Annunciation of the Most Holy Theotokos:*[^1453]
*If the Forefeast of the Annunciation occurs on any day of the week, except Saturday and Sunday:*
On the eve, at the Ninth Hour, we say the troparion and kontakion of the day from the Triodion. After the prayer of Saint Ephrem: "Come, let us worship," three times, with 3 prostrations; and the reader begins the prooemiac Psalm. And we chant Vespers with Kathisma and prostrations. At "Lord, I have cried": Stichera on 10; idiomelon of the day from the Triodion, twice; and the Martyr-hymn; and podoben of the Triodion, 3; and of the forefeast, 4. Glory, both now: Of the forefeast. Entrance, Prokeimenon, and the readings of the day. "Let my prayer be set forth"; and the rest of the Presanctified. But if there is no Presanctified, at "Lord, I have cried," stichera on 6: Podoben of the Triodion, 3; and of the forefeast, 3. Glory, both now: Of the forefeast. Entrance, "O Joyful Light"; Prokeimenon and the readings of the day. Then: "Vouchsafe, O Lord." At the Aposticha: Idiomelon of the day from the Triodion, twice; and the Martyr-hymn. Glory, both now: Of the forefeast. After "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart": Troparion of the forefeast; and 3 great prostrations, and the dismissal.
At Compline: We chant the triode or tetraode of the Triodion; troparion and kontakion of the forefeast.
At Matins: At "God is the Lord," troparion of the forefeast, three times. The customary Kathismata, with sessional hymns of the Triodion; and the biblical canticles. Canon of the forefeast, with the heirmos on 6; and of the Triodion on 8. After Ode 3: Sessional hymn of the forefeast; Glory, both now: Sessional hymn of the forefeast. After Ode 6: Kontakion and Ikos of the forefeast. After Ode 9: Exapostilarion of the forefeast, twice; Glory, both now: Exapostilarion of the forefeast. At the Praises: Stichera of the forefeast, 4. Glory, both now: Of the forefeast. Small Doxology, read. At the Aposticha: Idiomelon of the day from the Triodion, twice; and the Martyr-hymn. Glory, both now: Of the forefeast. "It is a good thing to give thanks." Troparion of the forefeast; litany, and 3 great prostrations; and the First Hour with Kathisma. At all the Hours: Troparion and kontakion of the forefeast; and the prayer of Saint Ephrem with prostrations.

*If the Forefeast of the Annunciation occurs on the Third or Fourth Saturday of the Fasts:*[^1454]
On Friday evening, at the Ninth Hour, we toll two small bells; and after the prayer of Saint Ephrem, we begin Great Vespers with the Presanctified Liturgy. At "Lord, I have cried": Stichera on 10; idiomelon of the day from the Triodion, twice; and of the Octoechos, Martyr-hymns, 4; and of the forefeast, 4. Glory, both now: Of the forefeast. Entrance, Prokeimenon, and the readings of the day. "Let my prayer be set forth"; and the Liturgy of the Presanctified.

Presanctified. But if there is no Presanctified: At "Lord, I have cried," stichera on 6: Of the Octoechos, Martyr-hymns, 3; and of the forefeast, 3. Glory, both now: Of the forefeast. Entrance, Prokeimenon, and readings of the day. "Vouchsafe, O Lord." At the Aposticha: Idiomelon of the day from the Triodion, twice; and the Martyr-hymn. Glory, both now: Of the forefeast. Troparion of the forefeast; litany, and 3 prostrations; and the dismissal.
At Compline: We chant the four-ode canon of the Triodion; troparion and kontakion of the forefeast.
At Matins: At "God is the Lord," troparion of the forefeast, three times. After the Kathismata: Sessional hymns of the Octoechos, and of the forefeast. Canon of the forefeast, with the heirmos on 6; and of the Triodion, tetraode, on 8. Katavasia of the Triodion. After Ode 3: Sessional hymn of the forefeast; Glory, both now: Sessional hymn of the forefeast. After Ode 6: Kontakion and Ikos of the forefeast. After Ode 9: Exapostilarion of the forefeast, twice. At the Praises: Stichera of the forefeast, 4. Glory, both now: Of the forefeast. Great Doxology. Troparion of the forefeast; litanies, and the dismissal. At the Liturgy: The Beatitudes of the forefeast, Ode 3, on 4; and of the Saturday, Ode 6, on 4. Prokeimenon, Apostle, Gospel, and Communion verse: First of the Saturday, then of the forefeast.

*If the Forefeast of the Annunciation occurs on the Third Sunday of the Fasts:*[^1455]
On Saturday at Small Vespers: Resurrection stichera, 4; and of the forefeast, 4. Glory, both now: Of the forefeast. At the Aposticha: Resurrection sticheron, 1; and of the Cross, 3. Glory, both now: Of the Cross. Troparion of the Cross; Glory: Of the forefeast; Both now: Resurrection Theotokion. At Great Vespers: "Blessed is the man," the entire Kathisma. At "Lord, I have cried": Resurrection stichera, 3; and of the Cross, 3; and of the forefeast, 4. Glory: Of the Cross; Both now: Of the forefeast. Entrance, Prokeimenon of the day. At the Litiya: The sticheron of the Temple, and of the Cross; Glory: Of the Cross; Both now: Of the forefeast. At the Aposticha: Resurrection stichera; Glory: Of the Cross; Both now: Of the forefeast. At the Blessing of the Loaves: Troparion of the Cross, twice; and of the forefeast, once.
At Matins: At "God is the Lord," Resurrection troparion, twice; Glory: Of the Cross; Both now: Of the forefeast. After the Kathismata: Resurrection sessional hymns; and of the Cross. Polyeleos, and the sessional hymns of the Cross; and the Resurrection Gospel. Canons: Resurrection on 4; and of the Cross on 4; and of the forefeast on 6. Katavasia of the Cross. After Ode 3: Kontakion and sessional hymn of the forefeast; Glory, both now: Sessional hymn of the Cross. After Ode 6: Kontakion and Ikos of the Cross, and the Synaxarion. At Ode 9: "More honorable"; Resurrection exapostilarion; Glory: Of the Cross; Both now: Of the forefeast. At the Praises: Resurrection stichera, 4; and of the Cross, 3; and of the forefeast with the Doxasticon, 4. Glory: Of the Cross; Both now: "Most blessed art thou." Great Doxology, and the procession of the Precious Cross. At the Liturgy: The Beatitudes of the Tone, on 4; and of the Cross, Ode 3, on 4; and of the forefeast, Ode 6, on 4. "Before Thy Cross." Prokeimenon, Apostle, Gospel, and Communion verse: First of the Sunday, then of the Cross, and of the forefeast.

*If the Forefeast of the Annunciation occurs on Mid-Lent Wednesday:*[^1456]
On Tuesday evening, the entire service of the forefeast is sung with the triode of the Cross, as indicated for fasting days; the prostrations are made, and at the First Hour the veneration of the Precious Cross takes place according to custom.

*If the Forefeast of the Annunciation occurs on Thursday of the Fourth Week of the Fasts:*[^1457]
On Wednesday evening, the Presanctified Liturgy is celebrated with the stichera of the Cross and of the forefeast. On Thursday morning, the service is sung as indicated for ordinary fasting days.

*If the Forefeast of the Annunciation occurs on the Fourth or Fifth Sunday of the Fasts:*[^1458]
On Saturday at Small Vespers: Stichera of the Resurrection, and of the forefeast. At Great Vespers: Stichera of the Resurrection, 3; Anatolian, 1; and of the Triodion, 3; and of the forefeast, 3. Glory: Of the Triodion; Both now: The first Theotokion of the Tone. At the Litiya and at the Aposticha: The hymns of the Triodion and of the forefeast. Troparion of the Resurrection; Glory: Of the forefeast; Both now: Resurrection Theotokion.
At Matins: Resurrection troparion, twice; Glory: Of the forefeast; Both now: Theotokion. Canons: Resurrection on 4; and of the Triodion on 4; and of the forefeast on 6. Katavasia: "I will open my mouth." After Ode 3: Kontakion and sessional hymn of the forefeast; Glory, both now: Of the Triodion. After Ode 6: Kontakion of the Triodion, and the Synaxarion. At Ode 9: "More honorable"; Resurrection exapostilarion; Glory: Of the forefeast; Both now: Of the Triodion. At the Praises: Resurrection stichera, 4; and of the Triodion, 4; and of the forefeast, 4. Great Doxology. At the Liturgy: The Beatitudes of the Tone, on 4; and of the Triodion, Ode 3, on 4; and of the forefeast, Ode 6, on 4. Prokeimenon, Apostle, Gospel, and Communion verse: First of the Sunday, then of the Triodion, and of the forefeast.

*If the Forefeast of the Annunciation occurs on the Fifth Saturday, of the Akathist:*[^1459]
On Friday evening, at "Lord, I have cried," we chant the automelon stichera of the day, twice; and the Martyr-hymn; and of the Akathist on 4; and of the forefeast, 3. Glory: Of the forefeast; Both now: Of the Akathist. Entrance, Prokeimenon, and the readings of the day. "Let my prayer be set forth"; and the rest of the Presanctified. The four-ode canon of the Triodion we chant at Compline. At Matins: At "God is the Lord," troparion of the Akathist, twice Glory, both now: Of the forefeast. And the customary Kathismata, the kontakia and ikoi of the Akathist according to their order. Canon of the forefeast, with the heirmos on 6; and of the Akathist on 8. Katavasia: "I will open my mouth." After Odes 3 and 6: Kontakia and ikoi according to custom. After Ode 9: Exapostilarion of the Akathist, twice; Glory, both now: Of the forefeast. At the Praises: Stichera of the Akathist on 4, Tone 4, podoben: "As one noble"; Glory, both now, Tone 4: "A language which he knew not." Great Doxology.

*If the Forefeast of the Annunciation occurs on Lazarus Saturday:*[^1460]
The service of the forefeast is sung beforehand on Thursday of that same week, as indicated in the chapter apart from Saturdays and Sundays.

# MARKIAN CHAPTERS (ANNUNCIATION DURING LENT)

## Instruction Concerning the Feast of the Annunciation of the Most Holy Theotokos[^1461]

It begins from Thursday of the Third Week of the Holy Fasts, and ascends unto Wednesday of Bright Week.
And if it is a fast day, we begin Vespers without Kathisma, and without prostrations. At "Lord, I have cried": We set 10 verses, and we chant in the Triodion the idiomelon of the day, twice; and the podoben, 3; and of the feast, 2, repeating two, Tone 6, podoben: "Having set aside all": "The pre-eternal Counsel"; Glory, both now, the same Tone: "The Archangel Gabriel was sent." Entrance. "O Joyful Light"; Prokeimenon. And the readings of the day; and of the feast, 3: First, from Genesis: "Jacob went forth from the well"; second, from the Prophecy of Ezekiel: "It shall come to pass from the eighth day"; third, from Proverbs: "Wisdom has built a house for herself." Then: "Let my prayer be set forth"; and three great prostrations; and the rest of the Presanctified. But if there is no Presanctified: At "Lord, I have cried," stichera: Podoben of the Triodion, 3; and of the feast, 5; Glory, both now: "The Archangel Gabriel was sent." Entrance, Prokeimenon, and readings of the day; and of the feast, 3. Then: "Vouchsafe, O Lord." At the Aposticha: Idiomelon of the day, twice; and the Martyr-hymn; Glory, both now: "Today is the joy." After "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart": Troparion of the feast. Litany, and three great prostrations, and the dismissal. In the refectory, we dispense for wine and oil, on whatever day it occurs, unto the glory of the Most Holy Theotokos.

*It is necessary to know: If the Annunciation occurs on any Saturday of the Fast:*[^1462]
The readings are read first of the day, and after these of the feast, 5: First: "Moses went in"; second: "The Lord created Me"; third: "Jacob went forth"; fourth: "It shall come to pass from the eighth day"; fifth: "Wisdom has built a house for herself." Similarly 5 readings of the feast are read if the Annunciation occurs also on a Sunday. But if it is a fast day, 3 are read in the evening, as written above; and at the Liturgy, 2: "Moses went in," and "The Lord created Me." At the first hour of the night, they strike the great bell sufficiently, and then all the bells. And having assembled in the church, the priest having given the blessing, and censing, we chant Great Compline, and "God is with us," with chanting, in Tone 8, by both choirs. And the customary troparia: "The day having passed." After the first Trisagion: Troparion of the feast: "Today is the fountainhead of our salvation"; after the second Trisagion: Kontakion of the feast: "To thee, the Champion Leader." And after the "Glory to God in the highest," we make the departure into the narthex. And the Litiya takes place according to custom, and we chant the idiomela stichera of the feast, 3, Tone 1; Glory, both now, Tone 2: "Gabriel announces the good tidings." Then the priest says the customary prayers of the vigil; and having entered into the church, we chant at the Aposticha the stichera of the feast, Tone 4, with the refrains of the feast: First: "Proclaim the good tidings of the salvation of our God from day to day"; second: "Sing unto the Lord a new song, sing unto the Lord, all the earth." Glory, both now, the same Tone: "Today is the joy of the Annunciation." At the Blessing of the Loaves: Troparion, Tone 4: "Today is the fountainhead of our salvation," three times. And "Blessed be the name of the Lord," with chanting, three times; Psalm 33: "I will bless the Lord," unto "They that seek the Lord shall not want any good thing." And the blessed loaves are distributed to the brethren, according to custom; and a reading of the feast.
At Matins: At "God is the Lord," troparion of the feast, three times; and we say three Kathismata. After the first Kathisma: Sessional hymns of the Triodion, both, without litany; and a reading of the day. After the second Kathisma: Litany, and sessional hymn of the feast, Tone 1, podoben: "Thy tomb": "The great commander"; Glory, both now: The same; and a reading of the feast. After the third Kathisma: Sessional hymn of the feast, Tone 3, podoben: "Awe-struck by the beauty of thy virginity": "Today all creation rejoices"; Glory, both now: The same. And after the reading, candles are given to the brethren. After the Polyeleos: Sessional hymn, Tone 4, podoben: "Joseph was astonished": "Gabriel from heaven"; Glory, both now, the same Tone: "Gabriel was sent unto the Virgin"; and a reading of the feast. The Anabathmoi, the first antiphon of Tone 4; Prokeimenon, Tone 4: "Proclaim the good tidings of the salvation of our God from day to day"; Verse: "Sing unto the Lord a new song." "Let every breath." Gospel of Luke, pericope 4: "Mary arose." After Psalm 50: Sticheron of the feast, Tone 2: "Gabriel announces the good tidings." Canon of the feast: The composition of Kyr Theophanes, Tone 4: The heirmoi twice, troparia on 12. Katavasia of the feast. But where there is a triode: We chant the canon of the feast, with the heirmos on 6, and the triode on 8. Katavasia: Heirmos of the Triodion, both choirs together. After Ode 3: Sessional hymn of the feast, Tone 8: "The Word of God"; Glory, both now, the same Tone: "He was sent." After Ode 6: Kontakion, Tone 8: "To thee, the Champion Leader," and the Ikos; and we read the Prologue. At Ode 9, the brethren again light the candles. "More honorable" we do not chant, but we chant the refrain of the feast: "Proclaim, O earth, glad tidings of great joy; praise, ye heavens, the glory of God." Then the heirmos: "Let no hand of the profane touch"; similarly also the second choir, the refrain and the heirmos; and unto the other troparia of the feast, the same refrain. With the triode, however, unto the troparia, the refrain: "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee." Unto the Theotokia, we chant the refrains of the feast. Then the heirmos of the Triodion, and the refrain of the feast, and the heirmos, both choirs together. Exapostilarion of the feast, twice, podoben: "With the disciples": "Of the angelic hosts"; Glory, both now: "That which from the ages is known today At the Praises: "Let every breath"; we set 4 verses, and chant stichera, Tone 1, podoben: "Joy of the heavenly ranks"; Glory, both now, Tone 2: "The mystery which was from eternity." [If it is a Saturday or a Sunday: Great Doxology, and the litanies, and the dismissal.] But if it is a fast day: We chant at the Aposticha of the Triodion, the idiomelon of the day, twice; and the Martyr-hymn. Glory, both now: Of the feast: "Let the heavens rejoice." Then: "It is a good thing to give thanks," once. After the "Our Father": Troparion of the feast. Litany, at the end 10 great prostrations, without dismissal of Matins, and the First Hour with Kathisma. Troparion and kontakion of the feast; and at the end, 10 great prostrations, and the prayer: "O Christ, the true Light." Holy oil is also given to the brethren. The idiomelon sticheron is chanted, and the dismissal. At the Third Hour of the day, we go forth with crosses and with a procession outside the monastery.[^1463] And having returned, we enter into the refectory, and chant the Hour: The Third and the Sixth with Kathismata, without prostrations; troparion and kontakion of the feast. At the Hours, we do not strike the bell. At the Sixth Hour: We chant the troparion, the Old Testament readings of the Triodion, and the rest according to their order, and the reading. And we read the homily whose beginning is: "Again the joy of the Annunciation."[^1464] We join also the Ninth Hour with Kathismata, and a reading. After this: The Beatitudes, quickly without chanting, and without prostrations: "Remember us, O Lord"; "The heavenly choir"; Glory: "The choir of holy angels"; "Remit, forgive." After the "Our Father": Kontakion of the feast; "Lord, have mercy," 40; Glory, both now: "More honorable"; and 3 great prostrations, and the prayer: "All-Holy Trinity"; and the dismissal. And we chant VESPERS without Kathisma, and without prostrations. At "Lord, I have cried": We chant the idiomelon of the Triodion of the day, twice, without the Martyr-hymn; and the podoben of the Triodion, 3; and of the feast, 3, Tone 4, idiomela, which are at the Aposticha. In order, the sixth of May; and of the Archangel, three times, Tone 4, podoben: "O all-praised martyrs." To the eleventh verse, the refrain: "Who makes His angels spirits."[^1465] Glory, both now: Of the feast: "The Archangel Gabriel was sent." The priest performs the Proskomide during the stichera. Entrance with the Gospel. "O Joyful Light"; Prokeimenon, and reading of the day; and of the feast, two: First, from Exodus: "Moses went in"; second, from Proverbs: "The Lord created Me." Then the small litany, and the exclamation of the Trisagion; and the Trisagion. Prokeimenon, Tone 4: "Proclaim the good tidings of the salvation of our God from day to day"; Verse: "Sing unto the Lord a new song." The Apostle to the Hebrews, pericope 306: "He that sanctifies and they who are sanctified."[^1466] Alleluia, Tone 7: "He shall come down like rain upon the fleece"; Verse: "His name shall be blessed unto ages."[^1467] Gospel of Luke, pericope 3: "Elizabeth conceived."[^1468] And the rest of the Divine Liturgy of Chrysostom. In place of "It is truly meet," we chant the heirmos: "Let no hand of the profane touch." Communion verse: "The Lord has chosen Zion, and has desired it for His habitation."[^1469]

*Decree of John the Faster:*[^1470]
We find in certain Typika that on this day of this precious feast there is sung: "Let my prayer be set forth." And this we do not know, in what manner it was determined. For some, out of arbitrary will and lack of instruction, have appended many things. But as for me, I judge that this ought not to be admitted at the complete Liturgy of Chrysostom, both at the Sixth Hour and when the Proskomide has already taken place. For it says: On whatever day the feast of the divine Annunciation occurs, the Liturgy of Chrysostom is celebrated, and at the refectory there is dispensation for fish, on whatever day it occurs. For this we received from the divine Fathers, to eat fish on the day of the divine Annunciation. But "Let my prayer be set forth" began to be sung in the Liturgy of the Presanctified, and at the Sixth Hour; for it is not fitting that any sign of mourning be sung on this day, for we honor it as the fountainhead of our salvation.

*If, by reason of great necessity, there is no Liturgy:*[^1471]
At "Lord, I have cried": Stichera of the Triodion, podoben, 3; and of the feast, 4; and of the Archangel, 3. Glory, both now: Of the feast. Entrance, Prokeimenon, and reading of the day; and of the feast, 2. Then the Prokeimenon, Apostle, and Gospel of the feast. And after the reading: "Vouchsafe, O Lord." At the Aposticha: Idiomelon of the day, twice; and the Martyr-hymn. Glory, both now: "Today is the joy." After "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart": Troparion of the Archangel; Glory, both now: Of the feast. Litany, and 3 great prostrations, and the dismissal. In the refectory, there is great consolation for the brethren: We eat fish, and drink wine, on whatever day it occurs, once during the day, except on Saturday and Sunday.
Compline we chant Small in the narthex, quickly, without prostrations and without canon. Only at "Glory to God in the highest," 3 prostrations; and after the Trisagia, 3 prostrations; and after "More honorable," 10 great prostrations with the prayer: "O Lord and Master"; and the other 12. And at the final Trisagion, 3 prostrations, and the dismissal.
At Matins toward the 26th day: We chant Alleluia, and the Triadica of the Tone.[^1472] But if it is a Saturday or a Sunday, we chant at "God is the Lord," the troparion of the Archangel, Tone 4: "Commanders of the heavenly hosts." After the first Kathisma: Sessional hymn of the Octoechos. After the second Kathisma and after the third: Sessional hymns of the Triodion. Canon of the feast of the Theotokos, with the heirmos on 6, Tone 4; and of the Archangel on 6, Tone 4. When the triode arrives, we chant the canon of the feast of the Theotokos and of the Archangel, with their heirmoi on 6; and the triode on 8. Katavasia: The heirmos of the Triodion. After Ode 3: Sessional hymn, Tone 4; Glory, both now: The same; and a reading. After Ode 6: Kontakion of the Archangel, Tone 2, podoben: "To thee, the Champion Leader": "Of the all-radiant and honorable and all-effecting [Trinity]." After Ode 9: Sessional hymn [exapostilarion], the Trinity Hymn of the Tone. At the Praises: Stichera of the Archangel on 4, Tone 4, podoben: "Thou hast given a sign"; Glory, both now: Of the feast, Tone 2: "Gabriel announces the good tidings." At the Aposticha of the Triodion: Idiomelon of the day, twice; and the Martyr-hymn. Glory, both now: Theotokion; and all the rest we chant with prostrations.
In the refectory: Dispensation for wine and oil.

*If the Annunciation occurs on the Third or Fourth Saturday of the Fasts:*[^1473]
On Friday evening we do not say the Kathisma. At "Lord, I have cried": Stichera on 10: Idiomelon in the Triodion of the day, twice; and of the feast, 8. Glory, both now: Of the feast; and the readings first of the day, and of the feast, 5; and "Let my prayer be set forth"; and the rest of the Presanctified. At the first hour of the night, we chant Great Compline according to custom. After the first Trisagion: Troparion of the feast; after the second: Kontakion of the feast. After "Glory to God in the highest": The departure, as indicated above on a fast day. At Matins, the entire service is of the feast; neither the four-ode canon nor anything else of Saturday is sung, but everything of the feast; we chant also the Great Doxology. The four-ode canon is sung on Thursday at Compline; likewise also at the Liturgy, everything is of the feast. Before the Liturgy, at the second hour of the day, we make the procession outside the monastery according to custom; and having returned, we chant the Liturgy. The Beatitudes from the canon of the feast, Odes 3 and 6.

*It is fitting to know: If the Annunciation occurs on the Third Sunday of the Fasts:*[^1474]
On Saturday at Small Vespers: At "Lord, I have cried," stichera of the Cross, 4; Glory, both now: Of the feast. At the Aposticha: Resurrection sticheron, 1; and of the feast, 3, idiomela: The Aposticha of Great Vespers with their refrains; Glory, both now: Of the feast. After the Trisagion: Resurrection troparion; Glory, both now: Of the feast. Litanies, and the dismissal.
At Great Vespers: "Blessed is the man," the entire Kathisma. At "Lord, I have cried": Resurrection stichera, 3; and of the Cross, podoben, 3; and of the feast, podoben, 4, on 10. Glory: Of the Cross, Tone 3: "O Christ our God"; Both now: Of the feast, Tone 6: "He was sent from heaven." Then the Entrance, and 5 readings. At the Litiya: Stichera of the feast, idiomela, 3, Tone 1; and of the Cross, 3, written at the Praises. Glory: Of the feast; Both now: Of the Cross. At the Aposticha: Resurrection stichera, alphabetically; Glory: Of the Cross; Both now: Of the feast. At the Blessing of the Loaves: Troparion of the feast, twice; and of the Cross, once; and a reading in the Apostolic Epistles, or of the feast.
At Matins: At "God is the Lord," the Resurrection troparion of the Tone, twice; Glory: Of the Cross; Both now: Of the feast. After the Kathismata: Resurrection sessional hymns, with their Theotokia; and a reading in the Explanatory Gospel. Polyeleos, and the sessional hymns of the feast, all once each; Glory, both now: Of the feast; and a reading of the feast. The Anabathmoi of the Tone; Prokeimenon of the feast; "Let every breath"; and the Gospel of the feast; "Having seen the Resurrection of Christ"; Psalm 50; sticheron of the feast. Canon: Resurrection on 4; and of the Cross on 4; and of the feast on 6. Katavasia of the feast: "I will open my mouth." After Ode 3: Kontakion of the Cross, and the Ikos. Then the sessional hymn of the Cross; Glory, both now: Of the feast; and a reading of the feast. After Ode 6: Kontakion of the feast, and the Ikos, and the Prologue. At Ode 9 we chant "More honorable"; Resurrection exapostilarion; Glory: Of the Cross; Both now: Of the feast. At the Praises: Resurrection stichera, 4; and of the feast, 3, Tone 1, podoben: "Joy of the heavenly ranks"; and idiomelon, Tone 2: "The mystery which was from eternity," with their refrains. Then the refrain: "Arise, O Lord my God"; and we chant the idiomelon sticheron of the day; Glory: The same; Both now: "Most blessed art thou." Great Doxology.
And the office of the veneration of the Cross takes place according to custom. And we chant the litanies, and the dismissal. Glory, both now: Gospel sticheron, and the catechesis of Theodore the Studite; and the First Hour in the narthex. At the First Hour: Resurrection troparion; Glory: Of the Cross; Both now: Theotokion of the Hours. After the "Our Father": Kontakion of the Cross, and the rest, and the complete dismissal.
At the second hour of the day, we go forth outside the monastery, as indicated above. And having returned, we chant the Hours, at which is said the Resurrection troparion, and of the feast, and of the Cross, alternating. Likewise also the kontakia. At the Liturgy: The Beatitudes of the Tone, on 4; of the feast, Ode 3, on 4; and of the Cross, Ode 6, on 4. After the Entrance: Resurrection troparion, and of the Cross, and of the feast. Glory: Kontakion of the Cross; Both now: Of the feast. In place of the Trisagion, we chant: "Before Thy Cross we bow down, O Master." Prokeimenon, Apostle, Alleluia, and Gospel, and Communion verse: First of the feast, then of the Cross. In place of "It is truly meet," we chant the heirmos: "Let no hand of the profane touch." The Liturgy of Basil the Great is celebrated; likewise also on all days of the Holy Fasts on which this feast occurs, the Liturgy of Basil the Great is celebrated without exception.[^1475]

*If the Annunciation occurs on Monday of the Second, Third, or Sixth Week of the Holy Fasts:*[^1476]
On Sunday at Small Vespers: Stichera of the feast, on 4; Glory, both now: Of the feast. At the Aposticha: Idiomelon of the day from the Triodion, twice; and the Martyr-hymn; Glory, both now: Of the feast. Troparion of the feast. Small Litany, and the dismissal.
At Great Vespers: After the customary Psalm, we chant: "Blessed is the man," the first antiphon. At "Lord, I have cried": Stichera on 10: Podoben of the Triodion, 3; and of the feast, 6. Glory, both now: "The Archangel Gabriel was sent." Entrance, Prokeimenon of the day; and 3 readings of the feast; and then the litany: "Let us all say"; then: "Vouchsafe, O Lord"; and "Let us complete our evening prayer."
At the Litiya: Stichera of the feast; Glory, both now: Of the feast. At the Aposticha: Stichera of the feast with the refrains of the feast; Glory, both now: Of the feast. At the Blessing of the Loaves: Troparion of the feast, three times; and a reading of the feast. At Matins, we chant the service of the feast, as prescribed above on a fast day in order.

*And if the Annunciation occurs on Cross-Veneration Wednesday:*[^1477]
The stichera, the Doxastica, and the canon of the Cross are left aside, and are sung on Monday or on Friday of that same week. Here, however, we chant the entire service of the Annunciation with the Wednesday triode, as indicated on the first day in order. And at Matins at the First Hour, the veneration of the Cross takes place according to the rite.

*And if the Annunciation occurs on the Fourth or Fifth Sunday of the Fasts:*[^1478]
On Saturday at Small Vespers: Stichera of the feast, on 4; Glory, both now: Of the feast. At the Aposticha: Resurrection sticheron, 1; and of the feast, the Aposticha of Great Vespers, with their refrains; Glory, both now: Of the feast. Troparion of the feast. Little Litany; and the Dismissal. At Great Vespers: **"Blessed is the man..."**, the entire kathisma. At "Lord, I have cried...", Resurrection stichera, 3; and Anatolian, 1; and of the feast, 6; Glory, both now, in Tone 6: **"He was sent from heaven..."** Entrance; Prokeimenon of the day; and 5 readings of the feast. At the Litiya, stichera of the feast; Glory, in Tone 8; Both now, in Tone 2. At the Aposticha, Resurrection stichera; Glory, both now: Of the feast. At the blessing of the loaves, troparion of the feast, thrice; and a reading from the apostolic epistles, or of the feast.

At Matins, at "God is the Lord...", Resurrection troparion, twice; Glory, both now: Of the feast. After the kathismata, Resurrection sessional hymns, with their Theotokia; and a reading from the Commentary Gospel. Then the Polyeleos, and the sessional hymns of the feast, all once; and a reading of the feast. The Graduals of the Tone; Prokeimenon of the feast; "Let every breath..."; and the Gospel of the feast; "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ..."; Psalm 50; Sticheron of the feast.

Resurrection canon with its Heirmos, on 4; and of the Triodion, on 4; and of the feast, on 6. Katavasia: The Heirmos of the feast. After the 3rd Ode, sessional hymn of the feast, and a reading of the feast. After the 6th Ode, we chant the Kontakion of the feast and the Ikos; and we read the Prologue. At the 9th Ode, we chant "More honorable..."; Resurrection Exapostilarion, and of the feast. At the Praises, stichera on 8: Resurrection, 4; and of the feast, 4, with their refrains; and with "Glory...", we chant the refrain: "Arise, O Lord my God..."; and we chant the idiomelon sticheron of the day; Glory, again the same; Both now: "Most blessed art thou..."; the Great Doxology. After the Trisagion, Resurrection troparion; the litanies; and the Dismissal. Then, Glory, both now: Gospel sticheron. And holy oil from the lamp of the Most Holy Theotokos is given to the brethren, while we sing the idiomelon sticheron of the feast. Procession into the narthex, and the First Hour. At the First Hour, Resurrection troparion; Glory: Of the feast; Both now: Theotokion of the Hours. After the Trisagion, Kontakion of the feast; and the rest; the complete Dismissal.

And at the second hour of the day, we make a procession outside the monastery, as indicated in order. And having returned, we chant the Divine Liturgy of St. Basil the Great. The Beatitudes of the Tone, on 6; and of the feast, Ode 3, on 4. After the Entrance, troparia: Resurrectional, and of the feast; Glory, both now: Kontakion of the feast; Prokeimenon, Epistle, Alleluia, Gospel, and Communion Verse: first of the Sunday, then of the feast.

*And if the Annunciation of the Most Holy Theotokos occurs on Wednesday of the Fifth Week of the Fasts:*[^1479]
We chant the service of the Forefeast of the Annunciation: The stichera and the canon on Monday in order; while that of the saint from the Menaion we chant at Compline; because the Great Canon is transferred from Thursday to Tuesday of that same week. And we chant the Great Canon with the Tuesday triode, on account of the feast of the Most Holy Theotokos; because on Wednesday, which is the feast itself, the kathismata are not recited, and prostrations do not take place; and we chant the Apodosis of the feast on Thursday; therefore, on Wednesday evening, the stichera are chanted with prostrations, and the Great Canon is not sung on Thursday, for it was sung beforehand on Tuesday.

On Wednesday of the Fifth Week of the Fasts, we chant the entire service of the feast in the evening and in the morning with the Triodion according to the Typikon, as indicated previously for a fasting day. And the Apodosis of the Annunciation we chant on Thursday at Matins with the apostolic triode, as shown under Monday of the Fourth and Fifth Weeks of the Fast, for the Apodosis of the Feast of the Annunciation.

*And if the Annunciation of the Most Holy Theotokos occurs on Thursday of the Fifth Week of the Fasts, when the Great Canon is sung:*[^1480]
The Great Canon of lord Andrew is transferred on account of the feast, and we sing it on Tuesday of that same week with the Tuesday triode; while the apostolic triode we chant with the feast of the Annunciation; and afterwards, the Katavasia of the Triodion.

*And if the Annunciation of the Most Holy Theotokos occurs on Friday of that same week:*[^1481]
We chant the Forefeast of the Annunciation, the stichera and the canon beforehand on Wednesday in order, on account of the Great Canon; and the service of the saint in the Menaion we sing at Compline.

*And if the Annunciation of the Most Holy Theotokos occurs on the Saturday of the Akathist:*[^1482]
On Friday evening, at "Lord, I have cried...", stichera on 10: In the Triodion, the idiomelon of the day, twice; and of the feast, on 8; Glory, both now: Of the feast: **"He was sent..."** Entrance; and the readings of the day; and 5 of the feast. After "Let my prayer be set forth...", 3 prostrations; and the rest of the Presanctified Gifts. And at "Blessed be the name of the Lord...", 3 prostrations; and at the Dismissal, prostrations.

And at the fourth hour of the night, the klepalo is sounded for the great bell, and afterwards for all the bells. And having gathered in the temple, when the priest has given the blessing, we chant Great Compline. And the priest censes according to custom, and after "Glory to God in the highest...", we go forth into the narthex and make the customary litiya, and we chant 3 idiomelon stichera of the feast, in Tone 1; Glory, both now: **"Gabriel announces the good tidings..."** And the customary prayers are recited by the priest. And upon the conclusion, we enter again into the temple; and we chant at the Aposticha the idiomelon stichera with their refrains; Glory, both now: **"Today is joy..."** At the blessing of the loaves, troparion of the feast, thrice; and a reading of the feast.

At Matins, at "God is the Lord...", troparion of the feast, thrice. After the 1st kathisma, the Kontakion: **"To thee, the Champion Leader..."**, and the other 3; and 3 ikoi; and again the 1st kontakion; and the reading of the Akathist. After the 2nd kathisma, 3 kontakia and 3 ikoi; and again the 1st kontakion: **"To thee, the Champion Leader..."**, as shown previously. And the reading of the Akathist; and the Polyeleos; and all the sessional hymns of the feast; and a reading of the feast. The Graduals, the 1st Antiphon of Tone 4; Prokeimenon of the feast; "Let every breath..."; Gospel of the feast;

Psalm 50; Sticheron of the feast. Canon of the feast, with the Heirmos, on 8; and of the Akathist, on 6; Katavasia of the feast, both choirs together.

The four-ode canon[^1483] we do not chant here, but we sing it beforehand on Thursday at Compline. After the 3rd Ode, 3 kontakia and 3 ikoi; and again the 1st kontakion. Then the sessional hymn, and a reading of the feast. After the 6th Ode, 3 kontakia and 3 ikoi. Then the kontakion: **"O all-hymned Mother..."**, thrice, and the 1st ikos; and the kontakion: **"To thee, the Champion Leader..."** And we read the Prologue and the Synaxarion. At the 9th Ode, we do not chant "More honorable...", but we sing the refrains of the feast, as indicated on the feast itself; and for the canon of the Akathist, the refrain to the troparia is: "Most Holy Theotokos, save us." Then at the descent[^1484] we chant the refrain and the Heirmos: **"As the living ark of God..."**; and a bow. Exapostilarion of the feast.

At the Praises, stichera of the feast, on 4: *Tone 1, Podoben: "Joy of the heavenly ranks" (Небе́сныхъ чино́въ):* Glory, both now: **"Let the heavens rejoice..."** Great Doxology. Troparion of the feast; litanies; and the Dismissal. And holy oil is given to the brethren according to custom; and the Catechesis of Theodore the Studite; and the First Hour in the narthex. At the First Hour, troparion of the feast. After the Trisagion, kontakion of the feast, and the rest; and the Dismissal. And a procession outside the monastery. At the Divine Liturgy, the Beatitudes of the feast, Odes 3 and 6, on 8; Prokeimenon, Epistle, Alleluia, Gospel, and Communion Verse of the feast.

[Decorative woodcut tailpiece]

**The End, and to God be the Glory.**[^1485]

[Seal: Lviv Theological Library]

[^1]: Printed in Cyrillic numerals: *҂ац҃ѕ* (1000 + 900 + 6 = 1906). The typography of the Stauropegion Institute in Lviv (attached to the historical Dormition Church and Brotherhood founded in the 16th century) published standard liturgical books for the Greek Catholic Church in Galicia. Physical Leaf p1 = Unnumbered Title Page.

[^2]: Inscription dedicates this exemplar to Bishop Ivan Prasko (1914–2001), Greek Catholic Bishop for Ukrainian Catholics in Australia, New Zealand, and Oceania (consecrated 1958, Eparch of SS. Peter and Paul of Melbourne from 1982), from Fr. Ihor Shpytkovsky, dated in Melbourne, July 29, 1968. Physical Leaf p1 = Unnumbered Title Page.

[^3]: Engraving of the architectural ensemble of the Lviv Stauropegion Dormition Church (Успенська церква) on Ruska Street in Lviv, featuring the Korniakt Tower (66 meters, built 1572–1578 by architect Peter Barbon), the Chapel of the Three Hierarchs (built 1578–1591 by Peter Krasowski), and the main church (built 1591–1629 by Paulo Romano). The bottom calligraphic vyaz inscription reads: *ТВОРЕНІЕ ЦАРЕВО И СЫНА ЕГО* ("The Work of the King and His Son"), evoking both the celestial King and His Son and the royal patrons who endowed the brotherhood. Physical Leaf p2 = Full-page frontispiece plate.

[^4]: The official hierarchy dedicatory leaf dated June 26, 1906 (Decree No. 1946), during the pontificate of Pope St. Pius X (reigned 1903–1914) and the reign of Austro-Hungarian Emperor Franz Joseph I (reigned 1848–1916). Servant of God Andrey Sheptytsky served as Metropolitan of Halych and Archbishop of Lviv from 1900 to 1944. Physical Leaf p3 = Dedicatory leaf.

[^5]: Mykola Herasymovych and Roman Ilnytsky served as Senior Wardens (*старѣйшины*) of the Stauropegion Institute. Fr. Volodymyr Hurhula (1866–1938) was a prominent Greek Catholic priest, liturgist, and editor of liturgical books at the Stauropegion typography. Physical Leaf p3 = Dedicatory leaf.

[^6]: An opening prayer to Our Lord Jesus Christ traditionally printed before the liturgical corpus in Ruthenian and Slavic Triodia, beseeching divine grace, compunction, and perseverance through the upcoming holy fast. Physical Leaf p4 = Unnumbered front matter prayer leaf.

[^7]: Physical Leaf p5 = Printed Page 1. Here begins the liturgical corpus of the Lenten Triodion (*Triodion Postnaja*). In this edition, physical leaf coordinates relate to printed book pagination by the formula: Physical Leaf = Printed Page + 4.

[^8]: Psalm 140 (LXX; MT Psalm 141).

[^9]: The Anatolian stichera (*Анатолієвы*) are attributed to Anatolius, Patriarch of Constantinople (449–458) or to an 8th/9th-century hymnographer of the same name.

[^10]: The three solemn penitential troparia (*Покаянія отверзи ми двери, Жизнодавче*, *На спасения стези настави мя, Богородице*, *Множества содѣланныхъ мною лютыхъ*) are chanted at Sunday Matins after Psalm 50 beginning on the Sunday of the Publican and the Pharisee and continuing through the Fifth Sunday of Great Lent.

[^11]: St. George of Nicomedia (9th century), chartophylax of the Great Church and metropolitan of Nicomedia, prominent Byzantine hymnographer. The Greek acrostic ΓΕΩΡΓΙΟΥ ("Of George") is formed by the initial letters of the Theotokia across the nine odes of the canon and is preserved in Church Slavonic transcription in the printed margins (*Г-Є-Ѡ-Р-Г-І-Ѡ-У*). Physical Leaf p6 = Printed Page 2.

[^12]: Nikephoros Kallistos Xanthopoulos (c. 1256–c. 1335), Byzantine ecclesiastical historian, poet, and monk of Hagia Sophia in Constantinople, author of the verse synaxaria and historical introductions for the movable festal cycle of the Triodion and Pentecostarion. Physical Leaf p8 = Printed Page 4.

[^13]: St. Cosmas the Melodist (Bishop of Maiuma, c. 675–752), foster-brother of St. John of Damascus, who first instituted canons consisting of three odes (*triodia*) for the days of Great and Holy Passion Week. The corpus was subsequently expanded by St. Theodore the Studite (759–826) and his brother St. Joseph the Studite (d. 830) to encompass the entire pre-Lenten and Lenten cycle. Physical Leaf p8 = Printed Page 4.

[^14]: The Resurrectional Exapostilarion (or Hymn of Light, *Свѣтиленъ*) of the Octoechos is chanted according to the weekly eothinon (Gospel reading) cycle, followed by the special proper Exapostilarion of the Triodion for the Publican and the Pharisee (*Высокорѣчія убѣжимъ фарисеева злѣйшаго*). Physical Leaf p10 = Printed Page 6.

[^15]: Physical Leaf p11 = Printed Page 7. The 11 Matins Gospel stichera (*Евангельскіѧ стихи̑ры* or *Eothina*) are attributed to Emperor Leo VI the Wise (886–912) and correspond to the 11 resurrectional Gospel pericopes of the Sunday Matins cycle. In monastic and cathedral Typika, from the Sunday of the Publican and the Pharisee through All Saints Sunday, the designated eothinon sticheron is chanted at the Litiya in the narthex.

[^16]: The Catechetical Homilies (*Ѡ҆глаше́ніѧ*) of St. Theodore the Studite (759–826), Abbot of the Monastery of Studios in Constantinople, provide spiritual instruction on monastic vigilance, ascetic struggle, and compunction. They are appointed to be read to the brethren in the narthex following the Litiya dismissal or at the First Hour throughout the pre-Lenten and Lenten cycle. Physical Leaf p11 = Printed Page 7.

[^17]: 2 Timothy 3:10–15 (Pericope 296). Physical Leaf p11 = Printed Page 7.

[^18]: Luke 18:10–14 (Pericope 84), the Parable of the Publican and the Pharisee. Physical Leaf p11 = Printed Page 7.

[^19]: The "Fast of Artzivurion" (*арцивꙋ́ріевъ по́стъ*, Armenian *Arachavorats*) was a traditional pre-Lenten fast of the Armenian Apostolic Church held ten weeks before Easter (the week following the Sunday of the Publican and the Pharisee). In Byzantine and Ruthenian polemical rubrics, it was condemned as a Monophysite fast, in response to which the Byzantine Typikon institutes a fast-free week (*сплошная седмица*) permitting cheese, eggs, and dairy for monastics and meat for laity on Wednesday and Friday. Physical Leaf p11 = Printed Page 7.

[^20]: The Resurrectional Theotokion of the Octoechos (Tone 6, by St. John of Damascus): "My Maker and Redeemer, Christ the Lord, having come forth from thy womb, O all-pure one, and having clothed Himself in me, has delivered Adam from the primal curse." Physical Leaf p12 = Printed Page 8.

[^21]: Psalm 136 (LXX; MT Psalm 137). In Ruthenian and Slavic practice, this psalm is solemnly chanted at Sunday Matins after the Polyeleos Psalms (134 and 135) with ornate or festive Alleluia (*со аллилуіею красною*) on three Sundays only: the Sunday of the Prodigal Son, Meatfare Sunday, and Cheesefare Sunday. Physical Leaf p12 = Printed Page 8.

[^22]: Cross-reference to printed folio 2 of the Triodion (Physical Leaf p6), where the penitential post-Gospel troparia (*Покаянія отверзи ми двери, Жизнодавче*, *На спасения стези*, *Множества содѣланныхъ мною лютыхъ*) are printed in full. Physical Leaf p12 = Printed Page 8.

[^23]: St. Joseph the Hymnographer (c. 816–886), monk of Constantinople and one of the preeminent liturgical poets of the Byzantine Church, composer of canons in the Parakletike, Menaia, and Triodion. Physical Leaf p12 = Printed Page 8.

[^24]: Luke 15:18, 21. Physical Leaf p13 = Printed Page 9.

[^25]: Habakkuk 3:3 (LXX). Physical Leaf p13 = Printed Page 9.

[^26]: Model troparion (*podoben*) "Today the Virgin" (*Дѣва днесь*) composed by St. Romanos the Melodist for the Nativity of Christ. Physical Leaf p14 = Printed Page 10.

[^27]: Synaxarion for the Sunday of the Prodigal Son, authored by Nikephoros Kallistos Xanthopoulos (c. 1256–c. 1335), monk and ecclesiastical historian of Constantinople. Physical Leaf p14 = Printed Page 10.

[^28]: In the Sunday Praises (*Хвалитехъ*), when 8 stichera are appointed, the Byzantine and Ruthenian order combines 4 Resurrectional stichera of the Octoechos, 1 Anatolian (Eastern) sticheron, and 3 idiomelon stichera of the Triodion. Physical Leaf p16 = Printed Page 12.

[^29]: 1 Corinthians 6:12–20 (Pericope 135). Physical Leaf p16 = Printed Page 12.

[^30]: Luke 15:11–32 (Pericope 79), the Parable of the Prodigal Son. Physical Leaf p16 = Printed Page 12.

[^31]: St. Macarius the Great (c. 300–391), Egyptian desert father. His ascetic homilies were appointed for spiritual reading during pre-Lenten and Lenten Matins. Physical Leaf p16 = Printed Page 12.

[^32]: Physical Leaf p17 = Printed Page 13. Meatfare Saturday is the first Universal Ancestral Saturday of the Dead (*Вселенская родительская суббота*) in the liturgical year, dedicated to the general commemoration of all departed Orthodox Christians from Adam to the present day, celebrated on the eve of the Sunday of the Last Judgment.

[^33]: One of the classic funeral idiomela (*самогласны*) composed by St. John of Damascus (c. 676–749), which also forms an integral part of the Byzantine burial office (*Otpevanie*). Physical Leaf p17 = Printed Page 13.

[^34]: Psalm 64:5 (LXX; MT Psalm 65:4) and Psalm 101:13 (LXX; MT Psalm 102:12). Physical Leaf p17 = Printed Page 13.

[^35]: Psalm 24:13 (LXX; MT Psalm 25:13). Physical Leaf p17 = Printed Page 13.

[^36]: St. John of Damascus (c. 676–749), Doctor of the Church and monk of the Laura of St. Sabbas the Sanctified, author of the Funeral Stichera of the Octoechos. Physical Leaf p17 = Printed Page 13.

[^37]: The Panikhida (*Паннихида*, from Greek παννυχίς, "all-night service") is the Byzantine memorial office for the departed, served in the narthex following Vespers on memorial days. Physical Leaf p18 = Printed Page 14.

[^38]: 1 Corinthians 15:12–58, St. Paul's exposition of the resurrection of the dead. Physical Leaf p18 = Printed Page 14.

[^39]: Psalm 118 (LXX; MT Psalm 119), known as the *Amomos* (from Greek Ἄμωμοι, "Blameless"), is divided into two sections (*staseis*) at funeral Matins, with distinct refrains. Physical Leaf p18 = Printed Page 14.

[^40]: Psalm 118:12 (LXX; MT Psalm 119:12), the refrain to the Funeral Evlogitaria (*Непорочны*), Tone 5. Physical Leaf p18 = Printed Page 14.

[^41]: The solemn priestly prayer for the deceased: "O God of spirits and of all flesh, Who hast trampled down death and overthrown the Devil..." from the Byzantine Euchologion (*Sluzhebnik* / *Trebnik*). Physical Leaf p18 = Printed Page 14.

[^42]: St. Theodore the Studite (759–826). His Canon for Meatfare Saturday systematically catalogues all conceivable manners of human demise (drowning, war, earthquakes, wild beasts, pestilence, fire, cold) so that no departed Christian remains unremembered by the church. Physical Leaf p19 = Printed Page 15.

[^43]: The Slavonic rubric translates the acrostic as "Недосто́йнагѡ Ѳео́дѡра" ("Of unworthy Theodore"), but the printed marginal letters transliterate the original Byzantine Greek acrostic composed by St. Theodore the Studite: ΤΟΥ ΤΑΠΕΙΝΟΥ ΘΕΟΔΩΡΟΥ ("Of the humble Theodore"). The letters printed in the margins across Odes 1–4 are: Ode 1: Т, О; Ode 2: Y, Т; Ode 3: А, П; Ode 4: Е, І, spelling ΤΟΥ ΤΑΠΕΙ... Physical Leaf p19 = Printed Page 15.

[^44]: Church Slavonic: *плинда*, a loanword from Byzantine Greek πλίνθος ("brick", "masonry tile"). Physical Leaf p20 = Printed Page 16.

[^45]: Typographical error in the 1906 Stauropegion edition, which prints *Г҃дороди́тельнице* instead of *Бг҃ороди́тельнице*. Physical Leaf p20 = Printed Page 16.

[^46]: Physical Leaf p21 = Printed Page 17. The Greek acrostic in the margins: Ode 5 has Ѳ (Theta) at Glory and V (Upsilon) at Now and ever; Ode 6 has О (Omicron) at Glory and Д (Delta) at Now and ever, continuing the Greek acrostic ΤΟΥ ТАПЕΙΝΟΥ ΘΕΟΔΩΡΟΥ ("Of the humble Theodore") composed by St. Theodore the Studite (759–826).

[^47]: Synaxarion for Meatfare Saturday, authored by Nikephoros Kallistos Xanthopoulos (c. 1256–c. 1335), monk and ecclesiastical historian of Constantinople. It expounds the theological rationale for commemorating all departed Orthodox Christians on the eve of the Sunday of the Dread Judgment. Physical Leaf p21 = Printed Page 17.

[^48]: Genesis 3:19, quoted in the Ikos: "For dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return." Physical Leaf p21 = Printed Page 17.

[^154]: The universal liturgical commemoration of All Holy Monastics and Ascetic Fathers and Mothers (*Па́мѧть всѣ́хъ преподо́бныхъ и҆ бг҃оно́сныхъ Ѻ҆тє́цъ, въ по́двиѕѣ просїѧ́вшихъ*), instituted on the Saturday of Cheesefare Week as a spiritual fortification and pattern of ascetic virtue immediately prior to entering Clean Week and the Great Fast. The troparion invokes the three foundational regions of early desert monasticism: Lower Egypt (Nitria and Kellia), Upper Egypt (the Thebaid, founded by St. Pachomius), and Libya/Pentapolis. Physical Leaf p61 = Printed Page 57.

[^155]: The primary pioneers of Christian monasticism: St. Anthony the Great (c. 251–356), the father of eremitic desert monasticism; St. Ammon of Nitria (c. 294–357), founder of the Nitrian monastic settlements; St. Arsenius the Great (c. 350–445), imperial tutor turned solitary hesychast (*держа́во безмо́лвїѧ*); and St. Pachomius the Great (c. 292–348), founder of Christian coenobitic (communal) monasticism in Tabennisi. Physical Leaf p61 = Printed Page 57.

[^156]: Celebrated Desert Fathers commemorated in the *Apophthegmata Patrum* (*Sayings of the Desert Fathers*): Abba Agathon, Abba Achillas, Abba Ammon, Abba Poemen the Shepherd (c. 340–450), Abba Paësius (brother of Poemen), Abba Pambo of Nitria (d. c. 375), and Abba Isaiah of Scetis (d. 491). Physical Leaf p61 = Printed Page 57.

[^157]: St. Athanasius of Mount Athos (c. 920–1004), founder of the Great Lavra and organized monastic life on the Holy Mountain of Athos, or St. Athanasius the Great (c. 296–373) who found refuge among the desert fathers of Egypt; here associated with ascetic fasting on Mount Idion. Physical Leaf p61 = Printed Page 57.

[^158]: St. Hilarion the Great (291–371), disciple of Anthony who established monasticism in Palestine and Gaza, living a detached, "bird-like" heavenly life (*пти́чее житїѐ*); St. Benjamin of Nitria; St. Helladius; St. Eulogius the Presbyter; and St. Bacchyllus. Physical Leaf p62 = Printed Page 58.

[^159]: Western and Eastern ascetic founders: St. Benedict of Nursia (c. 480–548), the father of Western coenobitic monasticism and author of the Holy Rule; St. John Cassian (c. 360–435), abbot of Saint-Victor in Marseilles and bridge between Egyptian desert wisdom and the West through his *Institutes* and *Conferences*; and St. Bassian the Recluse, who enclosed himself alive in a tomb-like cell (*во гро́бѣ бо живы́й всели́всѧ*) as an emblem of perfect ascetic obedience. Physical Leaf p62 = Printed Page 58.

[^160]: St. Gelasius of Palestine (5th c.), abbot of Nicopolis; St. Gerasimus of the Jordan (d. 475), founder of the famous Judean lavra near Jericho, renowned in hagio-liturgical tradition for his friendship with a wild lion that served him obediently in virtue (*є҆мꙋ́же порабо́та ѕвѣ́рь*); and Father Germanus and Gaius, ascetics of the Egyptian desert. Physical Leaf p62 = Printed Page 58.

[^161]: St. David of Thessalonica (c. 450–535), who spent three years living in an almond tree outside the city walls as a dendrite before dwelling in a small hut; St. Daniel of Scetis (6th c.), archimandrite of the Skete; St. Dius the Wonderworker (d. c. 430), founder of a major monastery in Constantinople; and St. Dalmatus (d. 440), former soldier who became archimandrite of the Dalmation monastery and a valiant defender of Orthodoxy at the Council of Ephesus (431). Physical Leaf p62 = Printed Page 58.

[^162]: St. Euthymius the Great (377–473), founding archimandrite of Judean lavra monasticism; St. Thalassius of Libya (7th c.), hesychast and author on ascetic virtues; St. Ephrem the Syrian (c. 306–373), the "Harp of the Spirit" (*бг҃одх҃нове́нный*); and St. Eulogius the Presbyter of Alexandria. Physical Leaf p62 = Printed Page 58.

[^163]: St. Theodore of Therme; St. Ennathas; St. Theodulus; St. Theonas; and St. Theodosius the Cenobiarch (c. 423–529), founder of organized communal monasticism in the Judean wilderness. Physical Leaf p62 = Printed Page 58.

[^164]: St. Theoctistus of Palestine (d. 467), co-laborer with St. Euthymius in the Judean desert; and St. Theodore the Sykeote (d. 613), Bishop of Anastasiopolis in Galatia, famed for his austere fasting from childhood and miraculous healings. Physical Leaf p62 = Printed Page 58.

[^165]: St. John Climacus (c. 579–649), Abbot of Saint Catherine's Monastery on Mount Sinai and author of *The Ladder of Divine Ascent* (*Лѣ́ствица / Κλῖмаξ*); and St. Chariton the Confessor (d. c. 350), founder of the Judean lavras of Pharan, Douka, and Souka (the Old Lavra). Physical Leaf p62 = Printed Page 58.

[^166]: St. Euphrasia the Virgin (c. 380–410), daughter of a senator of Constantinople who gave away her immense wealth and embraced strict asceticism in a convent in the Egyptian Thebaid, commemorated alongside the greatest male monastic founders. Physical Leaf p63 = Printed Page 59.

[^167]: An alphabetical acrostic hymnography honoring venerable fathers: St. Hesychius of Jerusalem, Hierax, and Joseph; Callistus, Laurence, and Longinus; St. Leucius the Confessor, St. Maximus the Confessor (c. 580–662), Marcian, and St. Mark the Ascetic (5th c.). Physical Leaf p63 = Printed Page 59.

[^168]: St. Macarius the Great (c. 300–391) and St. Macarius of Alexandria (d. c. 395); Jovian; Mark; and St. Moses the Ethiopian (c. 330–405), former brigand turned desert father and martyr at Scetis. Physical Leaf p64 = Printed Page 60.

[^169]: St. Martinian of Caesarea (4th c.), hermit who endured severe temptations to preserve chastity; St. Marcellus, Abbot of the Monastery of the "Unsleeping Ones" (Akoimetoi) in Constantinople; and St. Miles (Milas), Persian bishop and wonderworker who raised the dead. Physical Leaf p64 = Printed Page 60.

[^170]: St. Nilus of Ancyra (Nilus of Sinai, d. c. 430), disciple of St. John Chrysostom and prolific ascetic epistolographer whose verbal streams water the rational soul; St. Naucratis, brother of St. Basil the Great; St. Nicon; St. Nathanael; and St. Nistheron of Nitria. Physical Leaf p64 = Printed Page 60.

[^171]: St. Xenophon of Constantinople (5th c.), who with his wife Maria and sons Arcadius and John embraced monasticism; St. Porphyrius, Bishop of Gaza (c. 347–420); and St. Onuphrius the Great (4th c.), who lived in complete solitude in the inner Egyptian desert for sixty years. Physical Leaf p64 = Printed Page 60.

[^172]: St. Pambo of Nitria (d. c. 375); St. Paphnutius the Ascetic; Abba Pior; Abba Patermuthius; St. Paul the Simple (4th c.), disciple of St. Anthony famed for absolute obedience and casting out powerful demons; and St. Pitirion, disciple of Anthony on the Mountain of Pispir. Physical Leaf p64 = Printed Page 60.

[^173]: St. Pachomius the Great and his spiritual father Abba Palamon the Hermit; St. Petronius (Petronios), successor of Pachomius; and St. Patapius of Thebes (4th c.), desert hermit who later worked miracles in Constantinople. Physical Leaf p64 = Printed Page 60.

Physical Leaf p65 = Printed Page 61.

Physical Leaf p66 = Printed Page 62.

[^180]: St. Mary of Egypt (c. 344–421), supreme archetype of Lenten repentance who lived 47 years beyond the Jordan; St. Marina, who was brought up in a monastery disguised as a monk under the name Marinus; and St. Euphrosyne of Alexandria (5th c.), who lived in a men's monastery as the monk Smaragdus. Physical Leaf p66 = Printed Page 62.

[^181]: St. Theodula of Anazarbus (martyred under Diocletian); St. Theodote; St. Isaura; and St. Isidora the Fool-for-Christ of Tabennisi (4th c.), who wore a dishcloth on her head and endured contempt in silence until discovered by St. Pitirion. Physical Leaf p66 = Printed Page 62.

[^182]: St. Marina of Antioch; St. Matrona of Perge (5th c.), who founded a convent in Constantinople after living disguised in a men's monastery; St. Syncletica of Alexandria (c. 270–350), desert amma whose teachings are preserved in the *Apophthegmata*; Amma Sarah of Scetis; and St. Justina the Virgin Martyr (d. 304). Physical Leaf p66 = Printed Page 62.

[^183]: St. Pelagia of Antioch (d. c. 457), former actress and courtesan who repented at the preaching of Bishop Nonnus and lived as a recluse on the Mount of Olives; and St. Thaïs of Egypt (4th c.), converted by St. Paphnutius and confined to a cell of penance. Physical Leaf p66 = Printed Page 62.

[^184]: The three supreme Cappadocian and Alexandrian doctors of the Church: St. Basil the Great (c. 330–379), Archbishop of Caesarea; St. Athanasius the Great (c. 296–373), Patriarch of Alexandria and pillar of Nicaea; and St. Gregory the Theologian (Nazianzen, c. 329–390), Archbishop of Constantinople. Physical Leaf p66 = Printed Page 62.

[^185]: St. John Chrysostom (c. 349–407), Archbishop of Constantinople; St. Cyril of Alexandria (d. 444) and St. Cyril of Jerusalem (c. 313–386); St. Hesychius of Jerusalem (5th c.); and St. Meletius, Patriarch of Antioch (d. 381), who presided over the Second Ecumenical Council. Physical Leaf p66 = Printed Page 62.

[^186]: St. Gregory of Nyssa (c. 335–c. 395), mystical theologian and brother of St. Basil; the two wonderworking fathers (St. Gregory the Wonderworker of Neocaesarea and St. Nicholas of Myra); St. Epiphanius of Salamis (c. 315–403), Bishop of Cyprus; and St. Amphilochius, Bishop of Iconium (d. c. 394).
